47// Mirrors Perl `Package.pm` (`split(/\s*,\s*/, $options)`) — strips
48// whitespace on BOTH sides of each comma so option names are normalized
49// when LaTeX line-wraps the option list (e.g. `[twocolumn,amsmath\n
50// ,amssymb]`). Without leading `\s*` we'd get `"amsmath\n"` and the
51// declared option callback wouldn't fire — silently turning the option
52// into an unused-global.
53static OPTS_REGEX: Lazy<Regex> = Lazy::new(|| Regex::new(r"\s*,\s*").unwrap());
54
55// Perl `\ensuremathfollows` already-math test (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml
56// L2083/L2098): `$MATHENVS = 'displaymath|equation*?|eqnarray*?'` and the guard
57// `$csname !~ /^Math|\(|\[|(?:$MATHENVS)/o`. Kept verbatim (not hand-expanded)
58// so the automath wrapper matches Perl exactly.
59static AUTOMATH_ALREADY_MATH: Lazy<Regex> =
60  Lazy::new(|| Regex::new(r"^Math|\\\(|\\\[|(?:displaymath|equation*?|eqnarray*?)").unwrap());
61
62// Perl `\documentclass` (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml L78) wraps the
63// raw option string in `TrimmedCommaList(...)` — i.e. comma-split AND
64// strip whitespace from EACH element including the first/last.
65// OPTS_REGEX only strips whitespace around the comma delimiters, so a
66// leading-space bracket `[ amsmath, amssymb]` produces a first
67// element ` amsmath` (still has leading space) which fails to match
68// any DeclareOption. Wrap every OPTS_REGEX.split site with this
69// helper to mirror TrimmedCommaList exactly.
70// Witness: 2210.07776 (`\documentclass[ amsmath,amssymb,...]
71// {revtex4-1}` — leading space prevented amsmath option from firing,
72// so amsmath/amsbsy never loaded, so `\boldsymbol` was undefined).
73// Only brace-depth-0 commas split, as LaTeX's own `\@for` walk of
74// `\@classoptionslist` (latex.ltx `\@process@ptions`) and l3keys' clist
75// parsing do: `thesis={type=dr,dr=rernat}` is ONE option (DEMO-TUDaPhD;
76// Perl's `split(/\s*,\s*/)` cuts it in two — a Perl-only defect).
77fn split_trim_options(s: &str) -> Vec<String> {
78  let mut out = Vec::new();
79  let mut depth = 0usize;
80  let mut start = 0;
81  for (i, c) in s.char_indices() {
82    match c {
83      '{' => depth += 1,
84      '}' => depth = depth.saturating_sub(1),
85      ',' if depth == 0 => {
86        out.push(s[start..i].trim().to_string());
87        start = i + 1;
88      },
89      _ => {},
90    }
91  }
92  out.push(s[start..].trim().to_string());
93  out.retain(|o| !o.is_empty());
94  out
95}
96static SEMIVERBATIM_CHARS: [char; 4] = ['%', '\\', '{', '}'];
97static NOTE_TEXT_END: Lazy<Regex> = Lazy::new(|| Regex::new("^(\\w+?)text$").unwrap());
98static NOTE_MARK_END: Lazy<Regex> = Lazy::new(|| Regex::new("^(\\w+?)mark$").unwrap());

100/// Defensive sanitizer for section-type identifiers (the `{section}` arg of
101/// `\@@numbered@section` etc.). Some upstream paths — notably figure-block +
102/// section sequencing in BoxedEPS-loading papers (Cluster A / math0010095) —
103/// allow a trailing `\par` (or other CS) token to pollute the section type
104/// string. The type identifier should always be a bare letter sequence
105/// (`section`, `subsection`, `appendix` …); strip a single trailing CS if
106/// present so downstream `\csname @<type>...@ID\endcsname`-style construction
107/// stays well-formed.
108/// The NAME of a digested `{}` identifier argument — a section type, a note type (`\lx@note{footnote}`): its
109/// reverted tokens, not its typeset string. Digestion decodes letters through the current font encoding, so under
110/// LGR (babel greek, textalpha) the digested `section` read back as `σεςτιον` and `\csname the…\endcsname` built
111/// `\theσεςτιον` (greek-fontenc manuals, teubner, toptesi-it: 56 nested-section errors per doc); a note's type is
112/// digested after `neutralize_font`, in the document's encoding (`footnote` → `φοοτνοτε`, an undefined counter). Guards:
113/// `perfect_kernel_batch54::section_type_name_is_not_font_decoded`,
114/// `perfect_kernel_batch60::normalfont_note_expands_the_encoding_default`.
115pub(crate) fn type_name(stype: &Digested) -> String {
116  let name = stype
117    .revert()
118    .map(|t| t.to_string())
119    .unwrap_or_else(|_| stype.to_string());
120  strip_trailing_cs(name.trim())
121}
122
123fn strip_trailing_cs(stype: &str) -> String {
124  // Detect a trailing `\<letters>` token attached to the identifier. We strip
125  // exactly the well-known CS sentinels so we don't mis-mangle exotic but
126  // legitimate type names.
127  for tail in ["\\par", "\\@startsection@hook", "\\relax"] {
128    if let Some(stripped) = stype.strip_suffix(tail) {
129      return stripped.to_string();
130    }
131  }
132  stype.to_string()
133}

135/// The standard sectioning element for a `\@startsection` level, per
136/// latex.ltx's class conventions (classes.dtx: part −1, chapter 0, section 1,
137/// subsection 2, subsubsection 3, paragraph 4, subparagraph 5).
138fn section_element_for_level(level: i64) -> &'static str {
139  match level {
140    i64::MIN..=-1 => "ltx:part",
141    0 => "ltx:chapter",
142    1 => "ltx:section",
143    2 => "ltx:subsection",
144    3 => "ltx:subsubsection",
145    4 => "ltx:paragraph",
146    _ => "ltx:subparagraph",
147  }
148}
149
150/// Is `stype` one of the sectioning tag names the LaTeXML schema knows?
151fn is_known_section_type(stype: &str) -> bool {
152  matches!(
153    stype,
154    "part"
155      | "chapter"
156      | "section"
157      | "subsection"
158      | "subsubsection"
159      | "paragraph"
160      | "subparagraph"
161      | "appendix"
162      | "bibliography"
163      | "index"
164  )
165}

167/// The element `\@@numbered@section` / `\@@unnumbered@section` open for a
168/// section type. Mirrors Perl `latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:599-607`: a known
169/// schema tag is used as-is, `app` → `ltx:appendix`; otherwise Perl warns
170/// `malformed` and falls back to `ltx:section`. Before that fallback we consult
171/// the `SECTION_ELEMENT` mapping `\@startsection` records for a type it does
172/// not know, keyed by the heading LEVEL (`\DeclareSectionCommand`-defined
173/// headings — KOMA `\DeclareNewSectionCommand[level=2,…]{task}`, witness
174/// tudaexercise — carry their level only there), so the heading opens the
175/// element of its level instead of a warned `ltx:section`.
176fn section_element_for_type(stype: &str, numbered: bool) -> String {
177  section_element_for_type_maybe(stype).unwrap_or_else(|| {
178    let kind = if numbered { "numbered" } else { "unnumbered" };
179    Warn!(
180      "malformed",
181      s!("ltx:{stype}"),
182      s!("Tried to open an unknown tag ltx:{stype} for {kind} section")
183    );
184    "ltx:section".to_string()
185  })
186}
187
188/// `section_element_for_type` without the unknown-type warning: `None` when
189/// the type is unknown (the caller falls back to `ltx:section`).
190fn section_element_for_type_maybe(stype: &str) -> Option<String> {
191  if is_known_section_type(stype) {
192    Some(s!("ltx:{stype}"))
193  } else if stype == "app" {
194    Some("ltx:appendix".to_string())
195  } else {
196    // OXIDIZED_DESIGN #175 (level-keyed element; KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #118).
197    lookup_mapping("SECTION_ELEMENT", stype).map(|m| m.to_string())
198  }
199}

201/// Mirror of Perl `latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:2569-2574`'s
202/// `getShortSource =~ /^plain/` check. Two locator shapes count as
203/// "from plain":
204///   1. A short source starting with "plain" — e.g. `plain.tex`, `plain.dump.txt` — matching Perl's
205///      regex one-for-one.
206///   2. The Rust-only sentinel `<embedded:plain>` produced by dump-loaded definitions
207///      (`Locator::get_short_source` does not basename-strip this string because it contains a
208///      `:`).
209///
210/// We deliberately do NOT use looser `contains("plain.")` /
211/// `contains("/plain")` checks — they would match unrelated
212/// paths such as `complainttext.tex` or `…/plainness/foo.sty`.
213fn is_plain_definition_source(locator: Locator) -> bool {
214  if locator.get_short_source("").starts_with("plain") {
215    return true;
216  }
217  with(locator.get_source(), |s| s == "<embedded:plain>")
218}
219
220/// Mirror of Perl `isDefinableLaTeX` (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:2569-2574).
221/// Returns `(definable, plain_origin)`:
222///   * `definable` — Perl's bool result. The CS is either undefined, or its prior definition came
223///     from the plain pool (allowed to be overridden by LaTeX-pool `\newcommand`).
224///   * `plain_origin` — Rust-only flag. True when the prior definition came from plain. Callers use
225///     it to bypass any `<cs>:locked` guard installed on plain-pool CSes (Rust-specific lock
226///     mechanism not present in Perl). False when the CS was undefined (no prior locator → no lock
227///     to bypass).
228pub fn is_definable_latex(cs: &Token) -> Result<(bool, bool)> {
229  if is_definable(cs) {
230    return Ok((true, false));
231  }
232  // Autoload triggers (installed by `def_autoload` in tex.rs) appear
233  // defined but should not block `\newcommand` — Perl's analogous
234  // `DefAutoload` entries live in `OmniBus.cls.ltxml`, which isn't
235  // loaded for typical papers, so the user's `\newcommand` sees the
236  // CS as undefined and succeeds. Mirror that by treating the
237  // trigger as redefinable. (`plain_origin` stays false: there is
238  // no `<cs>:locked` guard to bypass for an autoload trigger.)
239  if has_value(&s!("{}:autoload", cs.to_string())) {
240    return Ok((true, false));
241  }
242  // A fallback class's guess (OmniBus's `\let\abst\abstract`, for a class with no binding): a document that
243  // compiles with its real class and `\newcommand`s the name shows that class leaves it undefined, so the
244  // document's definition wins (2605.05619's `\newcommand{\abst}[1]{|#1|}`; 59g, OXIDIZED_DESIGN_DIVERGENCES #408).
245  // The document's, and its author's own files' (K22: the author's files outrank our guesses; a raw file the author
246  // shipped beside the source, `binding::content::reading_author_file` — 0901.4335's `mn2e_journal_style.sty`): a
247  // TeX Live class or package loaded beside OmniBus (apa7.cls) yields to it, as raw files yield to bindings.
248  // A kernel stub (`DefinitionOrigin::Stub`: aaai's `\equalcontrib`, sect05.rs) yields to a raw file's own definition
249  // as well, since the real class or style defines the name (copernicus.cls:1673), and so does what a binding borrows
250  // from a package the real one does not load (`DefinitionOrigin::Borrowed`, `require_package_borrowed`: in LaTeX the
251  // name does not exist) — cc.cls's ccproof.sty:56 `\newenvironment{proof}` after theorem.sty (1507.02955).
252  if is_fallback_meaning(cs) {
253    use definition::origin::DefinitionOrigin;
254    let origin = definition::origin::current_origin();
255    if origin == DefinitionOrigin::Document
256      || (origin == DefinitionOrigin::File
257        && (reading_author_file()
258          || lookup_definition(cs)?
259            .is_some_and(|prev| prev.get_origin() == DefinitionOrigin::Stub)
260          || fallback_meaning_origin(cs) == Some(DefinitionOrigin::Borrowed)))
261    {
262      return Ok((true, false));
263    }
264  }
265  // A standard-class derivative read over its binding defines the declared text names the binding assigned as the
266  // class's own, as it does in TeX, read in the class's place (`state::standard_class_binding_name`; aip-cp.cls:875
267  // `\newcommand\refname{REFERENCES}`, 1506.04050; OXIDIZED_DESIGN_DIVERGENCES #731 rule 13).
268  // So does a copy its `\Provides` line routed to its binding, for a declared text name the binding (or one it
269  // requires) defined: proto.cls:1731 `\newcommand\apj{\ref@jnl{\it Astrophys.\ J.}}` over the aas_macros binding's
270  // "ApJ" (1402.7103; `state::routed_copy_text_name_yields`, rule 14, user ruling 2026-10-21); whether its definition
271  // stands for the document is decided by its body when the copy's read ends (`state::leave_copy_provides_frame`).
272  // The declarations are global (`state::declare_copy_text_names` assigns them so): a name any binding loaded so far
273  // declared counts for every routed copy, not only for one routed to that binding — a copy routed to the IEEEtran
274  // binding in a document that also loaded aas_macros may supply `\apj`.
275  if standard_class_binding_name(cs) || routed_copy_text_name_yields(cs) {
276    return Ok((true, false));
277  }
278  // Perl reads the definition's source (`=~ /^plain/`); Rust pools carry no such
279  // locator, so the plain LAYER is also read from the definition's provenance.
280  let plain = lookup_definition(cs)?.is_some_and(|prev| {
281    prev.get_origin() == definition::origin::DefinitionOrigin::Plain
282      || prev.get_locator().is_some_and(is_plain_definition_source)
283  });
284  Ok((plain, plain))
285}

292pub fn start_appendices(kind: &str) { begin_appendices(kind) }
293
294/// Whether `chapter` is a LaTeX counter — `\c@chapter` AND its reset list `\cl@chapter`, as every `\newcounter`
295/// (latex.ltx:10139 `\@definecounter`, our `new_counter`) makes both — so a class has chapters. Perl tests `\c@chapter`
296/// alone (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:690-693), safe while its kernel `\chapter` stayed defined; since
297/// OXIDIZED_DESIGN #179 retracts it in a chapterless class, tcilatex's no-chapters branch makes a bare count register
298/// (`\newcount\c@chapter`, tcilatex_tex.rs), and the appendix numbered `\thechapter.\Alph{section}` with `\thechapter`
299/// undefined (537 of run 336's papers: 1509.06343, quant-ph0609144). Not `\thechapter`: under OmniBus it is an autoload
300/// stub that loads book.cls (omnibus_cls.rs). Nor the counter a `\chapter` call TeX refuses makes for LaTeXML's
301/// chapter (`kernel_chapter_with_warning`, `\chapter:stand@in@counter`): jmlr's article appendix is "Appendix A".
302pub fn has_chapter_counter() -> bool {
303  let defined = |name: &str| lookup_definition(&T_CS!(name)).ok().flatten().is_some();
304  defined("\\c@chapter") && defined("\\cl@chapter") && !lookup_bool("\\chapter:stand@in@counter")
305}
306
307pub fn begin_appendices(counter: &str) {
308  // (numbered within chapters where the class has chapters, by `\chapter` — not a `chapter` counter alone, which
309  // WileyNJD-v2.cls:2410 and WileyNJDv5.cls:5728 declare for bookmarks with no `\chapter`: "Appendix A", not "0.A",
310  // 2211.16474; `state::class_defines_chapter`)
311  begin_appendices_within(
312    counter,
313    has_chapter_counter() && class_defines_chapter() && counter != "chapter",
314  )
315}
316
317/// [`begin_appendices`] with the numbering chosen by the caller: the units `\the<counter>` within the chapter
318/// (`\thechapter.\Alph{<counter>}`) or within the document (`\Alph{<counter>}`). A class with a `\chapter` of its own
319/// whose `\appendix` is still article's section-level one (llncs.cls:51 `\LoadClass{article}`, its `\chapter` at :302
320/// for proceedings volumes; article.cls:439-442) numbers them within the document: "Appendix A", not "0.A".
321pub fn begin_appendices_within(counter: &str, within_chapter: bool) {
322  let the_ctr = s!("\\the{counter}");
323  let the_ctr_id = s!("\\the{counter}@ID");
324  let cs_ctr = T_CS!(s!("\\{counter}"));
325  let_i(
326    &T_CS!("\\lx@save@theappendex"),
327    &T_CS!(&the_ctr),
328    Some(Scope::Global),
329  );
330  let_i(
331    &T_CS!("\\lx@save@theappendex@ID"),
332    &T_CS!(&the_ctr_id),
333    Some(Scope::Global),
334  );
335  let_i(&T_CS!("\\lx@save@appendix"), &cs_ctr, Some(Scope::Global));
336  let_i(
337    &T_CS!("\\lx@save@@appendix"),
338    &T_CS!("\\@appendix"),
339    Some(Scope::Global),
340  );
341  assign_mapping(
342    "BACKMATTER_ELEMENT",
343    "ltx:appendix",
344    Some(s!("ltx:{counter}")),
345  );
346  if within_chapter {
347    let _ = new_counter(
348      counter,
349      "chapter",
350      Some(NewDefault!(NewCounterOptions, idprefix => "A")),
351    );
352    let expansion: String = s!("\\thechapter.\\Alph{{{counter}}}");
353    let _ = def_macro(
354      T_CS!(the_ctr),
355      None,
356      Some(ExpansionBody::from(expansion)),
357      Some(NewDefault!(ExpandableOptions, scope => Some(Scope::Global))),
358    );
359  } else {
360    let _ = new_counter(
361      counter,
362      "document",
363      Some(NewDefault!(NewCounterOptions, idprefix => "A")),
364    );
365    let expansion: String = s!("\\Alph{{{counter}}}");
366    let _ = def_macro(
367      T_CS!(the_ctr),
368      None,
369      Some(ExpansionBody::from(expansion)),
370      Some(NewDefault!(ExpandableOptions, scope => Some(Scope::Global))),
371    );
372  }
373  let _ = assign_register(
374    &s!("\\c@{counter}"),
375    RegisterValue::Number(Number::new(0)),
376    None,
377    Vec::new(),
378  );
379  assign_mapping("counter_for_type", "appendix", Some(counter.to_string()));
380  let_i(&cs_ctr, &T_CS!("\\@@appendix"), Some(Scope::Global));
381  let_i(
382    &T_CS!("\\@appendix"),
383    &T_CS!("\\relax"),
384    Some(Scope::Global),
385  );
386}
387
388pub fn end_appendices() {
389  if let Some(counter_stored) = lookup_mapping("BACKMATTER_ELEMENT", "ltx:appendix") {
390    let counter_full = counter_stored.to_string();
391    let counter = counter_full.strip_prefix("ltx:").unwrap_or(&counter_full);
392    let the_ctr = s!("\\the{counter}");
393    let the_ctr_id = s!("\\the{counter}@ID");
394    let_i(
395      &T_CS!(the_ctr),
396      &T_CS!("\\lx@save@theappendex"),
397      Some(Scope::Global),
398    );
399    let_i(
400      &T_CS!(the_ctr_id),
401      &T_CS!("\\lx@save@theappendex@ID"),
402      Some(Scope::Global),
403    );
404    let_i(
405      &T_CS!(s!("\\{counter}")),
406      &T_CS!("\\lx@save@appendix"),
407      Some(Scope::Global),
408    );
409    let_i(
410      &T_CS!("\\@appendix"),
411      &T_CS!("\\lx@save@@appendix"),
412      Some(Scope::Global),
413    );
414  }
415}

417/// A note's size in the line it sits in: its displayed mark (the `mark` property, or plain's
418/// `prenote`), nothing without one — Perl's `\lx@note` `sizer => '#mark'`
419/// (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:460), which the port had dropped; extended to every note
420/// constructor (OXIDIZED_DESIGN_DIVERGENCES #391). The note's text is an insertion, set out of the
421/// line (tex.web §1100 `begin_insert_or_adjust`; in the HTML a popup, `.ltx_note_content`
422/// display:none). Measured with its body, a note holding a `\par` added its paragraphs' lines to
423/// the line; measured as its `tags`, it counted every registered tag form (cleveref's six: a
424/// `\resizebox` of a tabular with a footnote shrank to half); a `\footnotemark` summed its
425/// arguments, the counter's name included. Witnesses 2605.18427 S3.T4 (natural width 802.6 →
426/// 556.7pt, pdflatex 521.7), 2605.14713 S2.T1 (aa `\tablefoot`: `innerwidth` 2793.7 → 1644.8).
427/// Guard `perfect_kernel_batch58::notes_measure_as_their_mark`.
428pub fn note_size_in_line(whatsit: &Whatsit) -> Result<(Dimension, Dimension, Dimension)> {
429  for key in ["mark", "prenote"] {
430    if let Some(Stored::Digested(mark)) = whatsit.get_property(key).as_deref() {
431      return mark.compute_size(Default::default());
432    }
433  }
434  Ok(out_of_line_size())
435}

437/// The unit of a [`symbol_box_size`]: the font's em (quad) or ex (x-height).
438#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
439pub enum FontUnit {
440  Em,
441  Ex,
442}
443
444/// A symbol box `width` × `height` `unit`s of the whatsit's font, no depth: the size TeX measures for a class's QED
445/// box (a rule, `\openbox`, `\hbox{\rlap{$\sqcap$}$\sqcup$}`), given to a size-less constructor so a cell or box holding
446/// only it is not empty — alignment emptiness is by measured size (alignment/normalize.rs, Perl Alignment.pm:458-470),
447/// and a size-less whatsit alone in a cell was dropped. The constants are TFM ratios of the glyph font's design size
448/// (or the class's em/ex dimensions), applied as multiples of the current font's em or ex — equal at 10pt, where
449/// cmsy10's QUAD is 1.000003 of the design size.
450pub fn symbol_box_size(
451  whatsit: &Whatsit,
452  width: f64,
453  height: f64,
454  unit: FontUnit,
455) -> (Dimension, Dimension, Dimension) {
456  let font = whatsit
457    .get_font()
458    .ok()
459    .flatten()
460    .unwrap_or_else(|| Rc::new(Font::text_default()));
461  let scale = match unit {
462    FontUnit::Em => font.get_em_width(),
463    FontUnit::Ex => font.get_ex_height(),
464  } as f64;
465  (
466    Dimension::new((width * scale) as i64),
467    Dimension::new((height * scale) as i64),
468    Dimension::new(0),
469  )
470}

472/// llncs.cls:400, svjour3.cls (v3.2) :959, svmult.cls (v5.4) :1027, aa.cls (v5.3-7.0, :805-:914) and mn2e.cls:410
473/// `\squareforqed`/`\qedsymbol`
474/// `\hbox{\rlap{$\sqcap$}$\sqcup$}`: the glyph box of cmsy10's `\sqcup` (0.666669 × 0.555557 em).
475pub fn sqcup_qed_size(whatsit: &Whatsit) -> (Dimension, Dimension, Dimension) {
476  symbol_box_size(whatsit, 0.666669, 0.555557, FontUnit::Em)
477}

479/// The size in its line of material set out of it: a `\footnotetext`/`\endnotetext` (an
480/// insertion with no mark there) or a `\marginpar` (a float insertion, tex.web §1100) — nothing.
481pub fn out_of_line_size() -> (Dimension, Dimension, Dimension) {
482  (Dimension::new(0), Dimension::new(0), Dimension::new(0))
483}

485/// Whether a `\footnote` here is a minipage's (latex.ltx:16323 `\def\@mpfn{mpfootnote}`): `\@mpfn` names another
486/// counter than `footnote`.
487pub(crate) fn minipage_footnotes() -> Result<bool> {
488  Ok(has_meaning(&T_CS!("\\@mpfn")) && Expand!(Tokens!(T_CS!("\\@mpfn"))).to_string() != "footnote")
489}
490
491/// The tag a note of `note_type` is given (`\lx@note`'s `[<tag>]`, the `given` one or none). latex.ltx:17649-17656
492/// `\footnote` steps the counter `\@mpfn` names and marks the note `\thempfn` (`\footnote[<n>]` sets that counter to
493/// `<n>`); a minipage makes them `mpfootnote` and `\thempfootnote` (:16323, the counter set to 0; sect12.rs
494/// `{minipage}`), so a minipage's footnotes are lettered "a", "b", … (:17638) apart from the page's, which go on where
495/// they were; the note stays a footnote. `\footnotemark` keeps to `footnote` (:17677), and so does `\footnotetext`,
496/// which LaTeX marks `\thempfn` (:17690-17699): in a minipage LaTeX numbers a mark and letters the text answering it
497/// (2304.06412's table, `\footnotemark[1]` "1", `\footnotetext[1]` "a"), a mismatch that would leave the two unpaired.
498/// Perl (latex_base.pool.ltxml:270-272) numbers a minipage's notes as the page's (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1049). Witnesses
499/// 0802.0707, 2305.00493, 2309.00006; guards `perfect_kernel_batch78i::{minipage_footnotes_are_lettered,
500/// minipage_footnotetext_pairs_with_its_mark}`.
501pub(crate) fn footnote_tag<'a>(
502  note_type: &str,
503  given: Option<&'a Digested>,
504  number: &FootnoteNumber,
505) -> Result<Option<Cow<'a, Digested>>> {
506  if note_type != "footnote" || !minipage_footnotes()? {
507    return match given {
508      Some(given) => Ok(Some(Cow::Owned(numbered_footnote_mark(given, number)?))),
509      None => Ok(None),
510    };
511  }
512  let mut tokens = TokenizeInternal!(r"\begingroup").unlist();
513  match given {
514    None => tokens.extend(TokenizeInternal!(r"\stepcounter\@mpfn").unlist()),
515    Some(number) => {
516      tokens.extend(TokenizeInternal!(r"\csname c@\@mpfn\endcsname").unlist());
517      tokens.extend(number.revert()?.unlist());
518      tokens.push(T_CS!("\\relax"));
519    },
520  }
521  tokens.extend(TokenizeInternal!(r"\thempfn\endgroup").unlist());
522  Ok(Some(Cow::Owned(digest(Tokens::new(tokens))?)))
523}

525/// The document's class, as its `\documentclass` (or `\documentstyle`) named it (`lx@document@class`, recorded before
526/// the class loads): a binding another class's binding loads as its base (revtex4, IEEEtran, elsarticle and llncs
527/// load the article binding) is not the document's class, and its own title block is not in force.
528pub fn is_document_class(class: &str) -> bool { lookup_string("lx@document@class") == class }
529
530/// The title block's own `\thefootnote`, the one hook a binding declares its title's footnote marks with: defined, the
531/// marks of the notes made in the title, the authors and the date are it (`enter_title_footnotes`), and so are the
532/// frontmatter observer's Mark labels (`observer/rehearsal.rs` `TITLE_FOOTNOTE_HOOK`, OXIDIZED_DESIGN_DIVERGENCES #837,
533/// #851). Article, report and book declare it `\@fnsymbol\c@footnote` (`declare_fnsymbol_title_block`); a class
534/// numbering its title's marks otherwise defines its own (revtex4-2.cls:3040-3041 `\frontmatter@thefootnote`). Guard
535/// `perfect_kernel_batch78o::declared_title_thefootnote_prints_the_marks_the_observer_labels`.
536pub const TITLE_THEFOOTNOTE: &str = "\\lx@title@thefootnote";
537
538/// The title block of a class whose `\maketitle` marks its notes in `\@fnsymbol` — article, report and book (and
539/// extarticle, extreport, extbook, copies of them; article.cls:203-205, report.cls:211, book.cls:217, in the
540/// `\if@titlepage` false branch: `titlepage`, report's and book's default (:50-51) and an option of all three, keeps
541/// `\thefootnote`, `titlepage_default` `Some(..)`, the fallback for the binding's `\if@titlepage` after its options), siamltex (siamltex.cls:156-159, no title-page form, `None`) — when
542/// that class is the document's (`is_document_class`): the notes of the title, the authors and the date are marked so,
543/// and the footnote counter is set back to 0 after `\maketitle` (article.cls:190, :223; siamltex.cls:175), so the body's
544/// notes count from 1. The marks are made where the frontmatter digests the fields (`enter_title_footnotes`):
545/// `\footnotemark[1]` in an `\author` prints "∗" as the text `\footnotetext[1]` gives after
546/// `\renewcommand\thefootnote{\fnsymbol{footnote}}` (2412.20504, 2006.14582; siamltex 0903.0014; KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS
547/// #1060). Perl's classes mark them as the body (`\thefootnote`). The class's `\thanks` (and `\footnote`, which its
548/// `\maketitle` lets to `\thanks`) is `\footnotemark` and its text, so each steps the footnote counter, under a title
549/// page too (article.cls:173, :241, report.cls:179, :247, book.cls:185, :253; latex.ltx:17215 `\thanks`): the
550/// block's frontmatter notes step it as the `\maketitle` digests them (`lx_title_counts_footnotes`,
551/// `\lx@title@footnote@step`), and `\footnotemark[\arabic{footnote}]` after an author's `\footnote` is that note's "∗"
552/// (2201.11183 "Zhenan Fan∗1, Huang Fang∗2"; 2111.13260 "Suhani Vora1 *, Noha Radwan1 *").
553pub fn declare_fnsymbol_title_block(class: &str, titlepage_default: Option<bool>) -> Result<()> {
554  // (the class's `\if@titlepage` after its options, as the class reads it to define its `\maketitle`: article.cls:169,
555  // report.cls:175, book.cls:181; the binding declares it and its options, its default the fallback)
556  let titlepage = titlepage_default.map(|default| {
557    if_condition(&T_CS!("\\if@titlepage"))
558      .ok()
559      .flatten()
560      .unwrap_or(default)
561  });
562  if let Some(titlepage) = titlepage {
563    assign_value(&class_titlepage_key(class), titlepage, Some(Scope::Global));
564  }
565  if !is_document_class(class) {
566    return Ok(());
567  }
568  // (its `\thanks` steps the counter under a title page too: article.cls:173, :241, latex.ltx:17215)
569  assign_value("lx_title_counts_footnotes", true, Some(Scope::Global));
570  if titlepage != Some(true) {
571    def_macro(
572      T_CS!(TITLE_THEFOOTNOTE),
573      None,
574      TokenizeInternal!(r"\@fnsymbol\c@footnote"),
575      Some(ExpandableOptions {
576        scope: Some(Scope::Global),
577        ..Default::default()
578      }),
579    )?;
580  }
581  AddToMacro!("\\lx@maketitle@body", "\\setcounter{footnote}{0}");
582  Ok(())
583}
584
585/// The state key under which [`declare_fnsymbol_title_block`] keeps whether `class` (`article`, `report`, `book`, …) has
586/// its title page (`\if@titlepage` true after its options), so its `\maketitle` runs no `\@maketitle`
587/// (`ledger::class_maketitle_runs`, `MaketitleRuns::WithoutTitlepage`, TP1c).
588pub fn class_titlepage_key(class: &str) -> String { s!("lx_class_titlepage:{class}") }
589
590/// Before a note is made in the title block (a field the frontmatter digests: the title, an author, the date) of a
591/// class whose title marks its notes in a `\thefootnote` of its own ([`TITLE_THEFOOTNOTE`],
592/// `declare_fnsymbol_title_block`): `\thefootnote` is that one for the rest of the field, as in the class's
593/// `\maketitle` group.
594pub(crate) fn enter_title_footnotes() -> Result<()> {
595  // (the title block's contacts too — an affiliation, an address: the class prints them inside its title, under the same
596  // marks; revtex's `\affiliation{\footnotemark[2]Lab … \footnotetext[2]{\tt volkov@…}}` answers the `\author{Mikhail S.
597  // Volkov\footnotemark[2]}` above it with the same †, hep-th0302032)
598  if matches!(
599    lookup_string("lx_frontmatter_item").as_str(),
600    "ltx:creator" | "ltx:title" | "ltx:date" | "ltx:contact"
601  ) && has_meaning(&T_CS!(TITLE_THEFOOTNOTE))
602  {
603    let_i(&T_CS!("\\thefootnote"), &T_CS!(TITLE_THEFOOTNOTE), None);
604  }
605  Ok(())
606}

608/// A footnote's mark given as `[<n>]`: latex.ltx:17652-17657 `\@xfootnote`, :17678-17682 `\@xfootnotemark` and
609/// :17694-17699 `\@xfootnotenext` set the counter to `<n>` in a group and mark the note `\thefootnote` there, so under
610/// `\renewcommand\thefootnote{\fnsymbol{footnote}}` (or footmisc's `symbol`) `\footnotetext[1]` is "∗", as the
611/// `\footnotemark` it answers. A mark that is not a number but prints something (`\footnotemark[$\dagger$]`, an error
612/// in LaTeX: "Missing number, treated as zero", the note marked 0) is printed as given, as before and as in Perl
613/// (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1060, OXIDIZED_DESIGN_DIVERGENCES #851), with no diagnostic: a class may read the mark as text
614/// (pasj00.cls:2237-2239 and emulateapj.cls:558-563 `\@xfootnotemark` set `\@thefnmark{#1}`, ecai.cls:480 its author
615/// `\footnotemark[\dagger]`), which our locked `\footnotemark` does not see (78u, SYNC). `number` is the one
616/// `given_footnote_number` read for the note; a minipage's notes are `footnote_tag`'s.
617pub(crate) fn numbered_footnote_mark(
618  given: &Digested,
619  number: &FootnoteNumber,
620) -> Result<Digested> {
621  let Some(digits) = number.digits.as_ref() else {
622    return digest(given.revert()?);
623  };
624  let mut tokens = TokenizeInternal!(r"\begingroup\c@footnote").unlist();
625  tokens.extend(digits.clone().unlist());
626  tokens.extend(TokenizeInternal!(r"\relax\thefootnote\endgroup").unlist());
627  digest(Tokens::new(tokens))
628}
629
630/// The number a footnote's `[<n>]` gives (`given_footnote_number`).
631#[derive(Default)]
632pub(crate) struct FootnoteNumber {
633  /// Its digits, once expanded (`2`, `\arabic{footnote}`), or a count register's value (`\value{footnote}`); none for
634  /// any other mark, and for a note given no `[<n>]`, which is the counter's.
635  digits:       Option<Tokens>,
636  /// Whether the number moves with the footnote counter: a note given no `[<n>]`, and a `[<n>]` such as
637  /// `\value{footnote}`, `\arabic{footnote}` or `\the\c@footnote` (a literal `2`, or `\thealtnum` of a counter of its
638  /// own, does not).
639  from_counter: bool,
640}
641
642/// The number a footnote's `[<n>]` gives (`numbered_footnote_mark`, `footnote_pairing`), read once per note (none for
643/// any other type). The notes read `[<n>]` undigested (`OptionalUndigested`, sect03.rs `\lx@note`, `\lx@notemark`,
644/// `\lx@notetext`), as TeX reads `\c@footnote #1\relax` — digested on its own, `\value{footnote}` was a register
645/// assignment missing its number. The look is a check, its diagnostics held: a `[<n>]` whose expansion errs
646/// (`\footnotemark[\the\relax]`) is no number, and the mark's digestion as given reports that error, once, as pdflatex
647/// does (review probes rev78o2 valerr, val). Whether the number is the counter's is read the same way, the counter one
648/// ahead for the look. Any other `[<n>]` that is no number is `tex_footnote_number`'s.
649pub(crate) fn given_footnote_number(
650  note_type: &str,
651  given: Option<&Digested>,
652) -> Result<FootnoteNumber> {
653  if note_type != "footnote" {
654    return Ok(FootnoteNumber::default());
655  }
656  let Some(given) = given else {
657    return Ok(FootnoteNumber {
658      digits:       None,
659      from_counter: true,
660    });
661  };
662  let hold = util::logger::DiagnosticsHold::begin();
663  let digits = footnote_number_digits(given)?;
664  let from_counter = match digits.as_ref() {
665    Some(digits) => {
666      let saved = counter_value("footnote")?;
667      assign_register(
668        "\\c@footnote",
669        Number::new(saved.value_of() + 1).into(),
670        None,
671        Vec::new(),
672      )?;
673      let ahead = footnote_number_digits(given);
674      assign_register("\\c@footnote", saved.into(), None, Vec::new())?;
675      ahead?.map(|n| n.to_string()) != Some(digits.to_string())
676    },
677    None => false,
678  };
679  if !hold.is_empty() {
680    hold.discard();
681    return Ok(FootnoteNumber::default());
682  }
683  hold.commit();
684  let digits = match digits {
685    Some(digits) => Some(digits),
686    None => tex_footnote_number(given)?,
687  };
688  Ok(FootnoteNumber { digits, from_counter })
689}
690
691/// A `[<n>]` read as `\c@footnote #1\relax` reads it (latex.ltx:17678-17682), by the `\setcounter` siblings' reader,
692/// when what the scan leaves prints nothing: `\relax`, `\value` of a counter not yet defined (latex.ltx:10127). Then the
693/// mark is TeX's, its "Missing number, treated as zero" reported once (2407.13730, 2606.19583). A blank `[]` stays as
694/// given, as text marks do: arxstspdf.cls:1912's `\freefootnotetext[]` is a note with no mark (1011.1160).
695fn tex_footnote_number(given: &Digested) -> Result<Option<Tokens>> {
696  let given = given.revert()?;
697  if given
698    .unlist_ref()
699    .iter()
700    .all(|t| t.get_catcode() == Catcode::SPACE)
701  {
702    return Ok(None);
703  }
704  let hold = util::logger::DiagnosticsHold::begin();
705  let (value, tail) = read_braced_value(given, RegisterType::Number)?;
706  let relax = lookup_meaning(&T_RELAX!());
707  let prints_nothing = tail
708    .iter()
709    .all(|t| t.get_catcode() == Catcode::SPACE || (relax.is_some() && lookup_meaning(t) == relax));
710  if !prints_nothing {
711    hold.discard();
712    return Ok(None);
713  }
714  hold.commit();
715  let value = Number::from(value).value_of().to_string();
716  Ok(Some(Tokens::new(ExplodeText!(&value))))
717}
718
719/// `given_footnote_number`'s digits of a `[<n>]`.
720fn footnote_number_digits(given: &Digested) -> Result<Option<Tokens>> {
721  let expanded = Expand!(given.revert()?);
722  let text = expanded.to_string();
723  let text = text.trim();
724  if !text.is_empty()
725    && text
726      .trim_start_matches('-')
727      .chars()
728      .all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit())
729  {
730    return Ok(Some(Tokens::new(ExplodeText!(text))));
731  }
732  // (`\c@footnote #1\relax` reads `#1` as TeX's scan_int does, tex.web §440-§445: its leading spaces skipped, as in
733  // `[ \numexpr…]`, and an internal integer read whole)
734  let toks = expanded.unlist_ref();
735  let lead = toks
736    .iter()
737    .take_while(|t| t.get_catcode() == Catcode::SPACE)
738    .count();
739  Ok(match &toks[lead..] {
740    [register] if lookup_definition(register)?.is_some_and(|d| d.is_register()) => {
741      Some(Expand!(Tokens!(T_CS!("\\the"), *register)))
742    },
743    // (an e-TeX integer expression, which `\c@footnote #1\relax` reads whole: `\footnotetext[\numexpr\value{footnote}-1]`,
744    // 2210.14698; Perl and int59a "Missing number, treated as zero", the mark lost, KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1135. The
745    // expression ends at its own `\relax` (`[\numexpr\value{footnote}-1\relax]`, the common form) or at ours, and the
746    // `\relax` left over is unexpandable, so it is not part of the number: `\the\numexpr…\relax\relax` gives "1\relax")
747    [first, rest @ ..] if *first == T_CS!("\\numexpr") => {
748      let mut the = vec![T_CS!("\\the"), *first];
749      the.extend(rest.iter().copied());
750      the.push(T_CS!("\\relax"));
751      let mut value = Expand!(Tokens::new(the)).unlist();
752      while value
753        .last()
754        .is_some_and(|t| *t == T_CS!("\\relax") || t.get_catcode() == Catcode::SPACE)
755      {
756        value.pop();
757      }
758      let value = Tokens::new(value).to_string();
759      let value = value.trim();
760      (!value.is_empty()
761        && value
762          .trim_start_matches('-')
763          .chars()
764          .all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()))
765      .then(|| Tokens::new(ExplodeText!(value)))
766    },
767    _ => None,
768  })
769}
770
771/// A footnote's bookkeeping for `relocate_footnote`, kept on the note: the value of the footnote counter it stands for
772/// (`_fnvalue`: its `[<n>]`'s number, or the counter as it stepped or stands) — none for a minipage's notes, which
773/// count apart, and any other type —, and, in a class that sets the counter back after its `\maketitle`
774/// (`lx_title_counts_footnotes`, `declare_fnsymbol_title_block`), whether its number is the counter's (`_fncounted`,
775/// `FootnoteNumber::from_counter`): such a note in the title block has the title's count, one after it the body's,
776/// which counts from 1 again (`same_count`).
777pub(crate) fn footnote_pairing(
778  props: &mut SymHashMap<Stored>,
779  note_type: &str,
780  given: Option<&Digested>,
781  number: &FootnoteNumber,
782) -> Result<()> {
783  if note_type != "footnote" || minipage_footnotes()? {
784    return Ok(());
785  }
786  let value = match given {
787    Some(_) => number
788      .digits
789      .as_ref()
790      .and_then(|n| n.to_string().trim().parse::<i64>().ok()),
791    None => Some(counter_value("footnote")?.value_of()),
792  };
793  if let Some(value) = value {
794    props.insert("fnvalue", Stored::String(pin(value.to_string())));
795  }
796  if number.from_counter && lookup_bool("lx_title_counts_footnotes") {
797    props.insert("fncounted", Stored::String(pin("true")));
798  }
799  Ok(())
800}
801
802pub fn make_note_tags(
803  counter: &str,
804  mark_opt: Option<&Digested>,
805  tag_opt: Option<Cow<Digested>>,
806) -> Result<SymHashMap<Stored>> {
807  // Cluster A reprise (hep-ph0204075): strip a trailing \par that the {}
808  // parameter reader sometimes pulls into the counter identifier. Without
809  // this, the s!("\\the{counter}") and s!("\\ext@{counter}") paths below
810  // produce CSes named `\thefootnote\par` / `\ext@footnote\par`.
811  let counter = strip_trailing_cs(counter);
812  let counter = counter.as_str();
813  if let Some(tag) = tag_opt {
814    let mut props = ref_step_id(counter)?;
815    let mark = match mark_opt {
816      None => tag.clone(),
817      Some(mark) => Cow::Borrowed(mark),
818    };
819    props.insert("mark", mark.into());
820    props.insert(
821      "tags",
822      digest(Tokens!(
823        T_BEGIN!(),
824        T_CS!("\\def"),
825        T_CS!(s!("\\the{counter}")),
826        T_BEGIN!(),
827        tag.revert()?,
828        T_END!(),
829        T_CS!("\\def"),
830        T_CS!(s!("\\typerefnum@{counter}")),
831        T_BEGIN!(),
832        T_CS!(s!("\\{counter}typerefname")),
833        T_SPACE!(),
834        tag.revert()?,
835        T_END!(),
836        T_CS!("\\lx@make@tags"),
837        T_BEGIN!(),
838        T_OTHER!(counter),
839        T_END!(),
840        T_END!()
841      ))?
842      .into(),
843    );
844    Ok(props)
845  } else {
846    // LaTeX steps a note with `\stepcounter\@mpfn` (latex.ltx:17649, :17675), not `\refstepcounter`.
847    let mut props = ref_step_counter(counter, false)?;
848    let mark = Stored::Digested(match mark_opt {
849      None => digest_text(Tokens!(T_CS!(s!("\\the{counter}"))))?,
850      Some(mark) => mark.clone(),
851    });
852    props.insert("mark", mark);
853    Ok(props)
854  }
855}
856
857/// Pair a note's mark and text: Perl's `relocateFootnote` (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:498-510)
858/// matches their `mark`s exactly; here spaces are ignored, so a mark printed as set
859/// (`\tablenotemark{c, d}`, deluxetable_sty.rs `shown_mark`) pairs with the text given `c,d`. A
860/// counter's mark has no space, so a `\footnotemark`'s pairing is Perl's. A mark and a text that print no common
861/// mark, one of them in the title block — or neither printing a mark (`title_block_partner`) —, pair by the footnote
862/// counter value they stand for (`_fnvalue`, `footnote_pairing`): article's title block marks
863/// `\footnotemark[2]` "†" where a `\footnotetext[2]` after `\maketitle` prints "2" (2505.14146; pdflatex prints the
864/// two apart, the author pairs them), a class whose title marks are not known (siamltex: 1406.0089, 1503.07490), and
865/// `\fnsymbol`'s "∥" against `\@fnsymbol`'s "‖" for 6 (2002.11721). Either way a mark and a text on the two sides of
866/// a class's counter reset after `\maketitle` pair only as `same_count` admits. KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1060,
867/// OXIDIZED_DESIGN_DIVERGENCES #851.
868pub fn relocate_footnote(document: &mut Document, node: &mut Node) -> Result<()> {
869  if let Some(caps) = NOTE_TEXT_END.captures(&node.get_attribute("role").unwrap_or_default()) {
870    let notetype = caps.get(1).map_or("", |m| m.as_str());
871    let mut paired = false;
872    if let Some(mark) = node.get_attribute("mark") {
873      let key = mark.replace(' ', "");
874      for mut marknote in document.findnodes(
875        &format!(".//ltx:note[@role='{notetype}mark'][translate(@mark,' ','')='{key}']"),
876        None,
877      ) {
878        if is_descendant_or_self(&marknote, node) || !same_count(document, &marknote, node, BY_MARK)
879        {
880          continue;
881        }
882        relocate_footnote_aux(document, notetype, &mut marknote, node)?;
883        paired = true;
884      }
885    }
886    if !paired && let Some(value) = node.get_attribute(FOOTNOTE_VALUE) {
887      let partner = title_block_partner(document, node);
888      for mut marknote in document.findnodes(
889        &format!(".//ltx:note[@role='{notetype}mark'][@{FOOTNOTE_VALUE}='{value}']{partner}"),
890        None,
891      ) {
892        if is_descendant_or_self(&marknote, node)
893          || !same_count(document, &marknote, node, BY_VALUE)
894        {
895          continue;
896        }
897        relocate_footnote_aux(document, notetype, &mut marknote, node)?;
898      }
899    }
900  } else if let Some(caps) = NOTE_MARK_END.captures(&node.get_attribute("role").unwrap_or_default())
901  {
902    let notetype = caps.get(1).map_or("", |m| m.as_str());
903    let mut paired = false;
904    if let Some(mark) = node.get_attribute("mark") {
905      let key = mark.replace(' ', "");
906      for mut textnote in document.findnodes(
907        &format!(".//ltx:note[@role='{notetype}text'][translate(@mark,' ','')='{key}']"),
908        None,
909      ) {
910        if is_descendant_or_self(node, &textnote) || !same_count(document, node, &textnote, BY_MARK)
911        {
912          continue;
913        }
914        relocate_footnote_aux(document, notetype, node, &mut textnote)?;
915        paired = true;
916      }
917    }
918    if !paired && let Some(value) = node.get_attribute(FOOTNOTE_VALUE) {
919      let partner = title_block_partner(document, node);
920      for mut textnote in document.findnodes(
921        &format!(".//ltx:note[@role='{notetype}text'][@{FOOTNOTE_VALUE}='{value}']{partner}"),
922        None,
923      ) {
924        if is_descendant_or_self(node, &textnote)
925          || !same_count(document, node, &textnote, BY_VALUE)
926        {
927          continue;
928        }
929        relocate_footnote_aux(document, notetype, node, &mut textnote)?;
930      }
931    }
932  }
933  Ok(())
934}
935
936/// The bookkeeping attribute holding the footnote counter value a note stands for (`footnote_pairing`).
937const FOOTNOTE_VALUE: &str = "_fnvalue";
938
939/// The bookkeeping attribute of a note numbered from the footnote counter in a class that sets the counter back after
940/// its `\maketitle` (`footnote_pairing`).
941const FOOTNOTE_COUNTED: &str = "_fncounted";
942
943/// Whether the note is in the title block: in a creator, the document's title (not a section's: 1907.00457's
944/// `\section{Results\footnotemark}` and the `\footnotetext` after it are one body note) or the date.
945fn in_title_block(document: &mut Document, node: &Node) -> bool {
946  !document
947    .findnodes(
948      "ancestor::ltx:creator | ancestor::ltx:title[parent::ltx:document] | ancestor::ltx:date",
949      Some(node),
950    )
951    .is_empty()
952}
953
954/// `same_count`'s pairing by the printed mark.
955const BY_MARK: bool = false;
956/// `same_count`'s pairing by the counter value.
957const BY_VALUE: bool = true;
958
959/// Whether a mark and a text that print the same mark (`BY_MARK`) or stand for the same counter value (`BY_VALUE`) are
960/// one note (`relocate_footnote`), in a class that sets the footnote counter back to 0 after its `\maketitle`
961/// (article.cls:190, :223, report.cls:196, :229): two notes on the same side of the reset (both in the title block, or
962/// neither) count alike, as before; across it, a note numbered from the counter (`_fncounted`: no `[<n>]`,
963/// `[\value{footnote}]`, `[\arabic{footnote}]`) has its side's count. So a value pairs across the reset only between two
964/// notes that name it (`\footnotemark[2]` "†" and the body's `\footnotetext[2]` "2", 2505.14146), and a printed mark
965/// unless both are counted: article's "C†" for `\footnotemark[\value{footnote}]` after two `\thanks` is not the body's
966/// `\footnotetext[2]` "2 Body text two", and report's (title page) "B2" for a bare `\footnotemark` after a `\thanks` is
967/// not the body's bare `\footnotetext` "2", which answers the body's own mark (pdflatex; review probes rev78o2 art2,
968/// ttp3), while a title's bare `\footnotemark` "∗" and the body's `\footnotetext[1]` "∗" under `\fnsymbol` print one
969/// note (2507.05750, 1405.7962; astro-ph9712060's `[\thealtnum]` on both sides, a counter of its own).
970fn same_count(document: &mut Document, mark: &Node, text: &Node, by_value: bool) -> bool {
971  let counted = |node: &Node| node.get_attribute(FOOTNOTE_COUNTED).is_some();
972  let (mark_counted, text_counted) = (counted(mark), counted(text));
973  if !(mark_counted || text_counted)
974    || in_title_block(document, mark) == in_title_block(document, text)
975  {
976    return true;
977  }
978  !by_value && !(mark_counted && text_counted)
979}
980
981/// The notes a footnote mark or text pairs with by the counter value they stand for (`relocate_footnote`), as an XPath
982/// predicate on the partner: a title block's marks (article's `\@fnsymbol`, `declare_fnsymbol_title_block`) and the
983/// body's numbers are the two that print no common mark for the same note, so one of the two is in the title block —
984/// any note, when `node` is there, else one in a creator, the title or the date; and two notes that print no mark at all
985/// (`{\renewcommand\thefootnote{}\footnotemark\footnotetext{…}}`, 2606.03847) print the same, so they pair as a mark and
986/// its text printing the same mark do. A body text and a body mark of the same number that print different marks stay
987/// apart, as in pdflatex: `\footnotetext[1]{…}` under `\fnsymbol` ("∗ Equal contribution") is not the table's
988/// `\footnotemark` "1" (review probe rev78o f2).
989fn title_block_partner(document: &mut Document, node: &Node) -> &'static str {
990  if in_title_block(document, node) {
991    ""
992  } else if node
993    .get_attribute("mark")
994    .is_none_or(|mark| mark.trim().is_empty())
995  {
996    "[ancestor::ltx:creator or ancestor::ltx:title[parent::ltx:document] or ancestor::ltx:date or normalize-space(@mark)='']"
997  } else {
998    "[ancestor::ltx:creator or ancestor::ltx:title[parent::ltx:document] or ancestor::ltx:date]"
999  }
1000}
1001
1002fn relocate_footnote_aux(
1003  document: &mut Document,
1004  notetype: &str,
1005  marknote: &mut Node,
1006  textnote: &mut Node,
1007) -> Result<()> {
1008  document.append_clone(marknote, textnote.get_child_nodes())?;
1009  document.set_attribute(marknote, "role", notetype)?;
1010  if let Some(labels) = textnote.get_attribute("labels") {
1011    document.generate_id(marknote, "")?;
1012    document.set_attribute(marknote, "labels", &labels)?;
1013  }
1014  document.safe_unlink(textnote.clone());
1015  Ok(())
1016}
1017
1018pub fn only_preamble(cs: &str) -> Result<()> {
1019  // Legal while `inPreamble`. `\begin{document}` keeps `inPreamble=1` through the
1020  // begindocument hooks and only clears it AFTER them (matching real latex.ltx,
1021  // which disables the \@onlypreamble commands via `\@preamblecmds` (L9522) only
1022  // after firing the begindocument hook (L9512)), so a `\RequirePackage`/
1023  // `\usepackage` deferred to `\AtBeginDocument` is still legal — no separate hook
1024  // flag needed. Paragraph-breaking inside `\AtBeginDocument` (upstream #2754) is
1025  // handled independently by `\par`'s no-op-in-vertical-mode rule, NOT by clearing
1026  // `inPreamble` early (upstream #2846 is thus unnecessary; KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #43).
1027  if !lookup_bool_sym(pin!("inPreamble")) {
1028    Error!(
1029      "unexpected",
1030      cs,
1031      s!("The current command '{cs}' can only appear in the preamble")
1032    );
1033  }
1034  Ok(())
1035}
1036
1037pub fn tabular_bindings(
1038  mut template: Template,
1039  mut properties: SymHashMap<Stored>,
1040  mut xml_attributes: HashMap<String, String>,
1041) -> Result<()> {
1042  for col in template.get_columns_mut() {
1043    col.mark_intercol_after();
1044  }
1045  for col in template.get_repeated_mut() {
1046    col.mark_intercol_after();
1047  }
1048  // The macro its `\\` is in TeX: the kernel's `\@tabularcr` (latex.ltx:16562), unless the binding names its own
1049  // (longtable.sty:133 `\LT@tabularcr`); `\noalign\\` reads it (tex_tables.rs).
1050  if !properties.contains_key("row_end") {
1051    properties.insert("row_end", Stored::Token(T_CS!("\\@tabularcr")));
1052  }
1053  if !properties.contains_key("guess_headers")
1054    && let Some(v) = lookup_value("GUESS_TABULAR_HEADERS")
1055  {
1056    properties.insert("guess_headers", v);
1057  }
1058  if !xml_attributes.contains_key("colsep") {
1059    let sep_opt = lookup_dimension("\\tabcolsep");
1060    if let Some(sep) = sep_opt
1061      && sep.value_of()
1062        != lookup_dimension("\\lx@default@tabcolsep")
1063          .unwrap()
1064          .value_of()
1065    {
1066      xml_attributes.insert(String::from("colsep"), sep.to_attribute());
1067    }
1068  }
1069  if !xml_attributes.contains_key("rowsep") {
1070    let astr = do_expand(T_CS!("\\arraystretch"))?.to_string();
1071    if astr != "1"
1072      && let Ok(astr_f) = astr.parse::<f64>()
1073      && astr_f != 1.0
1074    {
1075      let rowsep = Dimension::from_str(&s!("{}em", astr_f - 1.0))?;
1076      xml_attributes.insert(String::from("rowsep"), rowsep.to_attribute());
1077    }
1078  }
1079  if !properties.contains_key("strut") {
1080    properties.insert("isLaTeX", Stored::Bool(true));
1081    if let Some(strut) = array_strut() {
1082      properties.insert("strut", strut);
1083    }
1084  }
1085  if array_zeroes_interline() {
1086    properties.insert("zero_interline", Stored::Bool(true));
1087  }
1088  alignment_bindings(template, String::from("text"), properties, xml_attributes);
1089  let_i(&T_CS!("\\\\"), &T_CS!("\\@tabularcr"), None);
1090  let_i(&T_CS!("\\lx@intercol"), &T_CS!("\\lx@text@intercol"), None);
1091  let_i(&T_CS!("\\tabularnewline"), &T_CS!("\\\\"), None);
1092  for name in [
1093    "@row@before",
1094    "@row@after",
1095    "@column@before",
1096    "@column@after",
1097  ] {
1098    let cs = T_CS!(s!("\\lx@alignment{name}"));
1099    let cs_def = lookup_definition(&cs)?.unwrap();
1100    let mut expansion = cs_def.get_expansion().cloned().unwrap_or_default();
1101    expansion.push(T_CS!(s!("\\@tabular{name}")));
1102    def_macro(cs, None, expansion, None)?;
1103  }
1104  Ok(())
1105}
1106
1107/// Port of Perl's `latexChangeCase` function.
1108/// Applies Unicode case conversion (not TeX uccode/lccode tables) to tokens.
1109/// Converts CC_SPACE to T_SPACE (matching latex3 behavior).
1110/// Handles \protect + excluded CS tokens (text_case_exclude mapping), and the
1111/// l3text case-change declarations a CS can carry (see [`lx_case_change_cs`]).
1112fn lx_change_case_tokens(req_case: &str, tokens: &Tokens) -> Result<Vec<Token>> {
1113  let mut keep = false;
1114  lx_change_case_in_mouth(req_case, tokens, true, &mut keep, 0)
1115}
1116
1117/// Case-change `tokens` from a mouth of their own. `expand` is false for a
1118/// `\DeclareCaseChangeEquivalent` replacement, which l3text walks with its
1119/// case loop only, never re-expanding it (`\__text_change_case_replace:nnnn`,
1120/// expl3-code.tex:36693-36694), as is the material before an excluded
1121/// command's argument. `keep` carries the sentence/title
1122/// "rest of the word is left alone" state across such a nested walk.
1123fn lx_change_case_in_mouth(
1124  req_case: &str,
1125  tokens: &Tokens,
1126  expand: bool,
1127  keep: &mut bool,
1128  depth: usize,
1129) -> Result<Vec<Token>> {
1130  let mouth = Mouth::new("", None)?;
1131  open_mouth(mouth, false);
1132  unread(tokens.clone());
1133  let result = lx_read_and_change_case(req_case, expand, keep, depth);
1134  close_mouth(true)?;
1135  result
1136}
1137
1138/// What [`lx_case_change_cs`] did with a CS or active token.
1139enum CaseChangeCs {
1140  /// The token (and whatever it consumed) is accounted for in the result.
1141  Done,
1142  /// The token carries no case-change declaration; the caller reads it as
1143  /// Perl's `latexChangeCase` does.
1144  Plain,
1145}
1146
1147/// Push a token the case changer passes through VERBATIM (l3text
1148/// `\exp_not:n`/`\exp_not:v`). The result is re-read by the `\edef` in
1149/// `\MakeUppercase`, so a CS or active token is shielded with `\dont_expand`:
1150/// expanding it there would run it on the already case-changed tokens after
1151/// it (textalpha's `\LGR@hiatus` composites, `\CaseSwitch` branches).
1152fn push_case_verbatim(result: &mut Vec<Token>, tok: Token) {
1153  if tok.get_catcode().is_active_or_cs() {
1154    result.push(T_CS!("\\dont_expand"));
1155  }
1156  result.push(tok);
1157}
1158
1159/// l3text's replacement for `\DeclareCaseChangeEquivalent{<cs>}{<replacement>}`
1160/// (latex.ltx:22400 `\cs_new_eq:NN \DeclareCaseChangeEquivalent
1161/// \text_declare_case_equivalent:Nn`), stored in the tl
1162/// `\l__text_case_<\token_to_str:N cs>_tl` (expl3-code.tex:36952-36956) and
1163/// read at change time (`\__text_change_case_replace:nnnN`,
1164/// expl3-code.tex:36684-36692). `name` is the token's string, `\>` for `\>`.
1165fn case_change_equivalent(name: &str) -> Result<Option<Tokens>> {
1166  // `\cs_if_exist:cTF` — a `\relax` left by a `\csname` probe is not a tl.
1167  Ok(
1168    match lookup_definition_stored(&T_CS!(s!("\\l__text_case_{name}_tl")))? {
1169      Some(Stored::Expandable(tl)) => match tl.get_expansion() {
1170        Some(ExpansionBody::Tokens(replacement)) => Some(replacement.clone()),
1171        _ => None,
1172      },
1173      _ => None,
1174    },
1175  )
1176}
1177
1178/// Whether `tok` is `\CaseSwitch` (latex.ltx:22399 `\cs_new_eq:NN \CaseSwitch
1179/// \text_case_switch:nnnn`): l3text's case loop tests the meaning
1180/// (expl3-code.tex:36698 `\cs_if_eq:NNTF #4 \text_case_switch:nnnn`).
1181fn is_case_switch(tok: &Token) -> bool {
1182  let switch = T_CS!("\\text_case_switch:nnnn");
1183  has_meaning(&switch) && x_equals(tok, &switch)
1184}
1185
1186/// The letter-like mapping of the CS named `name` in `map` (`text_uppercase`
1187/// or `text_lowercase`, keyed `"<cs> "` by `\lx@prepare@case@mapping`): l3text's
1188/// `c__text_<case>case_<cs>_tl` constants (expl3-code.tex:36749-36768
1189/// `\__text_change_case_letterlike:nnnnnN`).
1190fn case_letterlike(map: &str, name: &str) -> Option<Token> {
1191  match lookup_mapping(map, &s!("{name} ")) {
1192    Some(Stored::Token(mapped)) => Some(mapped),
1193    _ => None,
1194  }
1195}
1196
1197/// l3text's exclusion list (`\AddToNoCaseChangeList`, `\l_text_case_exclude_arg_tl`,
1198/// expl3-code.tex:36002-36007), the first check of both its passes
1199/// (`\__text_expand_exclude:N`, 36192-36233; `\__text_change_case_exclude:nnnN`,
1200/// 36632-36683). The command passes unchanged; everything up to its first `{`
1201/// (a star, optional arguments: `#5` of `\__text_change_case_exclude:nnnNw`,
1202/// 36668-36669) is case-changed without expansion, and the braced argument is
1203/// kept as is (36670-36683). So `\MakeUppercase{\cite[see][p.~5]{k}}` is
1204/// `\cite[SEE][P.~5]{k}`, and `\cite*{k}` keeps its star. Perl reads one
1205/// `[opt]` and cases it with an expanding changer. `prefix` is the `\protect`
1206/// of a robust command, whose output keeps Perl's shape.
1207fn lx_case_change_excluded(
1208  req_case: &str,
1209  tok: Token,
1210  name: &str,
1211  prefix: Option<Token>,
1212  depth: usize,
1213  result: &mut Vec<Token>,
1214) -> Result<bool> {
1215  if lookup_mapping("text_case_exclude", name).is_none() {
1216    return Ok(false);
1217  }
1218  let mut before_arg = Vec::new();
1219  while let Some(t) = read_token_across_input_ends()? {
1220    if t.get_catcode() == Catcode::BEGIN {
1221      unread_one(t);
1222      break;
1223    }
1224    before_arg.push(t);
1225  }
1226  match prefix {
1227    Some(protect) => {
1228      result.push(protect);
1229      result.push(tok);
1230    },
1231    None => push_case_verbatim(result, tok),
1232  }
1233  if !before_arg.is_empty() {
1234    let mut keep = false;
1235    result.extend(lx_change_case_in_mouth(
1236      req_case,
1237      &Tokens::new(before_arg),
1238      false,
1239      &mut keep,
1240      depth + 1,
1241    )?);
1242  }
1243  let arg = read_arg(ExpansionLevel::Off)?;
1244  result.push(T_BEGIN!());
1245  result.extend(arg.unlist());
1246  result.push(T_END!());
1247  Ok(true)
1248}
1249
1250/// l3text's case-change declarations on a CS met by its case loop, in its
1251/// order: a `\DeclareCaseChangeEquivalent` replacement (expl3-code.tex:
1252/// 36684-36695), `\CaseSwitch` (36696-36717), then the letter-like table built
1253/// from `\@uclclist` (36749-36768). l3text runs them on the output of
1254/// `\text_expand:n`, in which robust, protected and encoding commands survive
1255/// unexpanded (36274-36367) while other macros are expanded away. The changer
1256/// here expands as it reads, so, approximating the two passes, it checks the
1257/// declarations of EVERY command before expanding it. Without that,
1258/// `\MakeUppercase{\>\`α}` expanded textalpha's `\>` (equivalent
1259/// `\CaseSwitch{\>}{\LGR@hiatus}{\>}{\>}`, textalpha.sty:213-214) into
1260/// `\add@unicode@accent{"0313}{\`}`, whose accent then took `\char` as its
1261/// argument ("Missing number", `”0313` printed). Witness: greek-fontenc
1262/// char-list (lualatex).
1263///
1264/// In the sentence/title "rest of the word" state (`keep`), l3text copies
1265/// tokens verbatim (`\__text_change_case_skip:nnw`, 36718-36740), so a declared
1266/// token is passed through unexpanded rather than acted on. `name` is the
1267/// token's string without the trailing space of a robust command's inner name.
1268fn lx_case_change_cs(
1269  req_case: &str,
1270  tok: Token,
1271  name: &str,
1272  prefix: Option<Token>,
1273  keep: &mut bool,
1274  depth: usize,
1275  result: &mut Vec<Token>,
1276) -> Result<CaseChangeCs> {
1277  let titling = req_case == "sentence" || req_case == "title";
1278  let push_self = |result: &mut Vec<Token>| {
1279    if let Some(protect) = prefix {
1280      result.push(protect);
1281    }
1282    push_case_verbatim(result, tok);
1283  };
1284  if let Some(replacement) = case_change_equivalent(name)? {
1285    if *keep {
1286      push_self(result);
1287    } else if depth >= MAX_CASE_EQUIVALENT_DEPTH {
1288      Error!(
1289        "recursion",
1290        name,
1291        s!(
1292          "Case-change equivalent of {name} nests deeper than {MAX_CASE_EQUIVALENT_DEPTH} levels; it is left unchanged"
1293        )
1294      );
1295      push_self(result);
1296    } else {
1297      result.extend(lx_change_case_in_mouth(
1298        req_case,
1299        &replacement,
1300        false,
1301        keep,
1302        depth + 1,
1303      )?);
1304    }
1305    return Ok(CaseChangeCs::Done);
1306  }
1307  if prefix.is_none() && is_case_switch(&tok) {
1308    // `\CaseSwitch{<normal>}{<upper>}{<lower>}{<title>}`
1309    let args = [
1310      read_arg(ExpansionLevel::Off)?,
1311      read_arg(ExpansionLevel::Off)?,
1312      read_arg(ExpansionLevel::Off)?,
1313      read_arg(ExpansionLevel::Off)?,
1314    ];
1315    if *keep {
1316      push_case_verbatim(result, tok);
1317      for arg in args {
1318        result.push(T_BEGIN!());
1319        for t in arg.unlist() {
1320          push_case_verbatim(result, t);
1321        }
1322        result.push(T_END!());
1323      }
1324    } else {
1325      let [_, upper, lower, title] = args;
1326      let chosen = match req_case {
1327        "upper" => upper,
1328        "lower" => lower,
1329        _ => title,
1330      };
1331      for t in chosen.unlist() {
1332        push_case_verbatim(result, t);
1333      }
1334      if titling {
1335        *keep = true;
1336      }
1337    }
1338    return Ok(CaseChangeCs::Done);
1339  }
1340  let is_upper = req_case == "upper" || titling;
1341  let (map, other_map) = if is_upper {
1342    ("text_uppercase", "text_lowercase")
1343  } else {
1344    ("text_lowercase", "text_uppercase")
1345  };
1346  if let Some(mapped) = case_letterlike(map, name) {
1347    if *keep {
1348      push_self(result);
1349    } else {
1350      push_case_verbatim(result, mapped);
1351      if titling {
1352        *keep = true;
1353      }
1354    }
1355    return Ok(CaseChangeCs::Done);
1356  }
1357  // Already in the requested case: l3text still counts it as the letter that
1358  // starts a title-cased word (expl3-code.tex:36758-36766).
1359  if case_letterlike(other_map, name).is_some() {
1360    push_self(result);
1361    if titling {
1362      *keep = true;
1363    }
1364    return Ok(CaseChangeCs::Done);
1365  }
1366  Ok(CaseChangeCs::Plain)
1367}
1368
1369/// l3text's `\text_declare_expand_equivalent:Nn` replacement, stored in
1370/// `\l__text_expand_<\token_to_str:N cs>_tl` (expl3-code.tex:36395-36399) and
1371/// re-scanned by `\text_expand:n` in place of the CS (`\__text_expand_replace:N`,
1372/// 36339-36354). The kernel
1373/// declares every text accent and `\AA`…`\th` as themselves under `\exp_not:n`
1374/// (36401-36418): an accent reaches typesetting with its cased argument, as in
1375/// LaTeX (`\MakeUppercase{\'e}` typesets `\'E`), instead of being expanded
1376/// before its argument is cased.
1377fn case_expand_equivalent(name: &str) -> Result<Option<Tokens>> {
1378  Ok(
1379    match lookup_definition_stored(&T_CS!(s!("\\l__text_expand_{name}_tl")))? {
1380      Some(Stored::Expandable(tl)) => match tl.get_expansion() {
1381        Some(ExpansionBody::Tokens(replacement)) => Some(replacement.clone()),
1382        _ => None,
1383      },
1384      _ => None,
1385    },
1386  )
1387}
1388
1389/// l3text's `\__text_expand_testopt:N` (expl3-code.tex:36319-36328): when a
1390/// command's one-step expansion opens with `\@protected@testopt`, the command
1391/// is stored unexpanded and `\@protected@testopt`'s other two arguments are
1392/// dropped, so the optional argument is read where the command is typeset.
1393/// Every `\newcommand` optional-argument command expands that way
1394/// (latex.ltx:1249 `\@xargdef`); ours carry the `testopt` flag on their
1395/// optional parameter instead of the `\@protected@testopt` body. (`\@yargdef`
1396/// also flags the inner `\\cs`, a plain `[#1]` macro in latex.ltx that l3text
1397/// would expand; the loop never reaches it, as the outer command is stored
1398/// first.) Returns the tokens to store, or `None` when `tok` is no such
1399/// command. Guard: `case_change_equivalents::optional_argument_commands_stay_unexpanded`.
1400fn case_testopt_store(tok: Token) -> Result<Option<Vec<Token>>> {
1401  let protected_testopt = T_CS!("\\@protected@testopt");
1402  if has_meaning(&protected_testopt) && x_equals(&tok, &protected_testopt) {
1403    // `\@protected@testopt <cmd> <\\cmd> {<default>}` spelled out directly.
1404    let cmd = read_arg(ExpansionLevel::Off)?;
1405    read_arg(ExpansionLevel::Off)?;
1406    read_arg(ExpansionLevel::Off)?;
1407    return Ok(Some(cmd.unlist()));
1408  }
1409  let testopt = lookup_expandable(&tok, None)?.is_some_and(|defn| {
1410    defn.get_parameters().is_some_and(|params| {
1411      params
1412        .get_parameters()
1413        .first()
1414        .is_some_and(|param| param.testopt)
1415    })
1416  });
1417  Ok(testopt.then(|| vec![tok]))
1418}
1419
1420/// l3text's `\__text_expand_encoding:N` (expl3-code.tex:36330-36338), the next
1421/// check after `\__text_expand_testopt:N`: an encoding-dispatched text command
1422/// expands one step to `\<enc>-cmd <cmd> \<enc><cmd>`, the `\<enc>-cmd` being
1423/// `\@current@cmd` or `\@changed@cmd` (latex.ltx:9865/9871), and
1424/// `\__text_expand_encoding_escape:NN` keeps `<cmd>` under `\exp_not:n` and
1425/// drops `\<enc><cmd>`. Our `\DeclareTextCommand` family dispatches without
1426/// that step (sect08.rs `def_text_command_dispatcher`: `<cmd>` expands straight
1427/// to `\expandafter\ifx\csname\cf@encoding\string<cmd>\endcsname…`), so a
1428/// command that expands that way is the one the escape keeps. Expanded
1429/// instead, textalpha's `ά` (`\ensuregreek{\acctonos\textalpha}`) reached
1430/// `\greekscript`'s `\def\encodingdefault{LGR}` with `\encodingdefault`
1431/// expanded to `T1`, a definition named `T` (textalpha-doc, char-list,
1432/// hyperref-with-greek), and `\@changed@cmd` reached `\@use@text@encoding`'s
1433/// `\edef\f@encoding` (latex.ltx:9975). Returns the kept tokens, or `None`
1434/// for any other token. The escape's two arguments are undelimited
1435/// (`\__text_expand_encoding_escape:NN #1#2`); a command `\let` to a text
1436/// command keeps the command its dispatch names, as expanding it one step
1437/// and escaping would (`\let\foo\textalpha` keeps `\textalpha`).
1438/// Guards: `sweep125_roots::{case_change_keeps_a_text_command,
1439/// case_change_keeps_encoding_dispatched_command}`.
1440fn case_encoding_escape(tok: Token) -> Result<Option<Vec<Token>>> {
1441  let is_dispatch = ["\\@current@cmd", "\\@changed@cmd"]
1442    .into_iter()
1443    .any(|name| {
1444      let dispatch = T_CS!(name);
1445      has_meaning(&dispatch) && x_equals(&tok, &dispatch)
1446    });
1447  if is_dispatch {
1448    let kept = read_arg(ExpansionLevel::Off)?;
1449    read_arg(ExpansionLevel::Off)?;
1450    return Ok(Some(kept.unlist()));
1451  }
1452  Ok(text_command_dispatched_name(&tok)?.map(|name| vec![name]))
1453}
1454
1455/// The command our text-command encoding dispatch (sect08.rs
1456/// `def_text_command_dispatcher`) names, when `tok` expands to it: the body
1457/// opens with `\expandafter\ifx\csname\cf@encoding\string<cmd>`.
1458fn text_command_dispatched_name(tok: &Token) -> Result<Option<Token>> {
1459  let Some(defn) = lookup_expandable(tok, None)? else {
1460    return Ok(None);
1461  };
1462  let Some(ExpansionBody::Tokens(body)) = defn.get_expansion() else {
1463    return Ok(None);
1464  };
1465  let head = [
1466    "\\expandafter",
1467    "\\ifx",
1468    "\\csname",
1469    "\\cf@encoding",
1470    "\\string",
1471  ];
1472  let body = body.unlist_ref();
1473  let opens_dispatch = body.len() > head.len()
1474    && head
1475      .iter()
1476      .zip(body)
1477      .all(|(name, t)| t.get_catcode() == Catcode::CS && t.with_str(|s| s == *name));
1478  Ok(opens_dispatch.then(|| body[head.len()]))
1479}
1480
1481/// Whether `tok` means `\unexpanded` (`\exp_not:n`): `\text_expand:n` keeps its
1482/// argument unexpanded, the case loop still changes it
1483/// (`\__text_expand_cs_expand:N`/`\__text_expand_unexpanded:w`,
1484/// expl3-code.tex:36355-36394).
1485fn is_unexpanded(tok: &Token) -> bool {
1486  let unexpanded = T_CS!("\\unexpanded");
1487  has_meaning(&unexpanded) && x_equals(tok, &unexpanded)
1488}
1489
1490/// l3text `\__text_expand_explicit:N` (expl3-code.tex:36165-36191): an active
1491/// character is expanded unless it is protected, or its expansion starts with a
1492/// babel shorthand's `\active@prefix` or a UTF-8 octet handler; its case is then
1493/// that of the character (36622-36631), with no case-change declarations. A
1494/// babel shorthand kept whole composes as typed: babel-greek's `~` in
1495/// textalpha's `\>~` (greek-fontenc char-list-alphabeta).
1496fn active_char_kept(tok: &Token) -> Result<bool> {
1497  let Some(defn) = lookup_expandable(tok, None)? else {
1498    return Ok(false);
1499  };
1500  if defn.is_protected() {
1501    return Ok(true);
1502  }
1503  let head = match defn.get_expansion() {
1504    Some(ExpansionBody::Tokens(body)) => body.unlist_ref().first().copied(),
1505    _ => None,
1506  };
1507  Ok(head.is_some_and(|head| {
1508    [
1509      "\\UTFviii@two@octets",
1510      "\\UTFviii@three@octets",
1511      "\\UTFviii@four@octets",
1512      "\\active@prefix",
1513    ]
1514    .into_iter()
1515    .any(|marker| {
1516      let marker = T_CS!(marker);
1517      has_meaning(&marker) && x_equals(&head, &marker)
1518    })
1519  }))
1520}
1521
1522/// Bound on nested `\DeclareCaseChangeEquivalent` replacements (an equivalent
1523/// naming its own command would otherwise recurse without end; l3text loops).
1524const MAX_CASE_EQUIVALENT_DEPTH: usize = 32;
1525
1526fn lx_read_and_change_case(
1527  req_case: &str,
1528  expand: bool,
1529  keep: &mut bool,
1530  depth: usize,
1531) -> Result<Vec<Token>> {
1532  let mut result = vec![];
1533  let mut in_math = false;
1534  let is_upper = req_case == "upper" || req_case == "sentence" || req_case == "title";
1535  // `sentence`/`title` (`\text_titlecase_first:n`/`_all:n`, which
1536  // `\MakeTitlecase` is in the kernel) uppercase the first letter (of each
1537  // word, for `title`) and leave the rest as it is (l3text, TeX Live 2025:
1538  // `\text_titlecase_all:n{hELLO wORLD}` is `HELLO WORLD`). Perl lowercases the
1539  // rest (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:5507-5516 notes the ambiguity).
1540  loop {
1541    // Outside math a CS is read unexpanded first, so its case-change
1542    // declarations are seen before it is expanded (`lx_case_change_cs`), and
1543    // each expansion step is re-checked (`\__text_expand_cs_expand:N` expands
1544    // one step and re-enters its loop, expl3-code.tex:36355-36367). The read
1545    // crosses the end of an `\input` file or `\scantokens` pseudo-file into
1546    // the argument, as `read_x_token` does.
1547    let next = if in_math && expand {
1548      read_x_token(Some(false), false, None)?
1549    } else {
1550      read_token_across_input_ends()?
1551    };
1552    let mut tok = match next {
1553      None => break,
1554      Some(t) => t,
1555    };
1556    if !in_math && tok.get_catcode() == Catcode::ACTIVE {
1557      if active_char_kept(&tok)? || !expand {
1558        push_case_verbatim(&mut result, tok);
1559        continue;
1560      }
1561      if expand_once_partial(tok)? {
1562        continue;
1563      }
1564      unread_one(tok);
1565      tok = match read_x_token(Some(false), false, None)? {
1566        None => break,
1567        Some(t) => t,
1568      };
1569    } else if !in_math && tok.get_catcode() == Catcode::CS && !tok.with_str(|s| s == "\\protect") {
1570      let name = tok.with_str(|s| s.to_string());
1571      if lx_case_change_excluded(req_case, tok, &name, None, depth, &mut result)? {
1572        continue;
1573      }
1574      // `\text_expand:n` replaces or shields the token before the case loop
1575      // ever sees it (expl3-code.tex:36339-36394).
1576      if expand {
1577        if let Some(replacement) = case_expand_equivalent(&name)? {
1578          unread_expansion(replacement);
1579          continue;
1580        }
1581        if is_unexpanded(&tok) {
1582          let unexpanded = read_arg(ExpansionLevel::Off)?;
1583          result.extend(lx_change_case_in_mouth(
1584            req_case,
1585            &unexpanded,
1586            false,
1587            keep,
1588            depth + 1,
1589          )?);
1590          continue;
1591        }
1592      }
1593      match lx_case_change_cs(req_case, tok, &name, None, keep, depth, &mut result)? {
1594        CaseChangeCs::Done => continue,
1595        CaseChangeCs::Plain if !expand => {
1596          push_case_verbatim(&mut result, tok);
1597          continue;
1598        },
1599        CaseChangeCs::Plain => {
1600          if let Some(stored) = case_testopt_store(tok)? {
1601            for t in stored {
1602              push_case_verbatim(&mut result, t);
1603            }
1604            continue;
1605          }
1606          // The kept command is `\exp_not:n`'d: changed, not expanded, as
1607          // `\unexpanded` above is.
1608          if let Some(kept) = case_encoding_escape(tok)? {
1609            result.extend(lx_change_case_in_mouth(
1610              req_case,
1611              &Tokens::new(kept),
1612              false,
1613              keep,
1614              depth + 1,
1615            )?);
1616            continue;
1617          }
1618          if expand_once_partial(tok)? {
1619            continue;
1620          }
1621          // Unexpandable, undefined or `\let` to a character: the reader
1622          // Perl uses decides (an undefined CS becomes its error stub).
1623          unread_one(tok);
1624          tok = match read_x_token(Some(false), false, None)? {
1625            None => break,
1626            Some(t) => t,
1627          };
1628        },
1629      }
1630    }
1631    let cc = tok.get_catcode();
1632    if cc == Catcode::MATH {
1633      in_math = !in_math;
1634      result.push(tok);
1635    } else if in_math {
1636      // Math content is preserved verbatim (no case change). One hazard: a
1637      // robust command nested in the math — e.g. `$\MakeUppercase{C}$` — is
1638      // expanded by read_x_token above to `\protect\MakeUppercase ` (the
1639      // robust real macro). If we let the following `\MakeUppercase ` body
1640      // expand here, its OWN definition's literal `$` tokens (from
1641      // `\def\({$}\let\)\(`) get read into this loop and miscount the CC_MATH
1642      // toggle, desynchronising `in_math` and leaking math mode into the
1643      // surrounding digestion (witnessed in amsart frontmatter:
1644      // `\@add@frontmatter@now Attempt to end mode text in math`). On
1645      // `\protect` inside math, grab the following token WITHOUT expansion and
1646      // shield it with `\dont_expand` so the caller's `\edef\reserved@a{...}`
1647      // keeps it literal; it is then digested as ordinary math later. This
1648      // mirrors Perl, whose robust-command `\protect` survives the outer
1649      // `\edef` via `\noexpand`. Plain math symbols (`\alpha`, …) are not
1650      // `\protect`-prefixed, so normal math is unaffected.
1651      if cc == Catcode::CS && tok.with_str(|s| s == "\\protect") {
1652        if let Some(next) = read_token_across_input_ends()? {
1653          result.push(tok);
1654          result.push(T_CS!("\\dont_expand"));
1655          result.push(next);
1656        } else {
1657          result.push(tok);
1658        }
1659      } else if expand {
1660        result.push(tok);
1661      } else {
1662        push_case_verbatim(&mut result, tok);
1663      }
1664    } else if *keep && (cc == Catcode::LETTER || cc == Catcode::OTHER) {
1665      result.push(tok);
1666    } else if cc == Catcode::LETTER || cc == Catcode::OTHER {
1667      let new_str: String = tok.with_str(|s| {
1668        if is_upper {
1669          s.chars().flat_map(|c| c.to_uppercase()).collect()
1670        } else {
1671          s.chars().flat_map(|c| c.to_lowercase()).collect()
1672        }
1673      });
1674      let changed = tok.with_str(|s| s != new_str.as_str());
1675      // the case changes the character, not the token's out-of-band field provenance (`Token::prov`, as `\uppercase`)
1676      let new_tok = if changed {
1677        Token {
1678          prov: tok.prov,
1679          ..Token::new(new_str, cc)
1680        }
1681      } else {
1682        tok
1683      };
1684      result.push(new_tok);
1685      if req_case == "sentence" || req_case == "title" {
1686        *keep = true;
1687      }
1688    } else if cc == Catcode::SPACE {
1689      result.push(Token { prov: tok.prov, ..T_SPACE!() });
1690      if req_case == "title" {
1691        *keep = false;
1692      }
1693    } else if cc == Catcode::CS && tok.with_str(|s| s == "\\protect") {
1694      if let Some(next_tok) = read_token_across_input_ends()? {
1695        // Perl: $cs->getString (full CS name). Munged-robust CSes carry a
1696        // trailing space — canonicalise to NO trailing space for the
1697        // exclude and equivalent lookups (matches \AddToNoCaseChangeList
1698        // storage format, and l3text's `\__text_expand_protect:Nw`, which
1699        // hands the case loop the user-level `\foo` for `\protect\foo `,
1700        // expl3-code.tex:36308-36318), and to "CS + trailing space" for the
1701        // case-mapping lookup (matches `\lx@prepare@case@mapping` storage
1702        // format, which is `$lower->getString . ' '` in Perl).
1703        let next_key_bare = next_tok.with_str(|s| s.trim_end().to_string());
1704        if lx_case_change_excluded(
1705          req_case,
1706          next_tok,
1707          &next_key_bare,
1708          Some(tok),
1709          depth,
1710          &mut result,
1711        )? {
1712          continue;
1713        }
1714        let declared = lx_case_change_cs(
1715          req_case,
1716          next_tok,
1717          &next_key_bare,
1718          Some(tok),
1719          keep,
1720          depth,
1721          &mut result,
1722        )?;
1723        if let CaseChangeCs::Plain = declared {
1724          // Fall-through: not in exclude list, not in case-mapping. Pass
1725          // both `\protect` and the munged CS through, but mark the CS
1726          // un-expandable via `\dont_expand` so the OUTER `\edef`'s
1727          // `Partial` body-reader doesn't re-invoke it. Without
1728          // `\dont_expand`, the captured tokens go through `\edef` body
1729          // expansion which would re-trigger the robust macro (whose
1730          // body contains another `\edef\reserved@a{...}`), mangling
1731          // the saved tokens and dropping content during the outer
1732          // `\reserved@a` invocation. Driver: nested
1733          // `\MakeLowercase{\MakeUppercase{...}}`.
1734          result.push(tok);
1735          result.push(T_CS!("\\dont_expand"));
1736          result.push(next_tok);
1737        }
1738      }
1739    } else if expand {
1740      result.push(tok);
1741    } else {
1742      push_case_verbatim(&mut result, tok);
1743    }
1744  }
1745  Ok(result)
1746}
