3088/// The mapping from a counter to the macro (of one argument, the counter's name) a theorem numbered within it prints
3089/// in place of `\the<counter>`.
3090const THEOREM_WITHIN_DISPLAY: &str = "theorem_within_display";
3091
3092/// A class's `\@xnthm` printing a theorem numbered within `within` with `display{within}` in place of
3093/// `\the<within>`: IEEEtran.cls:5607-5627 `\@IEEEthmcounterinsection{section}`, so "Theorem 2.1" where `\thesection` is
3094/// "II" (1911.01952; ieeetran_cls.rs; OXIDIZED_DESIGN_DIVERGENCES #848). `None` removes it.
3095pub fn set_theorem_within_display(within: &str, display: Option<&str>) {
3096  assign_mapping(THEOREM_WITHIN_DISPLAY, within, display.map(String::from));
3097}
3098
3099/// A package whose own `\@xnthm` replaces the class's (amsthm, ntheorem, theorem.sty) drops every
3100/// [`set_theorem_within_display`]: its theorems print `\the<within>`.
3101pub fn clear_theorem_within_display() {
3102  for within in with_mapping_keys(THEOREM_WITHIN_DISPLAY, |keys| keys) {
3103    assign_mapping::<String>(THEOREM_WITHIN_DISPLAY, &to_string(within), None);
3104  }
3105}
3106
3107/// Set by a package whose unnumbered theorems still step their counter: ntheorem.sty:824-839 `\@othm` and :870-880
3108/// `\@thm` run `\refstepcounter{#2}` for every theorem, its `\newtheorem*` (a `nonumber` style, :720-727) only printing
3109/// no number, so `\newtheorem*{rmk}[thm]{Remark}` takes a number from `thm` (1606.01585: five references one behind).
3110/// Read where a theorem is declared ([`define_new_theorem`]). Global.
3111pub const THEOREM_UNNUMBERED_STEPS: &str = "lx@theorem@unnumbered@steps";
3112
3113pub fn define_new_theorem(
3114  flag: Option<Tokens>,
3115  thmset: Tokens,
3116  otherthmset: Option<Tokens>,
3117  typ: Option<Tokens>,
3118  within: Option<Tokens>,
3119  // Perl `\spnewtheorem` (llncs/sv) carries a per-theorem body font
3120  // (`afterDigestBegin => sub { Digest($bodyfont); }`, llncs.cls.ltxml L144):
3121  // e.g. `proof`/`case`/`example` pass `\rmfamily` = upright, overriding the
3122  // amsthm default `\thm@bodyfont` (`\itshape`). `\newtheorem`/thmtools pass
3123  // `None` (their body font comes from `\theoremstyle`).
3124  bodyfont: Option<Tokens>,
3125) -> Result<()> {
3126  let thmset_str = thmset.to_string();
3127  let classname = clean_class_name(&thmset_str);
3128  let listname = {
3129    let mut ln = s!("theorem:{thmset_str}");
3130    ln.retain(|c| !c.is_whitespace());
3131    ln = ln.replace('\'', "prime");
3132    ln = ln.replace('?', "question");
3133    ln = ln.replace('#', "hash");
3134    ln
3135  };
3136  // The shared counter is a name read through `\csname`, so a macro naming it expands to that name: latex.ltx
3137  // :17190-17195 `\@othm` tests `\@ifundefined{c@#2}` and defines `\the#1` as `\@nameuse{the#2}`. smfthm.sty:52-56
3138  // `\gdef\smf@thm{smfthm}` `\newtheorem{theo}[\smf@thm]{\theoname}` (witnesses 1711.11547, 1902.02049, 2108.12000)
3139  // and ccthm.sty's `[\cc@thmcnter]` (1507.02955) named a counter `\smf@thm`: "Counter not defined" and an undefined
3140  // `\the\smf@thm` for every theorem. Perl takes the literal string (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:2892
3141  // `ToString($otherthmset)`), KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #691. The trailing `[within]` is a counter name the same way
3142  // (latex.ltx `\@xnthm`: `\@addtoreset{#1}{#3}`, `\csname the#3\endcsname`), so it is read through `\csname` too:
3143  // digested (Perl `DigestLiteral`), `\newtheorem{x}{X}[todo_counter]` raised "Script _ can only appear in math mode"
3144  // where pdflatex is silent (1307.7314). Guards `perfect_kernel_batch67s::newtheorem_*`.
3145  let otherthmset_str = otherthmset
3146    .map(|t| ::latexml_core::gullet::expand_as_csname_text(t).map(|e| e.to_string()))
3147    .transpose()?
3148    .filter(|s| !s.is_empty());
3149  let has_type = typ.as_ref().is_some_and(|t| !t.is_empty());
3150  let is_starred = flag.is_some();
3151
3152  let within_str = within
3153    .map(|t| ::latexml_core::gullet::expand_as_csname_text(t).map(|e| e.to_string()))
3154    .transpose()?
3155    .filter(|s| !s.is_empty());
3156
3157  let counter = otherthmset_str
3158    .clone()
3159    .unwrap_or_else(|| thmset_str.clone());
3160  let counter = counter.replace(' ', ".");
3161
3162  // If counter != thmset, record mapping
3163  if counter != thmset_str {
3164    AssignMapping!("counter_for_type", &thmset_str => &counter);
3165    DefMacro!(
3166      T_CS!(s!("\\the{thmset_str}")),
3167      None,
3168      Some(ExpansionBody::Tokens(Tokens::new(vec![T_CS!(s!("\\the{counter}"))]))),
3169      scope => Some(Scope::Global)
3170    );
3171  }
3172
3173  let numbering = {
3174    let reg = LookupRegister!("\\thm@numbering");
3175    if let RegisterValue::Tokens(t) = reg {
3176      t.to_string()
3177    } else {
3178      "\\arabic".into()
3179    }
3180  };
3181
3182  let is_starred = is_starred || numbering.is_empty();
3183
3184  if otherthmset_str.is_none() {
3185    // A theorem declared with a counter of its own steps that counter, even where an earlier `\newtheorem{X}[Y]`
3186    // made X share Y's (latex.ltx `\@xnthm`: `\newcounter{X}`, `\theX` its own): the shared mapping goes, or its
3187    // numbers step Y's counter and print X's, "Proposition 1.0" (2407.21129, a paper's `\newtheorem{proposition}
3188    // {Proposition}[section]` over tac's `[theorem]` one) and "Remark 0" (1205.2947, 1307.5990: arxbj's
3189    // `\newtheorem{rem}{Remark}` over elsart_support's `[thm]` one). Guards
3190    // `perfect_kernel_batch77v::{newtheorem_over_shared_counter_theorem, elsart_support_theorem_tag_zero}`.
3191    assign_mapping::<Stored>("counter_for_type", &thmset_str, None);
3192    let idprefix = s!("Thm{}", classname.replace('*', "."));
3193    let c_counter = s!("\\c@{counter}");
3194    if !is_defined(&c_counter) {
3195      let within_ref = within_str.as_deref().unwrap_or("");
3196      NewCounter!(&counter, within_ref, idprefix => &idprefix);
3197    }
3198    // Define \the<counter>
3199    if !numbering.is_empty() {
3200      let the_counter_body = if let Some(ref w) = within_str {
3201        // A class's own `\@xnthm` may print the within-counter its own way ([`set_theorem_within_display`]).
3202        match lookup_mapping(THEOREM_WITHIN_DISPLAY, w) {
3203          Some(display) => s!("{display}{{{w}}}\\@thmcountersep{numbering}{{{counter}}}"),
3204          None => s!("\\csname the{w}\\endcsname\\@thmcountersep{numbering}{{{counter}}}"),
3205        }
3206      } else {
3207        s!("{numbering}{{{counter}}}")
3208      };
3209      DefMacro!(
3210        T_CS!(s!("\\the{counter}")),
3211        None,
3212        Some(ExpansionBody::Tokens(mouth::tokenize_internal(
3213          TeXString::assembled(the_counter_body)
3214        ))),
3215        scope => Some(Scope::Global)
3216      );
3217    }
3218  }
3219
3220  // Save current theorem style params for this theorem name
3221  let savable_keys = get_savable_keys();
3222  let mut saved_params: Vec<(String, Stored)> = Vec::new();
3223  for key in &savable_keys {
3224    if key.starts_with('\\') {
3225      let reg = LookupRegisterOrDefault!(key);
3226      let tokens = match reg {
3227        RegisterValue::Tokens(t) => t,
3228        _ => Tokens!(),
3229      };
3230      // Perl `\spnewtheorem`'s `afterDigestBegin => Digest($bodyfont)` applies
3231      // a per-theorem body font that overrides the amsthm default. Stage it
3232      // into the saved `\thm@bodyfont` so `use_theorem_style` restores it at
3233      // body-digest start (proof/case/... => `\rmfamily` = upright).
3234      let tokens = if key == "\\thm@bodyfont" {
3235        bodyfont
3236          .as_ref()
3237          .filter(|t| !t.is_empty())
3238          .cloned()
3239          .unwrap_or(tokens)
3240      } else {
3241        tokens
3242      };
3243      saved_params.push((key.clone(), Stored::Tokens(tokens)));
3244    } else {
3245      let val = lookup_value(key).unwrap_or(Stored::None);
3246      saved_params.push((key.clone(), val));
3247    }
3248  }
3249  save_theorem_style(&thmset_str, saved_params);
3250
3251  // Define \lx@name@<thmset>
3252  let thmname_cs = s!("\\lx@name@{thmset_str}");
3253  if has_type {
3254    let type_tokens = typ.clone().unwrap();
3255    DefMacro!(
3256      T_CS!(&thmname_cs),
3257      None,
3258      Some(ExpansionBody::Tokens(type_tokens)),
3259      scope => Some(Scope::Global)
3260    );
3261  } else {
3262    DefMacro!(
3263      T_CS!(&thmname_cs),
3264      None,
3265      Some(ExpansionBody::Tokens(Tokens!())),
3266      scope => Some(Scope::Global)
3267    );
3268  }
3269
3270  // Read swap value
3271  let swap = lookup_value("thm@swap")
3272    .map(|v| match v {
3273      Stored::Int(n) => n != 0,
3274      Stored::Bool(b) => b,
3275      _ => false,
3276    })
3277    .unwrap_or(false);
3278
3279  // Define \fnum@<thmset>
3280  let fnum_cs = s!("\\fnum@{thmset_str}");
3281  let fnum_tokens = if is_starred || counter.is_empty() {
3282    Tokens::new(vec![T_CS!(&thmname_cs)])
3283  } else if swap {
3284    let mut toks = vec![T_CS!(s!("\\the{counter}"))];
3285    if has_type {
3286      toks.push(T_SPACE!());
3287    }
3288    toks.push(T_CS!(&thmname_cs));
3289    Tokens::new(toks)
3290  } else {
3291    let mut toks = vec![T_CS!(&thmname_cs)];
3292    if has_type {
3293      toks.push(T_SPACE!());
3294    }
3295    toks.push(T_CS!(s!("\\the{counter}")));
3296    Tokens::new(toks)
3297  };
3298  DefMacro!(
3299    T_CS!(&fnum_cs),
3300    None,
3301    Some(ExpansionBody::Tokens(fnum_tokens)),
3302    scope => Some(Scope::Global)
3303  );
3304
3305  // Define \format@title@<thmset>
3306  let format_title_cs = s!("\\format@title@{thmset_str}");
3307  let headformatter = LookupRegisterOrDefault!("\\thm@headformatter");
3308  let headformatter_tokens = match headformatter {
3309    RegisterValue::Tokens(t) => t,
3310    _ => Tokens!(),
3311  };
3312
3313  let format_cs_token = T_CS!(&format_title_cs);
3314  if !headformatter_tokens.is_empty() {
3315    // amsthm-style head formatter
3316    let mut fmt_toks = vec![T_CS!("\\the"), T_CS!("\\thm@headfont")];
3317    fmt_toks.extend(headformatter_tokens.unlist());
3318    fmt_toks.push(T_BEGIN!());
3319    if has_type {
3320      fmt_toks.extend(typ.unwrap().unlist());
3321    }
3322    fmt_toks.push(T_END!());
3323    fmt_toks.push(T_CS!(s!("\\the{counter}")));
3324    fmt_toks.push(T_BEGIN!());
3325    fmt_toks.push(T_PARAM!());
3326    fmt_toks.push(T_OTHER!("1"));
3327    fmt_toks.push(T_END!());
3328    fmt_toks.push(T_CS!("\\the"));
3329    fmt_toks.push(T_CS!("\\thm@headpunct"));
3330
3331    let params = parse_parameters("{}", &format_cs_token, true)?;
3332    DefMacro!(
3333      format_cs_token,
3334      params,
3335      Some(ExpansionBody::Tokens(Tokens::new(fmt_toks))),
3336      scope => Some(Scope::Global)
3337    );
3338  } else {
3339    // Standard format
3340    let note_part = if has_type {
3341      "\\ifx.#1.\\else\\space\\the\\thm@notefont(#1)\\fi"
3342    } else {
3343      "#1"
3344    };
3345    let fmt_str = s!(
3346      // The `{}` after `\endcsname` is OXIDIZED_DESIGN #85 — see `\lx@fnum@@`
3347      // in `base_utilities.rs`. A theorem set's `\fnum@<set>` reaches the same
3348      // trap: an author redefinition that takes an argument (to eat LaTeX's
3349      // separator token) otherwise scans past the hook and swallows the tag
3350      // group's closing brace.
3351      "{{\\the\\thm@headfont\\lx@tag{{\\csname fnum@{thmset_str}\\endcsname{{}}}}{{{note_part}}}\\the\\thm@headpunct}}"
3352    );
3353    let params = parse_parameters("{}", &format_cs_token, true)?;
3354    DefMacro!(
3355      format_cs_token,
3356      params,
3357      Some(ExpansionBody::Tokens(mouth::tokenize_internal(
3358        TeXString::assembled(fmt_str)
3359      ))),
3360      scope => Some(Scope::Global)
3361    );
3362  }
3363
3364  // Define the environment.
3365  //
3366  // The env-trigger key MUST match what `\begin{<name>}`/`\end{<name>}`
3367  // look up, which is `ToString(Expand(<name>))` (see `\begin{}` above and
3368  // Perl LaTeX.pool L164). `\newenvironment` likewise registers under
3369  // `Expand!(name).to_string()`. But `thmset_str` (used for classname /
3370  // listname / counter / ids) is the *raw* `thmset.to_string()` — matching
3371  // Perl `defineNewTheorem` L3054 `ToString($thmset)`. These two agree for
3372  // Perl because Perl drops invalid input bytes (an undeclared Latin-1 `é`
3373  // never becomes a char, so raw == expanded == "df"). We preserve the
3374  // `é` (better output: café stays café), so for a theorem env whose name
3375  // carries an *active* accented char — e.g. `\newtheorem{déf}` in a
3376  // Latin-1 source under `[T1]{fontenc}`, where t1enc.dfu's
3377  // `\DeclareUnicodeCharacter{00E9}` makes `é` active → `\'e` →
3378  // `\lx@applyaccent…` — the raw name ("déf") and the `\begin`-expanded
3379  // name ("d\lx@applyaccent\'{e}f") diverge, and `\begin{déf}` fails to
3380  // find the env ("environment is not defined"). Expanding the trigger key
3381  // (only the key — classname/ids stay raw & clean) restores the match.
3382  // No-op for ASCII names. Witness: arXiv:1509.06785.
3383  let thmset_for_env = Expand!(thmset).to_string();
3384
3385  // Hand-written replacement closure (compile_replacement! only works with literals)
3386  let inlist_val = s!("thm {listname}");
3387  let class_val = s!("ltx_theorem_{classname}");
3388  let compiled_replacement: Option<ReplacementClosure> = Some(Rc::new(
3389    move |document: &mut Document, _args: &Vec<Option<Digested>>, props: &SymHashMap<Stored>| {
3390      let mut av_props: HashMap<String, String> = HashMap::default();
3391      if let Some(stored) = props.get("id") {
3392        av_props.insert("xml:id".into(), stored.to_string());
3393      }
3394      av_props.insert("inlist".into(), inlist_val.clone());
3395      av_props.insert("class".into(), class_val.clone());
3396      let this_font_opt = match props.get("font") {
3397        Some(Stored::Font(f)) => Some(Cow::Borrowed(&**f)),
3398        Some(Stored::FontDirective(FontDirective::Asset(fa))) => Some(Cow::Borrowed(&**fa)),
3399        Some(Stored::FontDirective(FontDirective::Closure(code))) => Some(Cow::Owned(code(None)?)),
3400        _ => None,
3401      };
3402      if let Some(this_font) = this_font_opt {
3403        document.open_element("ltx:theorem", Some(av_props), Some(&this_font))?;
3404      } else {
3405        document.open_element("ltx:theorem", Some(av_props), None)?;
3406      }
3407      // #tags
3408      if let Some(stored_digested) = props.get("tags") {
3409        let digested_opt: Option<Digested> = stored_digested.into();
3410        if let Some(ref digested) = digested_opt {
3411          document.absorb(digested, None)?;
3412        }
3413      }
3414      // <ltx:title font='#titlefont' _force_font='true'>#title</ltx:title>
3415      let mut title_av: HashMap<String, String> = HashMap::default();
3416      if let Some(stored) = props.get("titlefont") {
3417        title_av.insert("font".into(), stored.to_string());
3418      }
3419      title_av.insert("_force_font".into(), "true".into());
3420      let title_font_opt = match props.get("titlefont") {
3421        Some(Stored::Font(f)) => Some(Cow::Borrowed(&**f)),
3422        Some(Stored::FontDirective(FontDirective::Asset(fa))) => Some(Cow::Borrowed(&**fa)),
3423        Some(Stored::FontDirective(FontDirective::Closure(code))) => Some(Cow::Owned(code(None)?)),
3424        _ => None,
3425      };
3426      if let Some(title_font) = title_font_opt {
3427        document.open_element("ltx:title", Some(title_av), Some(&title_font))?;
3428      } else {
3429        document.open_element("ltx:title", Some(title_av), None)?;
3430      }
3431      if let Some(stored_digested) = props.get("title") {
3432        let digested_opt: Option<Digested> = stored_digested.into();
3433        if let Some(ref digested) = digested_opt {
3434          document.absorb(digested, None)?;
3435        }
3436      }
3437      document.close_element("ltx:title")?;
3438      // #body
3439      if let Some(stored_digested) = props.get("body") {
3440        let digested_opt: Option<Digested> = stored_digested.into();
3441        if let Some(ref digested) = digested_opt {
3442          document.absorb(digested, None)?;
3443        }
3444      }
3445      // #trailer — `set_body` (whatsit.rs) pops the LAST captured box off the
3446      // body and stashes it as the `trailer`. For a well-formed
3447      // `\begin{thm}…\end{thm}` that trailer is the content-less `\end{thm}`
3448      // whatsit (empty replacement → no-op absorb). But when a `\newtheorem`
3449      // command is used BARE in a brace group — `{\lem … }` with no `\end{lem}`
3450      // (common for inference/lemma figures) — the body capture over-captures
3451      // the *following* document content (the next `{\cor …}`, sections, …) and
3452      // it all lands in that last box, so the trailer holds real content. The
3453      // replacement absorbed only `#body`, silently dropping it (witness
3454      // 1905.00186: ~90 % of the document lost). Absorbing the trailer recovers
3455      // it (Perl keeps the content; both engines over-capture identically).
3456      if let Some(stored_digested) = props.get("trailer") {
3457        let digested_opt: Option<Digested> = stored_digested.into();
3458        if let Some(ref digested) = digested_opt {
3459          document.absorb(digested, None)?;
3460        }
3461      }
3462      Ok(())
3463    },
3464  ));
3465
3466  // `thmset_for_before` is for the before_digest closure; clone needed
3467  // because `thmset_str` is moved into `thmset_for_tags` below.
3468  let thmset_for_before = thmset_str.clone();
3469  let thmset_for_head_hooks = thmset_str.clone();
3470  let thmset_for_restate = thmset_for_env.clone();
3471  let thmset_for_foot_hooks = thmset_str.clone();
3472  // `thmset_for_tags` and `counter_for_tags` are the last uses of
3473  // thmset_str and counter — move instead of clone.
3474  let thmset_for_tags = thmset_str;
3475  let counter_for_tags = counter;
3476  let is_starred_for_props = is_starred;
3477  let unnumbered_steps = is_starred && lookup_bool(THEOREM_UNNUMBERED_STEPS);
3478  let has_type_for_props = has_type;
3479
3480  let mut options = ConstructorOptions {
3481    mode: Some("internal_vertical".into()),
3482    scope: Some(Scope::Global),
3483    ..Default::default()
3484  };
3485
3486  // before_digest
3487  let before_digest_closure: BeforeDigestClosure = Rc::new(move || {
3488    use_theorem_style(&thmset_for_before);
3489    // A theorem is a `\trivlist` (latex.ltx `\@begintheorem`, amsthm.sty's): it runs `\@trivlist`'s additions.
3490    run_trivlist_hook()?;
3491    let digested = digest(mouth::tokenize_internal("\\normalfont\\the\\thm@prework"))?;
3492    Ok(vec![digested])
3493  });
3494  options.before_digest.push(before_digest_closure);
3495
3496  // after_digest_begin
3497  let after_digest_begin_closure: DigestionClosure = Rc::new(move |whatsit| {
3498    let name_opt = whatsit.get_arg(1);
3499    let name_str = name_opt
3500      .map(|n| n.revert().map(|t| t.to_string()).unwrap_or_default())
3501      .unwrap_or_default();
3502    let mut digest_str =
3503      s!("\\the\\thm@bodyfont\\the\\thm@styling\\def\\lx@thistheorem{{{name_str}}}");
3504    // thm-patch.sty:33-62 runs a theorem's `\thmt@<env>@preheadhook`, `\thmt@generic@preheadhook` before its head
3505    // and `\thmt@<env>@postheadhook`, `\thmt@generic@postheadhook` after it, inside the theorem: the hooks thmtools'
3506    // `\addtotheorem…hook[<env>]` gathers (thmtools_sty.rs, the only binding that defines them).
3507    digest_str.push_str(&theorem_hooks(&[
3508      (&thmset_for_head_hooks, "preheadhook"),
3509      ("generic", "preheadhook"),
3510      (&thmset_for_head_hooks, "postheadhook"),
3511      ("generic", "postheadhook"),
3512    ]));
3513    let mut digested = vec![digest(mouth::tokenize_internal(TeXString::assembled(
3514      digest_str,
3515    )))?];
3516    // …and thm-kv's local post-head hook, last (thm-patch.sty:60 `\thmt@local@postheadhook`): the `label=` key's
3517    // `\label` (thm-kv.sty:485-487, `thmtools_use_keys`)
3518    if let Some(Stored::Tokens(label)) = lookup_value("thmt_local_label") {
3519      assign_value("thmt_local_label", Stored::None, None);
3520      digested.push(digest(Invocation!(T_CS!("\\label"), vec![label]))?);
3521    }
3522    // …and thm-restate's `restate=<name>` (thm-restate.sty:198-215, the same hook): the theorem is stored for
3523    // `\<name>` as `{restatable}` stores it (thm_restate_sty.rs `\lx@thm@restate@store`, with the theorem's other
3524    // keys for the restated copy). The store reads the body that follows, so it is read from the input, not digested
3525    // here.
3526    if let Some(Stored::Tokens(name)) = lookup_value("thmt_local_restate") {
3527      assign_value("thmt_local_restate", Stored::None, None);
3528      let keys = match lookup_value("thmt_local_restate_keys") {
3529        Some(Stored::Tokens(keys)) => keys,
3530        _ => Tokens!(),
3531      };
3532      let env = Tokens::new(Explode!(&thmset_for_restate));
3533      unread(Invocation!(T_CS!("\\lx@thm@restate@store"), vec![
3534        env.clone(),
3535        env,
3536        name,
3537        keys
3538      ]));
3539    }
3540    Ok(digested)
3541  });
3542  options.after_digest_begin.push(after_digest_begin_closure);
3543
3544  // before_digest_end. A theorem ended by a plain group closer (`{\Proof …}`)
3545  // never reaches its `\endX` in TeX, so neither the end mark (ntheorem's
3546  // `[thmmarks]` symbol) nor the postwork is set (stomach.rs
3547  // `close_environment_frame`).
3548  let before_digest_end_closure: BeforeDigestClosure = Rc::new(move || {
3549    if environment_ended_by_group() {
3550      return Ok(Vec::new());
3551    }
3552    // thm-patch.sty:130-142: the foot hooks, here before the theorem's end code (ditto).
3553    let foot_hooks = theorem_hooks(&[
3554      ("generic", "prefoothook"),
3555      (&thmset_for_foot_hooks, "prefoothook"),
3556      ("generic", "postfoothook"),
3557      (&thmset_for_foot_hooks, "postfoothook"),
3558    ]);
3559    let digested = digest(mouth::tokenize_internal(TeXString::assembled(s!(
3560      "{foot_hooks}\\thm@doendmark\\the\\thm@postwork"
3561    ))))?;
3562    Ok(vec![digested])
3563  });
3564  options.before_digest_end.push(before_digest_end_closure);
3565
3566  // after_construct
3567  let after_construct_closure: ConstructionClosure =
3568    Rc::new(move |document: &mut Document, _whatsit: &Whatsit| {
3569      document.maybe_close_element("ltx:theorem")?;
3570      Ok(())
3571    });
3572  options.after_construct.push(after_construct_closure);
3573
3574  // properties — capture thmset_for_tags / counter_for_tags by move.
3575  let props_closure: PropertiesClosure = Rc::new(
3576    #[allow(clippy::ptr_arg)]
3577    move |args: &Vec<Option<Digested>>| {
3578      let mut props = SymHashMap::default();
3579      // thm-kv's key=value optional argument (`thmtools_use_keys`), when thmtools is loaded
3580      let thmuse = match args.first() {
3581        Some(Some(arg)) if lookup_bool("thmtools_thmuse_keys") => thmtools_use_keys(&arg.revert()?),
3582        _ => None,
3583      };
3584      if let Some(label) = thmuse.as_ref().and_then(|u| u.label.clone()) {
3585        assign_value("thmt_local_label", Stored::Tokens(label), None);
3586      }
3587      if let Some(name) = thmuse.as_ref().and_then(|u| u.restate.clone())
3588        && has_meaning(&T_CS!("\\lx@thm@restate@store"))
3589      {
3590        assign_value("thmt_local_restate", Stored::Tokens(name), None);
3591        let keys = thmuse
3592          .as_ref()
3593          .map(|u| u.restate_keys.clone())
3594          .unwrap_or_default();
3595        assign_value(
3596          "thmt_local_restate_keys",
3597          Stored::Tokens(Tokens::new(keys)),
3598          None,
3599        );
3600      }
3601      // A starred restatement (thm_restate_sty.rs `\lx@thm@restate*`) is numbered as the theorem it restates
3602      // (thm-restate.sty:130-140: `\the<env>` faked from the stored number, the counter not stepped), as
3603      // `continues=` below numbers a theorem as the one it continues
3604      let restated = match lookup_value("thmt_restate_number") {
3605        Some(Stored::Tokens(number)) => {
3606          assign_value("thmt_restate_number", Stored::None, None);
3607          Some(number)
3608        },
3609        _ => None,
3610      };
3611      // `continues=<label>` (thm-kv.sty:511-516 `\thmt@suspendcounter`): the theorem is numbered as the one it
3612      // continues — its number, in its tags and its title, is a reference to that label — and its counter does not
3613      // step
3614      let continued = thmuse
3615        .as_ref()
3616        .and_then(|u| u.continues.as_ref())
3617        .map(|continued| {
3618          let mut number = vec![T_CS!("\\ref"), T_BEGIN!()];
3619          number.extend(continued.unlist_ref().iter().copied());
3620          number.push(T_END!());
3621          number
3622        });
3623      let suspended: Vec<Token> = match restated.map(|number| number.unlist()).or(continued) {
3624        Some(number) if !is_starred_for_props && !counter_for_tags.is_empty() => {
3625          let mut toks = Vec::new();
3626          for name in [&counter_for_tags, &thmset_for_tags] {
3627            toks.extend([T_CS!("\\def"), T_CS!(s!("\\the{}", name)), T_BEGIN!()]);
3628            toks.extend(number.iter().copied());
3629            toks.push(T_END!());
3630          }
3631          toks
3632        },
3633        _ => Vec::new(),
3634      };
3635
3636      if !counter_for_tags.is_empty() {
3637        if !suspended.is_empty() {
3638          let ctr_props = ref_step_id(&counter_for_tags)?;
3639          for (k, v) in ctr_props.iter() {
3640            props.insert_sym(*k, v.clone());
3641          }
3642          let mut toks = vec![T_BEGIN!()];
3643          toks.extend(suspended.iter().copied());
3644          toks.extend([T_CS!("\\lx@make@tags"), T_BEGIN!()]);
3645          toks.extend(
3646            mouth::tokenize_internal(TeXString::assembled(thmset_for_tags.clone())).unlist(),
3647          );
3648          toks.extend([T_END!(), T_END!()]);
3649          props.insert("tags", digest(Tokens::new(toks))?.into());
3650        } else if is_starred_for_props {
3651          if unnumbered_steps {
3652            step_counter(&counter_for_tags, false)?;
3653          }
3654          let ctr_props = ref_step_id(&counter_for_tags)?;
3655          for (k, v) in ctr_props.iter() {
3656            props.insert_sym(*k, v.clone());
3657          }
3658          // For starred theorems with a type, create tags without the counter number
3659          if has_type_for_props {
3660            let tag_tokens = Tokens::new(vec![
3661              T_BEGIN!(),
3662              T_CS!("\\let"),
3663              T_CS!(s!("\\the{}", counter_for_tags)),
3664              T_CS!("\\@empty"),
3665              T_CS!("\\lx@make@tags"),
3666              T_BEGIN!(),
3667            ]);
3668            let mut full_toks = tag_tokens.unlist();
3669            full_toks.extend(
3670              mouth::tokenize_internal(TeXString::assembled(thmset_for_tags.clone())).unlist(),
3671            );
3672            full_toks.push(T_END!());
3673            full_toks.push(T_END!());
3674            let tags = digest(Tokens::new(full_toks))?;
3675            props.insert("tags", tags.into());
3676          }
3677        } else {
3678          let ctr_props = ref_step_counter_by_meaning(&thmset_for_tags)?;
3679          for (k, v) in ctr_props.iter() {
3680            props.insert_sym(*k, v.clone());
3681          }
3682        }
3683      }
3684
3685      // Compute title
3686      let format_title_cs = s!("\\format@title@{}", thmset_for_tags);
3687      let mut title_tokens = vec![T_BEGIN!()];
3688      title_tokens.extend(suspended);
3689      title_tokens.extend([
3690        T_CS!("\\the"),
3691        T_CS!("\\thm@headstyling"),
3692        T_CS!(&format_title_cs),
3693        T_BEGIN!(),
3694      ]);
3695      if let Some(thmuse) = thmuse {
3696        title_tokens.extend(thmuse.note);
3697      } else if let Some(Some(arg)) = args.first() {
3698        title_tokens.extend(arg.revert()?.unlist());
3699      }
3700      title_tokens.push(T_END!());
3701      title_tokens.push(T_END!());
3702
3703      let title = digest_text(Tokens::new(title_tokens))?;
3704      let titlefont = title.get_font()?.map(|f| (*f).clone());
3705      props.insert("title", title.into());
3706      if let Some(f) = titlefont {
3707        props.insert("titlefont", Stored::Font(Rc::new(f)));
3708      }
3709
3710      Ok(props)
3711    },
3712  );
3713  options.properties = props_closure;
3714
3715  // Use the OptionalUndigested parameter
3716  let env_cs = T_CS!(s!("\\begin{{{thmset_for_env}}}"));
3717  let paramlist = parse_parameters("OptionalUndigested", &env_cs, true)?;
3718  def_environment(thmset_for_env, paramlist, compiled_replacement, options);
3719
3720  Ok(())
3721}
3722
3723/// What thm-kv makes of a theorem's optional argument written as keys (thm-kv.sty:434-437 adds `\thmt@garbleoptarg` to
3724/// every theorem's pre-head hook, :439-463): its note, the label it sets, the theorem it continues.
3725struct ThmUse {
3726  /// The note in place of the argument (`\thmt@newoptarg`, expanded): empty when only `label=` is given.
3727  note:         Vec<Token>,
3728  /// `label=<name>` (:485-487): a `\label` after the head (`\thmt@local@postheadhook`).
3729  label:        Option<Tokens>,
3730  /// `continues=<label>` (:511-516): the theorem continued, whose number this one takes.
3731  continues:    Option<Tokens>,
3732  /// thm-restate's `restate=[<keys>]<name>` (thm-restate.sty:198-215): the name the theorem is stored under for a
3733  /// later `\<name>`; the bracketed keys apply to the restated copy only.
3734  restate:      Option<Tokens>,
3735  /// The keys the restated copy is begun with (thm-restate.sty:217-229 `restate phase 2`): the theorem's other keys,
3736  /// then the bracketed ones.
3737  restate_keys: Vec<Token>,
3738}
3739
3740/// thm-kv's `\thmt@garbleoptarg` (thm-kv.sty:439-463) over the keys it defines: `label` (:485-487), `name` (:488-496,
3741/// `[short]long`, the long form the note) and `continues` (:511-516, "<name>, \thmcontinues{<label>}" or, alone,
3742/// "\thmcontinues{<label>}" — the `\@gobble` the note starts with eats its `{, }`), processed in order as `\kvsetkeys`
3743/// does. An argument none of whose keys is one of these is no key list (`\ifthmt@thmuse@iskv`), kept as written: a
3744/// note "Smith, 2001" is a note. Written as keys, a `_` in a label was a math error and "(label=ex:a_b)" its title (run
3745/// 336 first error `unexpected:_`, ~150 papers: 2002.09876, 2409.14881). thm-restate adds `restate=` (thm-restate.sty
3746/// :193-215, its "restate phase" families): the theorem stored for a later `\<name>`, its note none (2108.11527,
3747/// 2602.09462: "(restate=…)" was the title and `\<name>` undefined).
3748fn thmtools_use_keys(arg: &Tokens) -> Option<ThmUse> {
3749  let tokens = arg.unlist_ref();
3750  // the top-level `key=value` items, spaces trimmed, one brace level off a value (keyval's)
3751  let mut items: Vec<(String, Vec<Token>)> = Vec::new();
3752  let mut depth = 0i32;
3753  let mut start = 0;
3754  let mut push_item = |item: &[Token]| {
3755    let mut level = 0i32;
3756    let equals = item.iter().position(|t| {
3757      match t.get_catcode() {
3758        Catcode::BEGIN => level += 1,
3759        Catcode::END => level -= 1,
3760        _ => {},
3761      }
3762      level == 0 && t.get_catcode() == Catcode::OTHER && t.to_string() == "="
3763    });
3764    if let Some(equals) = equals {
3765      let key: String = item[..equals].iter().map(|t| t.to_string()).collect();
3766      let value = trim_spaces(&item[equals + 1..]);
3767      let value = match (value.first(), value.last()) {
3768        (Some(first), Some(last))
3769          if value.len() >= 2
3770            && first.get_catcode() == Catcode::BEGIN
3771            && last.get_catcode() == Catcode::END
3772            && balanced_group(&value) =>
3773        {
3774          value[1..value.len() - 1].to_vec()
3775        },
3776        _ => value,
3777      };
3778      items.push((key.trim().to_string(), value));
3779    }
3780  };
3781  for (i, token) in tokens.iter().enumerate() {
3782    match token.get_catcode() {
3783      Catcode::BEGIN => depth += 1,
3784      Catcode::END => depth -= 1,
3785      Catcode::OTHER if depth == 0 && token.to_string() == "," => {
3786        push_item(&tokens[start..i]);
3787        start = i + 1;
3788      },
3789      _ => {},
3790    }
3791  }
3792  push_item(&tokens[start..]);
3793  let mut iskv = false;
3794  // `\thmt@newoptarg`, `\@gobble` until a `name=` replaces it
3795  let mut gobbled = true;
3796  let mut note: Vec<Token> = Vec::new();
3797  let mut label = None;
3798  let mut continues = None;
3799  let mut restate = None;
3800  let mut restate_keys: Vec<Token> = Vec::new();
3801  let mut restate_extra: Vec<Token> = Vec::new();
3802  for (key, value) in items {
3803    if key != "restate" {
3804      if !restate_keys.is_empty() {
3805        restate_keys.push(T_OTHER!(","));
3806      }
3807      restate_keys.extend(Explode!(&key));
3808      restate_keys.extend([T_OTHER!("="), T_BEGIN!()]);
3809      restate_keys.extend(value.iter().copied());
3810      restate_keys.push(T_END!());
3811    }
3812    match key.as_str() {
3813      "label" => {
3814        iskv = true;
3815        label = Some(Tokens::new(value));
3816      },
3817      "name" => {
3818        iskv = true;
3819        // `name=[short]long`: the long form
3820        let long = match value.first() {
3821          Some(t) if t.get_catcode() == Catcode::OTHER && t.to_string() == "[" => {
3822            match value
3823              .iter()
3824              .position(|t| t.get_catcode() == Catcode::OTHER && t.to_string() == "]")
3825            {
3826              Some(close) => value[close + 1..].to_vec(),
3827              None => value,
3828            }
3829          },
3830          _ => value,
3831        };
3832        gobbled = false;
3833        note = long;
3834      },
3835      "continues" => {
3836        iskv = true;
3837        if !gobbled {
3838          note.extend([T_OTHER!(","), T_SPACE!()]);
3839        }
3840        gobbled = false;
3841        note.push(T_CS!("\\thmcontinues"));
3842        note.push(T_BEGIN!());
3843        note.extend(value.iter().copied());
3844        note.push(T_END!());
3845        continues = Some(Tokens::new(value));
3846      },
3847      "restate" => {
3848        iskv = true;
3849        // `\thmt@splitrestateargs`: `[<keys>]<name>`, the keys for the restated copy only; its `\@ifnextchar[` skips the
3850        // spaces before the bracket or the name (2602.09462 writes the value over several lines), a space after the
3851        // name is part of it
3852        let start = value
3853          .iter()
3854          .position(|t| t.get_catcode() != Catcode::SPACE)
3855          .unwrap_or(value.len());
3856        let value = value[start..].to_vec();
3857        let name = match value.first() {
3858          Some(t) if t.get_catcode() == Catcode::OTHER && t.to_string() == "[" => {
3859            // the `]` outside braces (`name={[x]}` keeps its own)
3860            let mut level = 0i32;
3861            let close = value.iter().position(|t| {
3862              match t.get_catcode() {
3863                Catcode::BEGIN => level += 1,
3864                Catcode::END => level -= 1,
3865                _ => {},
3866              }
3867              level == 0 && t.get_catcode() == Catcode::OTHER && t.to_string() == "]"
3868            });
3869            match close {
3870              Some(close) => {
3871                restate_extra = value[1..close].to_vec();
3872                value[close + 1..].to_vec()
3873              },
3874              None => value,
3875            }
3876          },
3877          _ => value,
3878        };
3879        if !name.is_empty() {
3880          restate = Some(Tokens::new(name));
3881        }
3882      },
3883      _ => {},
3884    }
3885  }
3886  if !restate_extra.is_empty() {
3887    if !restate_keys.is_empty() {
3888      restate_keys.push(T_OTHER!(","));
3889    }
3890    restate_keys.extend(restate_extra);
3891  }
3892  iskv.then_some(ThmUse {
3893    note,
3894    label,
3895    continues,
3896    restate,
3897    restate_keys,
3898  })
3899}
3900
3901/// `tokens` without its leading and trailing spaces.
3902fn trim_spaces(tokens: &[Token]) -> Vec<Token> {
3903  let start = tokens
3904    .iter()
3905    .position(|t| t.get_catcode() != Catcode::SPACE)
3906    .unwrap_or(tokens.len());
3907  let end = tokens
3908    .iter()
3909    .rposition(|t| t.get_catcode() != Catcode::SPACE)
3910    .map_or(start, |i| i + 1);
3911  tokens[start..end].to_vec()
3912}
3913
3914/// Whether `tokens`, which open with `{` and end with `}`, are one group (`{a}{b}` is two).
3915fn balanced_group(tokens: &[Token]) -> bool {
3916  let mut depth = 0i32;
3917  for (i, t) in tokens.iter().enumerate() {
3918    match t.get_catcode() {
3919      Catcode::BEGIN => depth += 1,
3920      Catcode::END => {
3921        depth -= 1;
3922        if depth == 0 && i + 1 < tokens.len() {
3923          return false;
3924        }
3925      },
3926      _ => {},
3927    }
3928  }
3929  true
3930}
3931
3932/// A float's counter steps — at `\caption` (`\@@add@caption@counters`) or at a sub-float's
3933/// pre-increment. A continued float keeps its number instead: caption's `\continuedfloat` sets its
3934/// "continued" flag (`\caption@setcontinued`, caption.sty:192), under which the float's next step
3935/// is `\caption@@refcounter` (:557-568, chosen by `\caption@ifrefstepcounter`, :580) — here the
3936/// counter steps back and refsteps without resetting its sub-counters, once. The pending
3937/// continuation is one global value, the continued type (`lx@float@continued`), as caption's flags
3938/// are one global counter (:173-192). A real step of the current float's own counter
3939/// (`lx@float@main`, see `begin_float_continuation`), or of any float counter when no float type is
3940/// current, first runs caption's hook (as `prepare_float_step` does); the counter of a float caption never types
3941/// (`before_untyped_float`: a sub-float, a listing) steps plainly.
3942/// Witness 2605.17685; repro captions-floats/continuedfloat_keeps_the_number_and_the_letters.
3943pub fn step_float_counter(counter: &str) -> Result<SymHashMap<Stored>> {
3944  // Through `\refstepcounter`'s current meaning (`ref_step_counter_planned`): a measuring pass's
3945  // local rebinding (floatrow) leaves the counter, the continuation and caption's hook as they were;
3946  // a wrapper (hyperref, cleveref) reaches the kernel step, which carries them out (witnesses
3947  // kaytannollista-latexia, 2605.17685).
3948  if lookup_string("lx@float@untyped") == counter {
3949    return ref_step_counter_by_meaning(counter);
3950  }
3951  let continued = lookup_string("lx@float@continued") == counter;
3952  let main = lookup_string("lx@float@main");
3953  let hook = T_CS!("\\lx@float@stepped");
3954  let before = if !continued && (main.is_empty() || main == counter) && has_meaning(&hook) {
3955    let mut tokens = vec![hook, T_BEGIN!()];
3956    tokens.extend(Explode!(counter));
3957    tokens.push(T_END!());
3958    tokens
3959  } else {
3960    Vec::new()
3961  };
3962  ref_step_counter_planned(counter, before, continued)
3963}
3964
3965/// caption's `\caption@prepare@stepcounter` (caption.sty:577-579): before a float's real step, the
3966/// `\lx@float@stepped{<counter>}` hook runs when a package defines it (caption's
3967/// `\caption@reset@continuedfloat`, :501-503: the type a `\ContinuedFloat` may continue, and its
3968/// count restarted). A sub-caption's step never prepares (caption's `\caption@subtypehook` points
3969/// its `\caption@refstepcounter` at plain `\refstepcounter`, caption.sty:662, :668).
3970pub fn prepare_float_step(counter: &str) -> Result<()> {
3971  let hook = T_CS!("\\lx@float@stepped");
3972  if has_meaning(&hook) {
3973    let mut tokens = vec![hook, T_BEGIN!()];
3974    tokens.extend(Explode!(counter));
3975    tokens.push(T_END!());
3976    digest(Tokens::new(tokens))?;
3977  }
3978  Ok(())
3979}
3980
3981/// caption's `\caption@settype` (caption.sty:300-303): the float of this type begins, which
3982/// records it as the current float's type (`lx@float@main`, local — the counter whose real steps
3983/// `step_float_counter` prepares; an enclosing untyped float's mark, `lx@float@untyped`, is reset)
3984/// and clears any pending continuation (`\caption@clrflags`, :302, global). caption runs it at every float's begin built by `\@xfloat` (`\caption@xfloat`,
3985/// :271-275; `before_float_ex`), at `\captionof` (`\caption@of` → `\setcaptiontype*`, :389-391,
3986/// :288-297), at `\captionsetup{type=…}` (:283) and at a longtable's caption (`\caption@LT@settype`,
3987/// :1167); not for a float it never types (`before_untyped_float`). Guards
3988/// `perfect_kernel_batch56::{continuedfloat_counts_only_the_main_floats_steps,
3989/// continuedfloat_scope_opens_where_caption_sets_the_type}`.
3990pub fn begin_float_continuation(float_type: &str) {
3991  assign_value("lx@float@main", float_type.to_string(), Some(Scope::Local));
3992  assign_value("lx@float@untyped", String::new(), Some(Scope::Local));
3993  assign_value("lx@float@continued", String::new(), Some(Scope::Global));
3994}
3995
3996/// `before_float` for a float caption never types: subfig's, subfigure.sty's and subfloat.sty's
3997/// sub-floats and containers (their own packages step them), and listings' floats — no
3998/// `\caption@settype`, so a pending continuation survives it, and its own counter's steps neither
3999/// prepare nor take the continuation (`step_float_counter`). Guard
4000/// `perfect_kernel_batch56::continuedfloat_scope_opens_where_caption_sets_the_type`.
4001pub fn before_untyped_float(float_type: &str) -> Result<()> {
4002  assign_value(
4003    "lx@float@untyped",
4004    float_type.to_string(),
4005    Some(Scope::Local),
4006  );
4007  begin_float(float_type, None, false, false)
4008}
4009
4010/// latex.ltx `\@floatboxreset` (`\reset@font\normalsize`, run by `\@xfloat`): a floating
4011/// environment's text starts in the body font, size and leading whatever surrounds it — through
4012/// `\lx@floatbox@reset`, which setspace makes single-spaced (setspace.sty:418-422), so a document's
4013/// `\doublespacing` no longer stretches its tables (2605.18633 S6.T1). Called by the environments
4014/// that model `\@xfloat` (figure/table, `\@float`, float.sty, rotating, acmart, jhep, aas plates,
4015/// wrapstuff) — not by sub-floats, wrapfig/floatflt, an algorithm2e placed `[H]` (a minipage),
4016/// supertabular (`\lx@float@keepsize`) or listings, which reset nothing in LaTeX. A class with no
4017/// `\normalsize` (amsppt) has none to run. Guards `perfect_kernel_batch58::{line_spacing_commands_set_the_stretch,
4018/// only_floats_reset_the_size}`.
4019pub fn reset_float_box() -> Result<()> {
4020  // A binding that opens `{table}`/`{figure}` for an environment LaTeX does not float (supertabular)
4021  // asks for no reset with `\lx@float@keepsize`, consumed by the next float begin.
4022  if lookup_bool("lx@float@keepsize") {
4023    assign_value("lx@float@keepsize", false, Some(Scope::Global));
4024    return Ok(());
4025  }
4026  // (`\\@xfloat`'s `\\@parboxrestore` before it, latex.ltx:17482: a float's paragraphs do not run the enclosing `\\everypar`)
4027  digest(TokenizeInternal!(r"\everypar{}"))?;
4028  if !x_equals(&T_CS!("\\normalsize"), &T_CS!("\\lx@kernel@normalsize")) {
4029    digest(Tokens!(T_CS!("\\lx@floatbox@reset")))?;
4030  }
4031  Ok(())
4032}
4033
4034/// The width registers a minipage of width `width` sets (latex.ltx:16312-16313 `\@iiiminipage`: `\hsize#4`,
4035/// `\textwidth\hsize \columnwidth\hsize`, then `\@parboxrestore`'s `\linewidth\hsize`), in the current group: the
4036/// `{minipage}` environment and the sub-float environments subcaption makes of one (subcaption.sty:70-92
4037/// `\subcaption@iiminipage`). Perl's `{minipage}` assigns the first three (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:4785-4787;
4038/// `\linewidth` OXIDIZED_DESIGN tcolorbox note, witness 2605.02240) and its sub-floats only `beforeFloat`'s `\hsize`
4039/// (:3377), so a `width=\linewidth` image in a `{subfigure}{.28\textwidth}` took the page's width (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS
4040/// #1028; witness 2509.19464 A1.F6). Guard `perfect_kernel_batch78d::subfigure_sets_the_line_width`.
4041pub fn set_minipage_width(width: Dimension) -> Result<()> {
4042  // The page outside the outermost such box (`PANEL_BOX_PAGE`), which a float held in it is a fraction of.
4043  if lookup_value(PANEL_BOX_PAGE).is_none() {
4044    let register = |name: &str| Stored::Dimension(lookup_dimension(name).unwrap_or_default());
4045    assign_value(
4046      PANEL_BOX_PAGE,
4047      Stored::VecDequeStored(VecDeque::from([
4048        register("\\textwidth"),
4049        register("\\columnwidth"),
4050      ])),
4051      Some(Scope::Local),
4052    );
4053  }
4054  let rv: RegisterValue = width.into();
4055  for register in ["\\hsize", "\\textwidth", "\\columnwidth", "\\linewidth"] {
4056    assign_register(register, rv.clone(), None, Vec::new())?;
4057  }
4058  Ok(())
4059}
4060
4061/// The state value that makes the next `{minipage}` a varwidth box (varwidth.sty's `\varwidth`, which runs
4062/// `\@vwid@setup` as the minipage's `\@minipagerestore`): set by the binding, taken by the minipage it begins.
4063pub const MINIPAGE_NATURAL_WIDTH: &str = "minipage:natural_width";
4064
4065/// varwidth.sty's `\endvarwidth`: the box is as wide as its widest line (`\@vwid@measure`, each line's natural
4066/// width), or the width it was given where that is less (`\ifdim\@vwid@<\hsize \hsize\@vwid@`). Algxpar's
4067/// `\axp@SetToWidth` measures with a 500cm one (algxpar-doc, 2401.12710).
4068pub fn minipage_takes_natural_width(whatsit: &mut Whatsit) -> Result<()> {
4069  let (Some(Stored::Digested(body)), Some(Stored::Dimension(given))) = (
4070    whatsit.get_property("body").map(|b| b.into_owned()),
4071    whatsit.get_property("width").map(|w| w.into_owned()),
4072  ) else {
4073    return Ok(());
4074  };
4075  let mut options = SymHashMap::default();
4076  options.insert("natural_width", Stored::Bool(true));
4077  let (natural, ..) = body.compute_size(options)?;
4078  let width = natural.value_of().clamp(0, given.value_of().max(0));
4079  // Narrower than given, the box's HTML follows its content (the minipage's `declared_width` style).
4080  if width < given.value_of() {
4081    whatsit.set_property("declared_width", Stored::Dimension(given));
4082  }
4083  whatsit.set_property("width", Stored::Dimension(Dimension::new(width)));
4084  Ok(())
4085}
4086
4087/// Perl: beforeFloat (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml L3430-3438)
4088/// Sets \@captype, adjusts \hsize for single/double column floats.
4089/// `preincrement`: if Some("figure"), pre-increments the parent float counter
4090///   on first subfloat entry (before main caption), storing result for later use.
4091pub fn before_float(float_type: &str, preincrement: Option<&str>) -> Result<()> {
4092  before_float_ex(float_type, preincrement, false)
4093}
4094/// Extended version with `double` flag for `*` variants (span both columns).
4095pub fn before_float_ex(float_type: &str, preincrement: Option<&str>, double: bool) -> Result<()> {
4096  begin_float(float_type, preincrement, double, true)
4097}
4098fn begin_float(
4099  float_type: &str,
4100  preincrement: Option<&str>,
4101  double: bool,
4102  typed: bool,
4103) -> Result<()> {
4104  set_aside_pending_caption(float_type);
4105  // The boxes open in this float (`begin_caption_box`) end before it does; `after_float` unwinds any whose end an
4106  // error recovery skipped.
4107  assign_value(
4108    BOX_DEPTH_AT_FLOAT,
4109    Stored::Number(Number(caption_box_depth() as i64)),
4110    Some(Scope::Local),
4111  );
4112  def_macro(
4113    T_CS!("\\@captype"),
4114    None,
4115    Tokens::new(ExplodeText!(float_type)),
4116    None,
4117  )
4118  .ok();
4119  // Scoped to the float's group: a `\caption` digested with `\@captype` set but
4120  // without this marker is outside any float (sect09.rs `\lx@@caption`).
4121  let in_float = lookup_bool("lx@in@float");
4122  assign_value("lx@in@float", true, Some(Scope::Local));
4123  // The float's own frame: latex.ltx's `\@endfloatbox` closes a float box only when a raw
4124  // opener made one on top of it (sect09.rs).
4125  assign_value(
4126    "lx@float@frame",
4127    Stored::Number(Number(current_frame_id() as i64)),
4128    Some(Scope::Local),
4129  );
4130  // Every float and sub-float is its own caption's target: a capture an enclosing float set up
4131  // (floatrow's `\@floatcapt`) does not take it, as caption.sty resets `\caption@setfloatcapt`
4132  // for sub-types (:648, in `\caption@subtypehook`, :639-664). Guard `perfect_kernel_batch58::floatrow_subcaption_stays_in_its_panel`.
4133  Let!("\\lx@setfloatcapt", "\\lx@kernel@setfloatcapt");
4134  // Perl #2775: rebind \\ to \lx@newline in floats to prevent
4135  // alignment-token early-return when floats are inside tabulars.
4136  Let!("\\\\", "\\lx@newline");
4137  // Between a float's panels (the panel grid rule), while each has the kernel's meaning — an author's or a package's
4138  // own stands (review rev78x finding 11): a forced `\linebreak` ends their row as `\\` does (`\lx@panel@linebreak`,
4139  // sect09.rs); a `\vspace` does not (`\lx@panel@vspace`, sect12.rs), a `\vskip` does; the glue an `\hspace` states
4140  // counts towards their row (`\lx@panel@hspace`, sect12.rs).
4141  for (name, kernel, panel) in [
4142    (
4143      "\\linebreak",
4144      "\\lx@kernel@linebreak",
4145      "\\lx@panel@linebreak",
4146    ),
4147    ("\\vspace", "\\lx@kernel@vspace", "\\lx@panel@vspace"),
4148    ("\\hspace", "\\lx@kernel@hspace", "\\lx@panel@hspace"),
4149  ] {
4150    if x_equals(&T_CS!(name), &T_CS!(kernel)) {
4151      let_definition(&T_CS!(name), &T_CS!(panel), None);
4152    }
4153  }
4154  // Perl: AssignRegister('\hsize' => LookupDimension($options{double} ? '\textwidth' :
4155  // '\columnwidth'));
4156  let dim_name = if double {
4157    "\\textwidth"
4158  } else {
4159    "\\columnwidth"
4160  };
4161  let dim_val = lookup_dimension(dim_name).unwrap_or_default();
4162  assign_register("\\hsize", dim_val.into(), None, Vec::new()).ok();
4163  // The real line the float's panels are set in rows against (`install_panel_line`), in a float not inside another.
4164  if !in_float {
4165    install_panel_line(double);
4166  } else {
4167    note_panel_hbox();
4168  }
4169  // Perl: if (my $main = $options{preincrement}) {
4170  //   if (($type ne (LookupValue('LAST_FLOATTYPE') || ''))
4171  //     && !IfCondition('\iflx@donecaption')) {
4172  //     AssignValue('PREINCREMENTED_' . $main => { RefStepCounter($main) }, 'global'); } }
4173  // A typed float's begin is caption's `\caption@settype` (`begin_float_continuation`) — except the
4174  // float `\@captionof@` wraps a caption in (`lx@float@captionof`, one-shot: `\captionof` has set
4175  // the type, a typed `\caption` sets none) and a pre-incrementing sub-float environment, whose own
4176  // counter steps plainly (caption's sub-captions, caption.sty:662, :668).
4177  if lookup_bool("lx@float@captionof") {
4178    assign_value("lx@float@captionof", false, Some(Scope::Global));
4179  } else if preincrement.is_some() {
4180    assign_value(
4181      "lx@float@untyped",
4182      float_type.to_string(),
4183      Some(Scope::Local),
4184    );
4185  } else if typed {
4186    begin_float_continuation(float_type);
4187  }
4188  if let Some(main_counter) = preincrement {
4189    preincrement_float_counter(float_type, main_counter);
4190  }
4191  Ok(())
4192}
4193/// The state value (and the whatsit property `after_float` copies it to) of the real line a float's panels are set in
4194/// rows against, and the frame of the float that installed it.
4195const PANEL_LINE: &str = "panel_line_width";
4196const PANEL_LINE_FRAME: &str = "lx@panel@line@frame";
4197/// The whatsit property of the line a float with no real line (`PANEL_LINE`) is arranged at under geometry
4198/// (`after_float`): `\Gm@tw`, as before the panel grid rule.
4199const PANEL_FALLBACK_LINE: &str = "panel_fallback_line";
4200/// The state value (and the whatsit property `after_float` copies it to) of the real running-text column at the float
4201/// (`install_panel_line`: the class's real column in two columns, its text width in one) that the float's line is a
4202/// fraction of (`panelline`, `annotate_panel_grid`).
4203const PANEL_COLUMN: &str = "panel_column_width";
4204/// The state value of the float's `\hsize` as `install_panel_line` found it: one its binding sets afterwards (a
4205/// wrapfigure's width, wrapfig_sty.rs) is the float's own line, which the class's page does not replace
4206/// (`after_float`; 2609.34643 S3.SS3.fig1, a 0.27\textwidth wrapfigure).
4207const PANEL_LINE_HSIZE: &str = "lx@panel@line@hsize";
4208/// The state value of the geometry a float's stated widths are evaluated at (`install_panel_line`): the registers' own
4209/// values and the real ones, `\textwidth`, `\columnwidth`, the line (`\linewidth`, `\hsize`), in scaled points.
4210const PANEL_GEOMETRY: &str = "lx@panel@geometry";
4211/// The whatsit property of a float whose panels' widths are the real ones though it has no real line of its own
4212/// (`after_float`): the registers are the real geometry where it is set.
4213const PANEL_REGISTERS_REAL: &str = "panel_registers_real";
4214/// The whatsit property a panel's box carries once its stated width is evaluated (`note_stated_widths`): what the
4215/// real geometry adds to it (scaled points, a `Dimension`), for `arrange_panels` alone.
4216const PANEL_WIDTH_DELTA: &str = "panel_width_delta";
4217/// The whatsit property of an `\hspace` between a float's panels (`\lx@panel@hskip`): what the real geometry adds to
4218/// its natural width.
4219pub(crate) const PANEL_GLUE_DELTA: &str = "panel_glue_delta";
4220
4221/// The kernel's `\textwidth` (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:1038 `DefRegister('\textwidth' => Dimension('345pt'))`).
4222const KERNEL_TEXTWIDTH: i64 = 345 * 65536;
4223
4224/// A class binding's declaration of the page its panels are set in rows against (`declare_panel_page`): the column
4225/// and text widths of the class's real page and the binding's own `\textwidth` (scaled points), and whether the page is
4226/// set in two columns now.
4227const PANEL_PAGE: &str = "lx@panel@page";
4228const PANEL_PAGE_TWOCOLUMN: &str = "lx@panel@page@twocolumn";
4229/// The state value of the page outside the outermost box that set the width registers (`set_minipage_width`: a
4230/// `{minipage}`), its `\textwidth` and `\columnwidth` (scaled points), for a float held in it (`install_panel_line`).
4231const PANEL_BOX_PAGE: &str = "lx@panel@box@page";
4232
4233/// The panel grid rule's line (user ruling 2026-10-22, FIDELITY_CHARTER §2 "Float panels"): a float's panels are set in
4234/// rows against the class's real line (`panel_page`: a class binding's declared page, else the registers' and the
4235/// geometry's) — in two columns a `figure` against the column, a `figure*` (`double`) against the text width. The
4236/// registers keep Perl's values (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:321 `\columnwidth` = `\textwidth`), so where the real
4237/// line differs the float keeps the widths its body states as tokens (`KEEP_STATED_LENGTHS`) and evaluates them once
4238/// more at the real geometry as its element opens (`note_stated_widths`), for `arrange_panels` alone. Witnesses 1707.00190
4239/// Fig 2, nucl-ex0511052 Fig 13, 2502.05562 Fig 6, astro-ph0205132 (`0.74\columnwidth` pairs in a two-column
4240/// `figure*`, one row in the PDF); 1508.01788 Figs 19-22, 1411.5428 Figs 6-7, 2111.05508 (the geometry's width).
4241/// OXIDIZED_DESIGN_DIVERGENCES #885.
4242fn install_panel_line(double: bool) {
4243  let register = |name: &str| lookup_dimension(name).map(|d| d.value_of());
4244  let (Some(textwidth), Some(columnwidth), Some(hsize)) = (
4245    register("\\textwidth"),
4246    register("\\columnwidth"),
4247    register("\\hsize"),
4248  ) else {
4249    return;
4250  };
4251  let linewidth = register("\\linewidth").unwrap_or(hsize);
4252  // A float held in a box that set the width registers (a `{minipage}`, latex.ltx `\@iiiminipage`: `\textwidth`,
4253  // `\columnwidth` and `\hsize` are its width) is set against that box's line, a fraction of the running-text column
4254  // outside it (`PANEL_BOX_PAGE`): a `[H]` figure in a `{minipage}{0.5\textwidth}` states `panelline` 0.5 as the PDF
4255  // gives it (review rev79c2 finding 2; the box's `\textwidth` read as the page stated 1). Only where the registers
4256  // outside the box are the real page are the box's registers real; elsewhere its real width is not known, and the
4257  // float is arranged at its `\hsize`, as before the rule, stating no line (never a guess).
4258  let box_page = match lookup_value(PANEL_BOX_PAGE) {
4259    Some(Stored::VecDequeStored(page)) => match (page.front(), page.get(1)) {
4260      (Some(Stored::Dimension(text)), Some(Stored::Dimension(column))) => {
4261        Some((text.value_of(), column.value_of()))
4262      },
4263      _ => None,
4264    },
4265    _ => None,
4266  };
4267  let (real_text, real_column, real_line, page_column) = match box_page {
4268    Some((outer_text, outer_column)) => {
4269      let (page_text, page_column) = panel_page(outer_text);
4270      if page_text != outer_text || page_column != outer_column {
4271        return;
4272      }
4273      (textwidth, columnwidth, hsize, page_column)
4274    },
4275    None => {
4276      let (real_text, real_column) = panel_page(textwidth);
4277      let real_line = if double { real_text } else { real_column };
4278      (real_text, real_column, real_line, real_column)
4279    },
4280  };
4281  assign_value(
4282    PANEL_COLUMN,
4283    Stored::Dimension(Dimension::new(page_column)),
4284    Some(Scope::Local),
4285  );
4286  assign_value(
4287    PANEL_LINE,
4288    Stored::Dimension(Dimension::new(real_line)),
4289    Some(Scope::Local),
4290  );
4291  assign_value(
4292    PANEL_LINE_FRAME,
4293    Stored::Number(Number(current_frame_id() as i64)),
4294    Some(Scope::Local),
4295  );
4296  assign_value(
4297    PANEL_LINE_HSIZE,
4298    Stored::Dimension(Dimension::new(hsize)),
4299    Some(Scope::Local),
4300  );
4301  // Where every register is already the real one, the stated widths add nothing.
4302  if [
4303    (textwidth, real_text),
4304    (columnwidth, real_column),
4305    (linewidth, real_line),
4306    (hsize, real_line),
4307  ]
4308  .iter()
4309  .all(|(ours, real)| ours == real)
4310  {
4311    return;
4312  }
4313  let geometry = [
4314    textwidth,
4315    columnwidth,
4316    linewidth,
4317    hsize,
4318    real_text,
4319    real_column,
4320    real_line,
4321  ];
4322  assign_value(
4323    PANEL_GEOMETRY,
4324    Stored::VecDequeStored(
4325      geometry
4326        .iter()
4327        .map(|v| Stored::Dimension(Dimension::new(*v)))
4328        .collect(),
4329    ),
4330    Some(Scope::Local),
4331  );
4332  assign_value(KEEP_STATED_LENGTHS, true, Some(Scope::Local));
4333}
4334
4335/// The state values (and whatsit properties, `after_float`) of a sub-float set in a TeX `\hbox` (the panel grid rule):
4336/// its body is one (`PANEL_HBOX_BODY`: subfigure.sty's `\subfigure`, whose body `\@subfloat` sets in an `\hbox`,
4337/// subfigure.sty:232), or it is begun in one, with the group of that box it is begun in (`PANEL_HBOX_ROW`: the
4338/// sub-figures of an adjustbox, one `\hbox` in TeX, 2311.18531 A7.F5/F6). TeX breaks no line inside an `\hbox`, so
4339/// `arrange_panels` keeps such panels on one row however wide they add up, as a binding's fixed row (`_gridrow`);
4340/// overfull, they are TeX's overfull box (cond-mat0610021 Fig 11: two `width=200pt` graphics in one sub-figure).
4341const PANEL_HBOX_BODY: &str = "panel_hbox_body";
4342const PANEL_HBOX_ROW: &str = "panel_hbox_row";
4343
4344/// A sub-float's `\hbox` (`PANEL_HBOX_BODY`, `PANEL_HBOX_ROW`), as it begins: its own mode (its environment's) and the
4345/// mode of the group it is begun in. The box is the group that set that mode, not the group the sub-float is begun
4346/// in: subcaption's `\subfloat` begins its sub-figure in a `\begingroup` of its own (subcaption_sty.rs
4347/// `subfloat_tokens`), so four `\subfloat`s in an `adjustbox` or a `\resizebox`, one `\hbox` in TeX, were four
4348/// groups and four rows (review rev78x2 finding 3; 2311.18531 A7.F5/F6 the environment form).
4349fn note_panel_hbox() {
4350  let modes = value_history("MODE", 2);
4351  let horizontal_box = |mode: Option<&String>| mode.is_some_and(|m| m == "restricted_horizontal");
4352  assign_value(
4353    PANEL_HBOX_BODY,
4354    horizontal_box(modes.first()),
4355    Some(Scope::Local),
4356  );
4357  if horizontal_box(modes.get(1))
4358    && let Some(frame) = frame_of_binding("MODE", 1)
4359    && let Some(group) = value_in_frame("lx@frame@id", frame)
4360  {
4361    assign_value(
4362      PANEL_HBOX_ROW,
4363      Stored::String(pin(group.to_string())),
4364      Some(Scope::Local),
4365    );
4366  } else {
4367    assign_value(PANEL_HBOX_ROW, Stored::None, Some(Scope::Local));
4368  }
4369}
4370
4371/// The class's real text and column widths for panel rows (scaled points). The text width is `\textwidth`, or the
4372/// geometry's `\Gm@tw` where it computed one and `\textwidth` is still the class's (`\Gm@doctw`), or a class binding's
4373/// declared page (`declare_panel_page`) while `\textwidth` is still the binding's (an author's `\textwidth 7.2in` is
4374/// the page: 2211.03584). In two columns — the declared page's setting, else `\if@twocolumn` — the column is the
4375/// declared one on the declared page, else `(text − \columnsep)/2` as latex.ltx's `\twocolumn` sets `\columnwidth`, the
4376/// declared page's separation between its columns where it has one. A two-column binding that keeps the kernel's 345pt
4377/// line and declares no page states no page of its own: that line is the column, the text width two of them and the
4378/// column separation (1705.10798's 4cm pairs in a REVTeX column, one row in the PDF).
4379fn panel_page(textwidth: i64) -> (i64, i64) {
4380  let register = |name: &str| lookup_dimension(name).map(|d| d.value_of());
4381  let declared = match lookup_value(PANEL_PAGE) {
4382    Some(Stored::VecDequeStored(page)) => {
4383      match (page.front(), page.get(1), page.get(2), page.get(3)) {
4384        (
4385          Some(Stored::Dimension(column)),
4386          Some(Stored::Dimension(text)),
4387          Some(Stored::Dimension(own)),
4388          Some(Stored::Dimension(own_columnsep)),
4389        ) => Some((
4390          column.value_of(),
4391          text.value_of(),
4392          own.value_of(),
4393          own_columnsep.value_of(),
4394        )),
4395        _ => None,
4396      }
4397    },
4398    _ => None,
4399  };
4400  let mut real_text = textwidth;
4401  let geometry = match (register("\\Gm@tw"), register("\\Gm@doctw")) {
4402    (Some(gm), Some(doc)) if gm > 0 && gm != doc && textwidth == doc => Some(gm),
4403    _ => None,
4404  };
4405  if let Some(gm) = geometry {
4406    real_text = gm;
4407  } else if let Some((_, text, own, _)) = declared
4408    && textwidth == own
4409  {
4410    real_text = text;
4411  }
4412  let two_column = match declared {
4413    Some(_) => lookup_bool(PANEL_PAGE_TWOCOLUMN),
4414    None => if_condition(&T_CS!("\\if@twocolumn")).ok().flatten() == Some(true),
4415  };
4416  // (the declared page's separation while `\columnsep` is still the binding's: a style that sets its own page, as
4417  // 2008.06630's 3dv.sty over `[twocolumn]{article}`, `\textwidth 6.875in` 0.3125in apart, sets its separation)
4418  let columnsep_register = register("\\columnsep").unwrap_or(0);
4419  let columnsep = match declared {
4420    Some((column, text, _, own_columnsep)) if columnsep_register == own_columnsep => {
4421      text - 2 * column
4422    },
4423    _ => columnsep_register,
4424  };
4425  if !two_column {
4426    (real_text, real_text)
4427  } else if let Some((column, text, ..)) = declared
4428    && real_text == text
4429  {
4430    (text, column)
4431  } else if declared.is_none() && real_text == KERNEL_TEXTWIDTH {
4432    (2 * real_text + columnsep, real_text)
4433  } else {
4434    (real_text, (real_text - columnsep) / 2)
4435  }
4436}
4437
4438/// A class binding declares its real page for panel rows (§3 of the panel grid rule, OXIDIZED_DESIGN_DIVERGENCES
4439/// #885): the column and text widths of the class's page in points (`column_pt`, `text_pt`, as pdflatex's
4440/// `\the\columnwidth`/`\the\textwidth` in a two-column float give them for the options given), and whether the page
4441/// is set in two columns now (`twocolumn`; `set_panel_page_twocolumn` follows a one-column region). The registers keep
4442/// the binding's values; only the rows are set against this page. Without a declaration the rows follow the registers
4443/// (`panel_page`).
4444pub fn declare_panel_page(column_pt: f64, text_pt: f64, twocolumn: bool) {
4445  let sp = |pt: f64| Stored::Dimension(Dimension::new((pt * 65536.0).round() as i64));
4446  // (and the binding's own `\textwidth`, while which the page is the declared one, and `\columnsep`, while which its
4447  // columns are the declared ones apart: `panel_page`)
4448  let own = lookup_dimension("\\textwidth").unwrap_or_default();
4449  let own_columnsep = lookup_dimension("\\columnsep").unwrap_or_default();
4450  assign_value(
4451    PANEL_PAGE,
4452    Stored::VecDequeStored(VecDeque::from([
4453      sp(column_pt),
4454      sp(text_pt),
4455      Stored::Dimension(own),
4456      Stored::Dimension(own_columnsep),
4457    ])),
4458    Some(Scope::Global),
4459  );
4460  assign_value(PANEL_PAGE_TWOCOLUMN_CLASS, twocolumn, Some(Scope::Global));
4461  set_panel_page_twocolumn(twocolumn);
4462}
4463
4464/// A class binding that loaded another's declaration (`declare_panel_page`; AASTeX over REVTeX's) whose page it does
4465/// not know withdraws it: its rows follow the registers.
4466pub fn withdraw_panel_page() { assign_value(PANEL_PAGE, Stored::None, Some(Scope::Global)); }
4467
4468/// The two-column page of LaTeX's standard classes (`declare_panel_page`), as `size10.clo`/`size11.clo`/`size12.clo`
4469/// (and `bk1x.clo`) set it for the options `class` was given (`standard_class_options`): in two columns `\textwidth`
4470/// is the paper's width less 2in, at most twice the size's one-column 345/360/390pt, `\@settopoint`ed; `\columnwidth`
4471/// is half of it less the classes' 10pt `\columnsep` (article.cls:627, latex.ltx `\twocolumn`). The paper is the last
4472/// declared of the classes' paper options (article.cls:53-77, `landscape` swapping its sides), the size the last of
4473/// `10pt`/`11pt`/`12pt` (`\ProcessOptions` runs them in their declaration order); under 2.09 compatibility
4474/// (`\documentstyle`) the size files set 410pt (size10.clo `\if@compatibility\if@twocolumn\setlength\textwidth{410\p@}`).
4475/// Returns (column, text) in points; pdflatex gives 229.5/469pt on letter paper, 221/452pt on A4, 200/410pt for
4476/// `\documentstyle`.
4477pub fn standard_class_twocolumn_page(class: &str) -> (f64, f64) {
4478  if lookup_bool("2.09_COMPATIBILITY") {
4479    return (200.0, 410.0);
4480  }
4481  let (paper_width, one_column) = standard_class_size_file(class);
4482  let text = (paper_width - 144.54_f64).min(2.0 * one_column).floor();
4483  ((text - 10.0) / 2.0, text)
4484}

4486/// The options a standard class was given: latex.ltx's `\ProcessOptions` in a class reads its `\opt@<class>.cls`
4487/// alone (`\@process@ptions`, no `\@classoptionslist`), which is the document's options when it is the document's class
4488/// and what a class passes it otherwise (`\PassOptionsToClass`, `\LoadClass[…]`: elsarticle.cls:113, llncs.cls:47);
4489/// here the State list `pass_options_with_raw` keeps with it.
4490fn standard_class_options(class: &str) -> Vec<String> {
4491  lookup_vecdeque(&s!("opt@{class}.cls"))
4492    .unwrap_or_default()
4493    .iter()
4494    .flat_map(|item| match item {
4495      Stored::String(o) => vec![with(*o, |o| o.to_string())],
4496      Stored::Strings(os) => os.iter().map(|o| with(*o, |o| o.to_string())).collect(),
4497      _ => Vec::new(),
4498    })
4499    .collect()
4500}
4501
4502/// The size file's facts the standard classes' `\textwidth` is computed from: the paper's width (the last declared of
4503/// the paper options, article.cls:53-77, `landscape` swapping its sides) and the size's one-column width (size10.clo,
4504/// size11.clo, size12.clo and bk1x.clo `\@tempdimb`: 345/360/390pt for the last of `10pt`/`11pt`/`12pt`), in points;
4505/// under 2.09 compatibility bk1x.clo:105's one column is 4.5in/5in/5in instead (`declare_standard_class_page`).
4506fn standard_class_size_file(class: &str) -> (f64, f64) {
4507  let given = standard_class_options(class);
4508  let (width, height) = match last_declared_option(&given, &[
4509    "a4paper",
4510    "a5paper",
4511    "b5paper",
4512    "letterpaper",
4513    "legalpaper",
4514    "executivepaper",
4515  ]) {
4516    Some("a4paper") => (597.50787, 845.04684),
4517    Some("a5paper") => (421.10078, 597.50787),
4518    Some("b5paper") => (500.76849, 711.31892),
4519    Some("legalpaper") => (614.295, 1011.78),
4520    Some("executivepaper") => (523.9575, 758.835),
4521    _ => (614.295, 794.97),
4522  };
4523  let width = if given.iter().any(|o| o == "landscape") {
4524    height
4525  } else {
4526    width
4527  };
4528  (
4529    width,
4530    standard_class_one_column(standard_class_ptsize(class)),
4531  )
4532}
4533
4534/// The standard classes' `\@ptsize` (article.cls:45-49 `\DeclareOption{11pt}{\renewcommand\@ptsize{1}}`): 0, 1 or 2
4535/// for the last declared of `10pt`/`11pt`/`12pt` among the options `class` was given (`standard_class_options`; a raw
4536/// class's bare `\LoadClass{article}` gives it none).
4537pub fn standard_class_ptsize(class: &str) -> u8 {
4538  match last_declared_option(&standard_class_options(class), &["10pt", "11pt", "12pt"]) {
4539    Some("11pt") => 1,
4540    Some("12pt") => 2,
4541    _ => 0,
4542  }
4543}
4544
4545fn standard_class_one_column(ptsize: u8) -> f64 {
4546  match ptsize {
4547    1 => 360.0,
4548    2 => 390.0,
4549    _ => 345.0,
4550  }
4551}
4552
4553/// A standard class (article, report, book) given `twocolumn` (the last declared of `onecolumn`/`twocolumn`) that is
4554/// the document's (`is_document_class`) declares its page in two columns (`standard_class_twocolumn_page`): its
4555/// `figure` is set against the 229.5pt column, its `figure*` against the 469pt text on letter paper, where the
4556/// registers' 345pt read as the column and twice it as the text (`panel_page`; rev79c2: `figure*` `panelline` 2 for
4557/// the PDF's 2.044). A class loading it (OmniBus, elsarticle, REVTeX) declares its own page. In one column it sets
4558/// `\textwidth` from the options it was given, a loading class's own setting after it standing (llncs.cls:55).
4559pub fn declare_standard_class_page(class: &str) -> Result<()> {
4560  if last_declared_option(&standard_class_options(class), &["onecolumn", "twocolumn"])
4561    == Some("twocolumn")
4562  {
4563    if is_document_class(class) {
4564      let (column, text) = standard_class_twocolumn_page(class);
4565      declare_panel_page(column, text, true);
4566    }
4567  } else {
4568    // size1x.clo:101-126 in one column: the paper's width less 2in, at most the size's width, `\@settopoint`ed (issue
4569    // #779: 12pt's 390pt, where the kernel's register is 10pt's 345pt). Under 2.09 compatibility size1x.clo's
4570    // 345/360/390pt and bk1x.clo:105's 4.5in/5in/5in, unrounded (pdflatex 325.215pt, 361.34999pt).
4571    let (paper_width, one_column) = standard_class_size_file(class);
4572    let sp = match (
4573      lookup_bool("2.09_COMPATIBILITY"),
4574      class,
4575      standard_class_ptsize(class),
4576    ) {
4577      (true, "book", 0) => 21_313_290,
4578      (true, "book", _) => 23_681_433,
4579      (true, ..) => (one_column * 65536.0) as i64,
4580      (false, ..) => ((paper_width - 144.54_f64).min(one_column).floor() * 65536.0) as i64,
4581    };
4582    assign_register("\\textwidth", Dimension::new(sp).into(), None, Vec::new())?;
4583  }
4584  Ok(())
4585}

4587/// The state value of a class whose floats are centred (`declare_panel_floats_centred`).

4590/// A class binding declares that its floats are centred, every `\\` in them `\@centercr` (REVTeX's `\@xfloat@prep`,

4598/// A class binding that loaded REVTeX's (`declare_panel_floats_centred`) whose floats are not centred withdraws the

4607/// The document's class options, as given (`\@classoptionslist`), for a binding's `declare_panel_page`.
4608pub fn given_class_options() -> Vec<String> {
4609  let given = match lookup_definition(&T_CS!("\\@classoptionslist")) {
4610    Ok(Some(defn)) => match defn.get_expansion() {
4611      Some(ExpansionBody::Tokens(body)) => body.to_string(),
4612      _ => String::new(),
4613    },
4614    _ => String::new(),
4615  };
4616  given.split(',').map(|o| o.trim().to_string()).collect()
4617}

4619/// Which of `options` the document's class options give last (`\@classoptionslist`, a later option overriding an
4620/// earlier one), for a binding's `declare_panel_page`.
4621pub fn last_class_option<'a>(options: &[&'a str]) -> Option<&'a str> {
4622  given_class_options()
4623    .iter()
4624    .rev()
4625    .find_map(|g| options.iter().find(|o| **o == g).copied())
4626}
4627
4628/// Which of `options` (in the order the class declares them) the document's class options give, the last declared:
4629/// the one that stands where `\ProcessOptions` runs the options in their declaration order (latex.ltx's
4630/// `\ProcessOptions`, as IEEEtran.cls's :376), for a binding's `declare_panel_page`.
4631pub fn last_declared_class_option<'a>(options: &[&'a str]) -> Option<&'a str> {
4632  last_declared_option(&given_class_options(), options)
4633}
4634
4635/// Which of `options` (in their declaration order) `given` holds, the last declared.
4636fn last_declared_option<'a>(given: &[String], options: &[&'a str]) -> Option<&'a str> {
4637  options
4638    .iter()
4639    .rev()
4640    .find(|o| given.iter().any(|g| g == **o))
4641    .copied()
4642}

4645/// one-column region: REVTeX's and AASTeX's `\onecolumngrid`/`\twocolumngrid`).
4646pub fn set_panel_page_twocolumn(twocolumn: bool) {
4647  assign_value(PANEL_PAGE_TWOCOLUMN, twocolumn, Some(Scope::Global));

4650/// The declared page's own column setting (`declare_panel_page`), which a region's end restores (REVTeX's

4658/// The state value naming where a construct's stated width is (`declare_panel_width`), by the construct's control
4659/// sequence.
4660fn panel_width_key(cs: &str) -> String { s!("lx@panel@width@{cs}") }
4661
4662/// A binding declares where a construct states its width (the panel grid rule, `note_stated_widths`): its argument
4663/// `arg` (1-based: `{minipage}{0.48\textwidth}`'s 4, `\resizebox`'s first), or, with `keys`, the last of those keys
4664/// given in its `KeyVals` argument `arg` (`\includegraphics[width=0.48\linewidth]`), and with `height_keys` the keys
4665/// whose value scales its natural width when it states none of `keys` (an aspect-keeping graphic's `height`). `cs` is
4666/// the construct's control sequence as its whatsit names it (`\begin{minipage}` for an environment).
4667pub fn declare_panel_width(cs: &str, arg: usize, keys: &[&str], height_keys: &[&str]) {
4668  let spec = if keys.is_empty() {
4669    arg.to_string()
4670  } else {
4671    s!("{arg}:{}|{}", keys.join(","), height_keys.join(","))
4672  };
4673  assign_value(
4674    &panel_width_key(cs),
4675    Stored::String(pin(&spec)),
4676    Some(Scope::Global),
4677  );
4678}
