5986
5987/// The state value counting the `{center}`-like environments whose bodies are being built (`aligning_environment`): a
5988/// row separator in their capture is the float's (`note_panel_separator`). In the document's state, so it ends with it.
5989const ALIGNING_CAPTURES: &str = "lx@aligning@captures";
5990
5991/// Build an aligning environment's body (`build`), its capture's row separators the float's (`note_panel_separator`).
5992pub fn in_aligning_capture<T>(build: impl FnOnce() -> T) -> T {
5993  let depth = aligning_captures();
5994  assign_value(
5995    ALIGNING_CAPTURES,
5996    Stored::Int(depth + 1),
5997    Some(Scope::Global),
5998  );
5999  let result = build();
6000  assign_value(ALIGNING_CAPTURES, Stored::Int(depth), Some(Scope::Global));
6001  result
6002}
6003
6004fn aligning_captures() -> i64 {
6005  match lookup_value(ALIGNING_CAPTURES) {
6006    Some(Stored::Int(n)) => n,
6007    _ => 0,
6008  }
6009}
6010
6011/// The internal attribute of a row separator the source states between a float's panels (`note_panel_separator`):
6012/// `par` (a blank line or `\par`), `env` (a `{center}`/`{flushleft}`/`{flushright}` boundary), `vskip`, `cr` (a `\\`
6013/// in such an environment: `\@centercr`, which ends the paragraph), `break` (a `\linebreak`, which ends a line of it),
6014/// `glue` (`\hskip`, `\hspace`, `\quad`; its natural width in `PANEL_GLUE`; `glue*` an `\hspace*`'s, which a line break
6015/// keeps).
6016/// `arrange_panels` turns a break between two panels into the row's `ltx:break` and drops the rest.
6017pub(crate) const PANEL_SEPARATOR: &str = "_panelsep";
6018const PANEL_GLUE: &str = "_panelglue";
6019
6020/// A row separator `note_panel_separator` recorded: a mark for the float's `arrange_panels`, not content.
6021pub(crate) fn is_panel_separator(node: &Node) -> bool {
6022  node.get_attribute(PANEL_SEPARATOR).is_some()
6023}
6024
6025/// The internal attribute of a `\newline`'s break (sect01.rs): `\@normalcr`, the justified break in every context
6026/// (latex.ltx:9256 `\DeclareRobustCommand\newline{\@normalcr\relax}`), where a `\\` under `\centering` or in a
6027/// `{center}` is `\@centercr`. `arrange_panels` reads it as a line's end, not a paragraph's.
6028const PANEL_NORMALCR: &str = "_normalcr";
6029
6030/// Record a row separator the source states at the current insertion point, when that is a float's own panel list
6031/// (the float, or the capture of a `{center}`-like environment directly in it) — the panel grid rule (user ruling
6032/// 2026-10-22, FIDELITY_CHARTER §2 "Float panels"): an explicit break always breaks, and the glue the source states
6033/// between two panels counts towards their row's width (plain spaces and `\hfill` count 0). Our panels are digested
6034/// in vertical mode, where TeX's are in a paragraph (subfigure.sty's `\@subfloat`, graphicx's `\leavevmode`), so a
6035/// `\par` or the glue between them leaves nothing in the tree to set the rows by. A `\par` that leaving horizontal
6036/// mode inserts is not the source's (2605.00347: one per inter-panel `\hfill` broke a 4-panel row into four).
6037/// Witnesses 1110.0084 Figs 12-16, 27, 29 (a blank line between sub-figures), 0706.4410 Figs 3, 5 (`\hspace{1in}`
6038/// between two 0.45\textwidth panels: two rows in the PDF). OXIDIZED_DESIGN_DIVERGENCES #885.
6039pub fn note_panel_separator(document: &mut Document, kind: &str, glue: Option<i64>) -> Result<()> {
6040  let Some(context) = document.get_element() else {
6041    return Ok(());
6042  };
6043  // The float's own list, or the capture of a `{center}`-like environment directly in it (its lines are the float's
6044  // rows; `aligning_environment`), never a box's: a separator in a minipage's capture changed how the capture settles.
6045  let qname = document::get_node_qname(&context);
6046  let at_float = with(qname, |q| PANEL_FLOATS.contains(&q))
6047    || (aligning_captures() > 0
6048      && document::is_capture_block(&context)
6049      && context.get_parent().is_some_and(|parent| {
6050        with(document::get_node_qname(&parent), |q| {
6051          PANEL_FLOATS.contains(&q)
6052        })
6053      }));
6054  if !at_float {
6055    return Ok(());
6056  }
6057  let mut attributes = map!(PANEL_SEPARATOR => kind.to_string());
6058  if let Some(width) = glue {
6059    attributes.insert(PANEL_GLUE.to_string(), width.to_string());
6060  }
6061  document.insert_element("ltx:break", Vec::new(), Some(attributes))?;
6062  Ok(())
6063}
6064
6065/// A paragraph of nothing but float-boxes (57g; user rulings 2026-09-27): boxes that became floats
6066/// (`absorb_figure_material`, base_utilities.rs) sit in the paragraph they start as inline blocks;
6067/// a paragraph holding only them — besides `\\` breaks and whitespace — is a line of nothing but
6068/// those boxes, so it gives way to them ([`settle_float_paragraphs`], once the document is built).
6069/// One box becomes its float, the box's class and sizes folded onto it as Perl's single-node fold
6070/// does (`<figure
6071/// class="ltx_minipage">`); several become a row: an uncaptioned `ltx:figure` holding them as
6072/// panels, with the author's breaks, laid out by `arrange_panels` (the row's `after_close`) — the
6073/// markup LaTeXML gives a figure float holding captioned minipages. A paragraph holding anything
6074/// else (text, a box that is not a float, arXiv 2605.18920's algorithm box beside a table box)
6075/// keeps its boxes inline, side by side. Only a paragraph of one `ltx:p`, in a context that holds
6076/// floats and is not a float's own panel list.
6077pub(crate) fn settle_float_paragraph(document: &mut Document, para: &Node) -> Result<()> {
6078  let Some(parent) = para.get_parent() else {
6079    return Ok(());
6080  };
6081  if parent.get_type() != Some(NodeType::ElementNode) {
6082    return Ok(());
6083  }
6084  // A streaming segment's parse wrapper stands for the segment's real parent.
6085  let parent_qname = match document::get_node_qname(&parent) {
6086    wrapper if with(wrapper, |q| q == "ltx:_lxfragment") => match document.fragment_parent_qname {
6087      Some(real) => real,
6088      None => return Ok(()),
6089    },
6090    qname => qname,
6091  };
6092  if with(parent_qname, |q| PANEL_FLOATS.contains(&q)) {
6093    return Ok(());
6094  }
6095  let whitespace = |n: &Node| n.get_content().trim().is_empty();
6096  let mut paragraph = None;
6097  for child in para.get_child_nodes() {
6098    match child.get_type() {
6099      Some(NodeType::TextNode) if whitespace(&child) => {},
6100      Some(NodeType::ElementNode)
6101        if paragraph.is_none() && with(document::get_node_qname(&child), |q| q == "ltx:p") =>
6102      {
6103        paragraph = Some(child)
6104      },
6105      Some(NodeType::ElementNode) | Some(NodeType::TextNode) => return Ok(()),
6106      _ => {},
6107    }
6108  }
6109  let Some(paragraph) = paragraph else {
6110    return Ok(());
6111  };
6112  // The line's items: each box with its one float, and the breaks between them.
6113  let mut items: Vec<(Node, Option<Node>)> = Vec::new();
6114  for child in paragraph.get_child_nodes() {
6115    match child.get_type() {
6116      Some(NodeType::TextNode) if whitespace(&child) => {},
6117      Some(NodeType::ElementNode) => {
6118        let qname = document::get_node_qname(&child);
6119        if with(qname, |q| q == "ltx:break") {
6120          items.push((child, None));
6121          continue;
6122        }
6123        if !with(qname, |q| {
6124          q == "ltx:inline-logical-block" || q == "ltx:inline-block"
6125        }) {
6126          return Ok(());
6127        }
6128        let mut float = None;
6129        for inner in child.get_child_nodes() {
6130          match inner.get_type() {
6131            Some(NodeType::TextNode) if whitespace(&inner) => {},
6132            Some(NodeType::ElementNode)
6133              if float.is_none()
6134                && with(document::get_node_qname(&inner), |q| {
6135                  PANEL_FLOATS.contains(&q)
6136                }) =>
6137            {
6138              float = Some(inner)
6139            },
6140            Some(NodeType::ElementNode) | Some(NodeType::TextNode) => return Ok(()),
6141            _ => {},
6142          }
6143        }
6144        let Some(float) = float else {
6145          return Ok(());
6146        };
6147        if !document::can_contain_qsym(parent_qname, document::get_node_qname(&float)) {
6148          return Ok(());
6149        }
6150        items.push((child, Some(float)));
6151      },
6152      Some(NodeType::TextNode) => return Ok(()),
6153      _ => {},
6154    }
6155  }
6156  let boxes = items.iter().filter(|(_, float)| float.is_some()).count();
6157  if boxes == 0 || (boxes == 1 && items.len() > 1) {
6158    return Ok(());
6159  }
6160  let align = paragraph.get_attribute("align");
6161  let class = paragraph.get_attribute("class");
6162  let mut placed = Vec::new();
6163  let mut anchor = para.clone();
6164  for (wrapper, float) in items {
6165    let mut node = match float {
6166      Some(mut float) => {
6167        // The box's own annotation onto its float: `class` merges, the rest where absent.
6168        for (name, value) in wrapper.get_attributes() {
6169          if name == "class" {
6170            document.add_class(&mut float, &value)?;
6171          } else if name != "xml:id"
6172            && name != "id"
6173            && float.get_attribute(&name).is_none()
6174            && document::can_node_have_attribute(&float, &name)
6175          {
6176            document.set_attribute(&mut float, &name, &value)?;
6177          }
6178        }
6179        float
6180      },
6181      None => wrapper,
6182    };
6183    node.unlink();
6184    anchor.add_next_sibling(&mut node)?;
6185    anchor = node.clone();
6186    placed.push(node);
6187  }
6188  // A row takes over the paragraph's identity — its id and id counters, minted during
6189  // construction — so it is numbered as in the whole document when it settles in a streaming
6190  // segment, and no paragraph number is skipped (57g review).
6191  let mut identity: Vec<(String, String)> = para
6192    .get_attributes()
6193    .into_iter()
6194    .filter(|(name, _)| name.starts_with("_ID_counter"))
6195    .collect();
6196  identity.sort();
6197  if let Some(id) = para.get_attribute_ns("id", XML_NS) {
6198    identity.insert(0, ("xml:id".to_string(), id));
6199  }
6200  // The paragraph's content lives on in the floats: keep its box (`remove_node_keeping_box`).
6201  document.remove_node_keeping_box(para.clone());
6202  let mut settled = if boxes == 1 {
6203    placed.into_iter().next()
6204  } else {
6205    document.wrap_nodes_as("ltx:figure", placed, &identity)?
6206  };
6207  // The line's alignment (`\\centering`, `{center}`, `\\raggedleft`) goes with it.
6208  if let Some(settled) = settled.as_mut() {
6209    if let Some(align) = align
6210      && settled.get_attribute("align").is_none()
6211    {
6212      document.set_attribute(settled, "align", &align)?;
6213    }
6214    if let Some(class) = class {
6215      document.add_class(settled, &class)?;
6216    }
6217  }
6218  Ok(())
6219}
6220
6221/// Settle every paragraph of nothing but float-boxes (`settle_float_paragraph`), innermost
6222/// first, once construction is over: every alignment has been stamped and no construction step
6223/// holds a handle into a paragraph any more (settling at a paragraph's close freed nodes a
6224/// `{center}` still held, dropping its alignment — 57g review).
6225pub fn settle_float_paragraphs(document: &mut Document, root: &Node) -> Result<()> {
6226  // (and the row separators no float's `arrange_panels` took: those of a box's own content, `note_panel_separator`)
6227  fn collect(node: &Node, paras: &mut Vec<Node>, separators: &mut Vec<Node>) {
6228    for child in node.get_child_elements() {
6229      collect(&child, paras, separators);
6230      let qname = document::get_node_qname(&child);
6231      if with(qname, |q| q == "ltx:para") {
6232        paras.push(child);
6233      } else if with(qname, |q| q == "ltx:break") && child.get_attribute(PANEL_SEPARATOR).is_some()
6234      {
6235        separators.push(child);
6236      }
6237    }
6238  }
6239  let (mut paras, mut separators) = (Vec::new(), Vec::new());
6240  collect(root, &mut paras, &mut separators);
6241  for separator in separators {
6242    document.remove_node(separator);
6243  }
6244  for para in paras {
6245    settle_float_paragraph(document, &para)?;
6246  }
6247  Ok(())
6248}
6249
6250/// Port of Perl's `arrange_panels_and_breaks`
6251/// (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml L3229-3349): partition a figure/table/float's
6252/// children into rows, inserting `<ltx:break>` where the accumulated panel WIDTH
6253/// would overflow the float width. Author-deposited breaks and captions/metadata
6254/// flush the current row. Panels are marked with `ltx_figure_panel` only when the
6255/// figure has more than one. Beyond Perl, the panel grid rule (user rulings
6256/// 2026-10-22, OXIDIZED_DESIGN_DIVERGENCES #885): the row separators the source
6257/// states (`note_panel_separator`: a `\par`, a `{center}` boundary, `\vskip`,
6258/// glue) break the row or count towards it, and the widths and the line are the
6259/// class's real geometry's (`install_panel_line`, `panel_width_delta`).
6260fn arrange_panels(
6261  document: &mut Document,
6262  node: &mut Node,
6263  whatsit: Option<&Digested>,
6264) -> Result<PanelLayout> {
6265  // The rows are set against the real line (`install_panel_line`): a panel's width is its stated width at the real
6266  // geometry, the width its box has at the registers' values plus what the real values add (`panel_width_delta`).
6267  // The float's `\hsize` (Perl's `floatwidth`) is what a panel with no width of its own fills.
6268  // A row with no real line of its own (a paragraph of floats settled into a row, `settle_float_paragraph`) is set at
6269  // the registers' widths, as before the rule (2202.03884 S4.SS1.fig1).
6270  // A float with no real line is arranged as before the rule: at its `\hsize`, or the geometry's text width
6271  // (`PANEL_FALLBACK_LINE`, `after_float`), which a panel with no width of its own then fills.
6272  let real_line = panel_line_of(whatsit);
6273  let float_width = real_line
6274    .or_else(|| panel_dimension_of(whatsit, PANEL_FALLBACK_LINE))
6275    .unwrap_or_else(|| float_width_of(whatsit));
6276  let hsize = if real_line.is_some() {
6277    float_width_of(whatsit)
6278  } else {
6279    float_width
6280  };
6281  // Perl L3233: 0.03125x min width => at most 32 panels per row.
6282  let min_panel_width = 0.03125 * float_width;
6283  let hbox_body = whatsit.is_some_and(|w| w.get_property_bool(PANEL_HBOX_BODY));
6284
6285  let note_qname = pin!("ltx:note");
6286  let caption_qname = pin!("ltx:caption");
6287  let block_qname = pin!("ltx:block");
6288
6289  let mut current_width: f64 = 0.0;
6290  let mut all_panels: Vec<Node> = Vec::new();
6291  // Bookkeeping triples for the current row: (node, qname, width).
6292  let mut row: Vec<(Node, SymStr, f64)> = Vec::new();
6293  // The source's row separators (`note_panel_separator`): the glue stated since the row's last panel, and a row break
6294  // the source stated after it, kept only when another panel follows before the next break or caption.
6295  let mut pending_glue: f64 = 0.0;
6296  let mut pending_break: Option<Node> = None;
6297  // A row that begins a paragraph (the float's first, one after a `\par`, a `{center}` boundary, a `\vskip`, a
6298  // caption, or a centred `\\`) keeps the glue stated before its first panel, as TeX keeps glue at a paragraph's start;
6299  // a row after a justified `\\` or a `\linebreak` keeps only an `\hspace*`'s (`glue*`: latex.ltx's `\vrule
6300  // width\z@\nobreak\hskip`, which a line break does not discard) and a computed break none (2212.03198 Figs 6, 10-12,
6301  // 15: `\hspace*{-0.5cm}` before three sub-figures, one row in the PDF; `\\\hspace*{-1.1cm}` before a second row of
6302  // four). Under `\centering`, `\raggedright`, `\raggedleft` and in a `{center}`, `{flushleft}` or `{flushright}`, `\\`
6303  // is `\@centercr` (latex.ltx `\let\\\@centercr`), whose `\par` ends the paragraph, so an `\hspace` after it starts
6304  // the next one and is kept (review rev78x3 finding 3, `p7.tex` F1: `\\\hspace{-0.05\columnwidth}` before three
6305  // 0.34\columnwidth panels, one line in the PDF); so is every `\\` in a class's centred floats (`PANEL_FLOATS_CENTRED`).
6306  // A `\newline` is `\@normalcr` in every context (latex.ltx:9256), a justified break, whatever alignment class its
6307  // break took (`PANEL_NORMALCR`; review rev78x4 finding 1: n3 F4 `\centering`, n7 F1 `{center}`,
6308  // `\newline\hspace{0.15\columnwidth}` before three 0.3\columnwidth panels, two lines in the PDF).
6309  let floats_centred = whatsit.is_some() && lookup_bool(PANEL_FLOATS_CENTRED);
6310  let centred_break = |node: &Node| {
6311    node.get_attribute(PANEL_NORMALCR).is_none()
6312      && (floats_centred
6313        || node.get_attribute("class").is_some_and(|class| {
6314          class
6315            .split_whitespace()
6316            .any(|c| matches!(c, "ltx_centering" | "ltx_align_left" | "ltx_align_right"))
6317        }))
6318  };
6319  let mut paragraph_start = true;
6320  let mut leading_glue: f64 = 0.0;
6321  // The width each panel was set at, and whether the source states it (`panel_width_is_stated`), for the grid's
6322  // markup (`annotate_panel_grid`); a merged block's, its parts'.
6323  let mut widths: Vec<(Node, f64, bool)> = Vec::new();
6324  let stated_of = |widths: &[(Node, f64, bool)], node: &Node| {
6325    widths
6326      .iter()
6327      .find(|(n, ..)| n == node)
6328      .is_some_and(|(.., stated)| *stated)
6329  };
6330  let record =
6331    |widths: &mut Vec<(Node, f64, bool)>, node: &Node, width: f64, stated: bool| match widths
6332      .iter_mut()
6333      .find(|(n, ..)| n == node)
6334    {
6335      Some(entry) => {
6336        entry.1 = width;
6337        entry.2 = stated;
6338      },
6339      None => widths.push((node.clone(), width, stated)),
6340    };
6341
6342  for mut child in node.get_child_elements() {
6343    let child_name = document::get_node_qname(&child);
6344
6345    // Perl L3260-3267: move a top-level ltx:note to the nearest caption sibling.
6346    if child_name == note_qname {
6347      let sibling_caption = node
6348        .get_child_elements()
6349        .into_iter()
6350        .find(|c| document::get_node_qname(c) == caption_qname);
6351      if let Some(mut cap) = sibling_caption {
6352        child.unlink_node();
6353        cap.add_child(&mut child).ok();
6354      }
6355      continue;
6356    }
6357
6358    // A separator the source states between panels: glue counts towards the row's width, a break ends the row
6359    // before the next panel; one before the row's first panel or after its last is dropped.
6360    if let Some(kind) = child.get_attribute(PANEL_SEPARATOR) {
6361      if kind == "glue" || kind == "glue*" {
6362        let width = child
6363          .get_attribute(PANEL_GLUE)
6364          .and_then(|w| w.parse::<f64>().ok())
6365          .unwrap_or(0.0);
6366        if !row.is_empty() && pending_break.is_none() {
6367          pending_glue += width;
6368        } else if paragraph_start || kind == "glue*" {
6369          leading_glue += width;
6370        }
6371        document.remove_node(child);
6372      } else if row.is_empty() || pending_break.is_some() {
6373        if kind != "break" && pending_break.is_none() {
6374          paragraph_start = true;
6375          leading_glue = 0.0;
6376        }
6377        document.remove_node(child);
6378      } else {
6379        // The row's break, as a computed one: an alignment's class stamped on the separator (`\centering`) is not its.
6380        // (a `\linebreak` begins no paragraph, a centred `\\`, `cr`, does)
6381        paragraph_start = kind != "break";
6382        child.remove_attribute(PANEL_SEPARATOR).ok();
6383        child.set_attribute("class", "ltx_break").ok();
6384        pending_break = Some(child);
6385      }
6386      continue;
6387    }
6388
6389    if is_panel_break_name(child_name) {
6390      // Perl L3269-3275: a break/caption/meta flushes the current row.
6391      if let Some(stated) = pending_break.take() {
6392        document.remove_node(stated);
6393      }
6394      pending_glue = 0.0;
6395      leading_glue = 0.0;
6396      // (a caption is a paragraph of its own; a justified `\\` ends a line of the paragraph, a centred one the
6397      // paragraph)
6398      paragraph_start = child_name != pin!("ltx:break") || centred_break(&child);
6399      current_width = 0.0;
6400      row.clear();
6401      continue;
6402    }
6403    // A sub-float holding nothing but its number — `\subfloat{\label{…}}`, a label's anchor (2208.08007's
6404    // `\labelphantom`) — makes no box: it is no panel and takes no place in a row (a `\label` is a `\write`).
6405    if holds_only_its_number(&child) {
6406      continue;
6407    }
6408    // A row break the source stated before this panel: the row ends there.
6409    if pending_break.take().is_some() {
6410      pending_glue = 0.0;
6411      current_width = 0.0;
6412      row.clear();
6413    }
6414
6415    // Perl L3277-3284: a standalone block on its own row — break first.
6416    if is_standalone_panel_name(child_name) && box_panel_width(&child).is_none() && !row.is_empty()
6417    {
6418      insert_break_before(document, &mut child)?;
6419      current_width = 0.0;
6420      row.clear();
6421    }
6422
6423    let mut child_width = panel_width(document, &child);
6424    // #6903: a subcaptionbox / subfig \subfloat panel is sized to the full float
6425    // \hsize (it has no explicit `{width}`), so it would take its own row. When
6426    // it wraps a single narrower graphic, size it to that graphic so sibling
6427    // panels share a row — an explicit-width `{subfigure}{W}` already does.
6428    let mut sole_graphic = false;
6429    if let Some(inner) = sole_graphic_width(document, &child) {
6430      if child_width >= hsize && inner < child_width {
6431        child_width = inner;
6432        sole_graphic = true;
6433      } else {
6434        // (a sub-float measured by its body, `panel_body_width` — subfig's and subfigure.sty's — that holds one graphic
6435        // states its width as the one the full-`\hsize` box did above, its body's in the row: 1903.10543 S4.F7,
6436        // `\subfloat[…]{\begin{tabular}{c}\includegraphics[width=5.6cm]{…}\end{tabular}}`, 79f)
6437        sole_graphic = panel_body_width_of(document, &child).is_some();
6438      }
6439    }
6440    let child_stated = sole_graphic || panel_width_is_stated(document, &child, child_width, hsize);
6441    if real_line.is_some() {
6442      child_width = (child_width + panel_width_delta(document, &child)).max(0.0);
6443    }
6444    // The glue the source states between this panel and the row's previous one.
6445    let glue = std::mem::take(&mut pending_glue);
6446
6447    // A row a binding fixed (AASTeX's `\gridline`, a `\hbox to\hsize` of panels: `_gridrow`) stays one row however
6448    // wide its panels add up (2609.09897's two 0.53\textwidth panels and a third, beside negative `\hspace`s).
6449    // So does a row TeX sets in one `\hbox` (`note_panel_hbox`): a sub-float's body, the sub-floats of one box.
6450    let same_fixed_row = hbox_body
6451      || row.last().is_some_and(|(prev, ..)| {
6452        prev
6453          .get_attribute("_gridrow")
6454          .is_some_and(|r| child.get_attribute("_gridrow").as_ref() == Some(&r))
6455          || hbox_row(document, prev).is_some_and(|r| hbox_row(document, &child) == Some(r))
6456      });
6457    if !row.is_empty() && !same_fixed_row && (current_width + glue + child_width > float_width) {
6458      // Perl L3287-3295: row overflow — break before this child, start a new row.
6459      insert_break_before(document, &mut child)?;
6460      document.add_class(&mut child, "ltx_figure_panel")?;
6461      all_panels.push(child.clone());
6462      record(&mut widths, &child, child_width, child_stated);
6463      row = vec![(child, child_name, child_width)];
6464      current_width = child_width;
6465      paragraph_start = false;
6466    } else if let Some((mut prev_node, prev_name, prev_width0)) = row.pop() {
6467      // Perl L3296-3330: try to merge into the previous panel, else append.
6468      let prev_width = if prev_width0 > 0.0 {
6469        prev_width0
6470      } else {
6471        panel_width(document, &prev_node)
6472      };
6473      let big_disparity = prev_width > 0.0
6474        && child_width > 0.0
6475        && (prev_width.max(child_width) / prev_width.min(child_width) > 8.0);
6476      // #2709: the merge groups small/disparate content into an `ltx:block`, but
6477      // the schema forbids a float (`ltx:figure`/`ltx:table`, or any future
6478      // `ltx:float`) as a block child — wrapping one yields an invalid
6479      // `<block><figure/></block>`. Ask the MODEL (not a hard-coded name list)
6480      // whether the block can hold what would go into it, per merge branch; if
6481      // not, keep the panels as siblings. Minipage grids stay valid block content
6482      // and are unaffected.
6483      // Perl reuses any `ltx:block` as the container, a minipage's or `\parbox`'s own
6484      // included: the neighbouring panel went inside that box, which TeX set at its width
6485      // with only its own material — a label minipage beside a picture minipage came out
6486      // under the picture (witness 2605.00042 S5.F4; KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #331). Such a box
6487      // stays closed and the merge wraps the two.
6488      let reuse_prev = prev_name == block_qname && box_panel_width(&prev_node).is_none();
6489      let reuse_child = child_name == block_qname && box_panel_width(&child).is_none();
6490      let merge_is_valid = if reuse_prev {
6491        model::can_contain_sym(block_qname, child_name)
6492      } else if reuse_child {
6493        model::can_contain_sym(block_qname, prev_name)
6494      } else {
6495        model::can_contain_sym(block_qname, prev_name)
6496          && model::can_contain_sym(block_qname, child_name)
6497      };
6498      if merge_is_valid
6499        && (child_width == 0.0 || big_disparity || (prev_width + child_width < min_panel_width))
6500      {
6501        // Perl L3312-3325: contain the two pieces in a single ltx:block panel.
6502        let merged_width = prev_width + child_width;
6503        if reuse_prev {
6504          child.unlink_node();
6505          prev_node.add_child(&mut child).ok();
6506          let stated = stated_of(&widths, &prev_node) && child_stated;
6507          record(&mut widths, &prev_node, merged_width, stated);
6508          row.push((prev_node, prev_name, merged_width));
6509        } else if reuse_child {
6510          // The previous panel goes FIRST in the block, keeping source order.
6511          // Perl `$child->appendChild($prev_node)` (L3318) puts it last: an
6512          // `\includegraphics` before a `{minipage}` came out after the
6513          // minipage's text (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #274; guard
6514          // `node_box_append::a_panel_merged_into_a_block_keeps_its_place`).
6515          prev_node.unlink_node();
6516          match child.get_first_child() {
6517            Some(mut first) => {
6518              first.add_prev_sibling(&mut prev_node).ok();
6519            },
6520            None => {
6521              child.add_child(&mut prev_node).ok();
6522            },
6523          }
6524          all_panels.push(child.clone());
6525          let stated = stated_of(&widths, &prev_node) && child_stated;
6526          record(&mut widths, &child, merged_width, stated);
6527          row.push((child, child_name, merged_width));
6528        } else {
6529          // The wrapper is the panel now: a row-start box already marked one (overflow, Perl
6530          // L3292) keeps its own classes only, and leaves the panel list (Perl L3324 pops the last
6531          // entry, which a zero-width row start never was).
6532          if all_panels.last() == Some(&prev_node) {
6533            all_panels.pop();
6534          }
6535          document.remove_class(&mut prev_node, "ltx_figure_panel");
6536          let stated = stated_of(&widths, &prev_node) && child_stated;
6537          if let Some(block) = document.wrap_nodes("ltx:block", vec![prev_node, child])? {
6538            all_panels.push(block.clone());
6539            record(&mut widths, &block, merged_width, stated);
6540            row.push((block, block_qname, merged_width));
6541          }
6542        }
6543      } else {
6544        // Perl L3327-3330: keep the previous panel, append this one as a sibling.
6545        let prev_stated = stated_of(&widths, &prev_node);
6546        record(&mut widths, &prev_node, prev_width, prev_stated);
6547        record(&mut widths, &child, child_width, child_stated);
6548        row.push((prev_node, prev_name, prev_width));
6549        all_panels.push(child.clone());
6550        row.push((child, child_name, child_width));
6551      }
6552      current_width += glue + child_width;
6553    } else {
6554      // Perl L3331-3333: no previous panel in the row — just add this child.
6555      paragraph_start = false;
6556      record(&mut widths, &child, child_width, child_stated);
6557      if child_width > 0.0 {
6558        all_panels.push(child.clone());
6559      }
6560      if is_standalone_panel_name(child_name) && box_panel_width(&child).is_none() {
6561        // Perl L3334-3342: a standalone panel as the sole row content flushes the
6562        // row and forces a break before the next sibling (unless that sibling is
6563        // itself a break/caption/meta), so subsequent content starts a new row.
6564        if let Some(mut trailer) = child.get_next_sibling() {
6565          // (a row separator the source states is passed over: what follows it decides)
6566          let mut next = Some(trailer.clone());
6567          while let Some(node) = next
6568            .as_ref()
6569            .filter(|n| n.get_attribute(PANEL_SEPARATOR).is_some())
6570          {
6571            next = node.get_next_sibling();
6572          }
6573          let trailer_name = next
6574            .as_ref()
6575            .map_or(pin!("ltx:caption"), document::get_node_qname);
6576          if !is_panel_break_name(trailer_name) {
6577            insert_break_before(document, &mut trailer)?;
6578          }
6579        }
6580        // The standalone panel is a row of its own, so the next row starts
6581        // empty. Perl resets `$current_width` here and then adds the panel's
6582        // width to it (L3341-3343), so the next row starts that full: with
6583        // W12's node boxes the `{\small\makebox[0.49\textwidth]{…}\hfill
6584        // \makebox[0.49\textwidth]{…}}` caption line of a subfigure grid is
6585        // its whole width, and the four `0.24\textwidth` panels after it split
6586        // 1 | 3, where pdflatex sets them in one row (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #274;
6587        // witness 2605.02317; guard `node_box_append::a_standalone_panel_row_starts_the_next_row_empty`).
6588        current_width = 0.0;
6589      } else {
6590        row.push((child, child_name, child_width));
6591        // Perl L3343: the row was empty (current_width is 0), so this seeds
6592        // the accumulator with the child's width (and the glue its paragraph's start keeps).
6593        current_width += child_width + std::mem::take(&mut leading_glue);
6594      }
6595    }
6596  }
6597
6598  if let Some(stated) = pending_break {
6599    document.remove_node(stated);
6600  }
6601  // Perl L3346-3348: only mark panels when the figure is complex (>1 panel).
6602  if all_panels.len() > 1 {
6603    for panel in &mut all_panels {
6604      document.add_class(panel, "ltx_figure_panel")?;
6605    }
6606  }
6607  // The widths are the real ones where the float's line is (`install_panel_line`, `note_stated_widths`), or where the
6608  // registers are the real geometry already (`PANEL_REGISTERS_REAL`); a float arranged at the registers' line or the
6609  // geometry's fallback (a width it could not evaluate) states none for its markup.
6610  let evaluated =
6611    real_line.is_some() || whatsit.is_some_and(|w| w.get_property_bool(PANEL_REGISTERS_REAL));
6612  Ok(PanelLayout {
6613    widths,
6614    line: float_width,
6615    column: panel_dimension_of(whatsit, PANEL_COLUMN).filter(|_| evaluated),
6616    evaluated,
6617  })
6618}
6619/// What `arrange_panels` decided a float's panels are set at, for its grid's markup (`annotate_panel_grid`): each
6620/// panel's width (scaled points; a merged block's its parts'), the line its rows were set against, the real
6621/// running-text column at the float (`PANEL_COLUMN`, where the widths are the real geometry's), and whether those are
6622/// the real geometry's (`evaluated`: the float's line is the class's real one, or the registers are it).
6623pub(crate) struct PanelLayout {
6624  widths:    Vec<(Node, f64, bool)>,
6625  line:      f64,
6626  column:    Option<f64>,
6627  evaluated: bool,
6628}
6629
6630/// A sub-float holding nothing but its number (`ltx:tags`): `\subfloat{\label{…}}` (2208.08007's
6631/// `\newcommand{\labelphantom}[1]{\subfloat{\label{#1}}}`, five or six before the one graphic that draws every
6632/// panel). TeX sets it as an empty box (a `\label` is a `\write`), so it is no panel of its float.
6633fn holds_only_its_number(node: &Node) -> bool {
6634  with(document::get_node_qname(node), |q| {
6635    PANEL_FLOATS.contains(&q)
6636  }) && node
6637    .get_child_nodes()
6638    .iter()
6639    .all(|child| match child.get_type() {
6640      Some(NodeType::ElementNode) => document::get_node_qname(child) == pin!("ltx:tags"),
6641      Some(NodeType::TextNode) => child.get_content().trim().is_empty(),
6642      _ => true,
6643    })
6644}
6645
6646/// The panel grid's attributes on a float (`annotate_panel_grid`).
6647const PANEL_GRID_ATTRIBUTES: [&str; 4] = ["panelrows", "panelcols", "panelline", "panelfill"];
6648
6649/// How far apart (a fraction of the line) two panel widths may be and still be one column's (`annotate_panel_grid`).
6650const PANEL_WIDTH_TOLERANCE: f64 = 0.01;
6651
6652/// The panel grid's markup (user rulings 2026-10-22, FIDELITY_CHARTER §2 "Float panels"; grid design study option
6653/// (a)): the float `arrange_panels` set in rows says them — `panelrows`, `panelcols` (the most columns a row takes),
6654/// and `ltx_panels_matrix` or `ltx_panels_gallery` — and each panel its width as a fraction of the row's line
6655/// (`panelwidth`, 3 decimals) where that width is one the source states (`states_its_width`: a graphic's, a rule's,
6656/// a box's of a declared width, or theirs side by side; not a measure of our own setting of text, a tabular, a list)
6657/// taken at the real geometry (none where the float could not take its widths there, `PanelLayout`: never a guess),
6658/// and, in a matrix, the columns it spans when 2 or more (`panelspan`); where every panel states its width, the float
6659/// its line as a fraction of the PDF's running-text column at the float (`panelline`: the class's real column in two
6660/// columns, its text width in one; 1 for a `figure`, about 2.07 for a two-column class's `figure*`, under 1 for a
6661/// wrapfigure) and its widest row's sum of `panelwidth` (`panelfill`, fractions of its own line) — user ruling
6662/// 2026-10-23: a panel renders at `panelwidth` × `panelline` of the theme's column, divided by max(1, `panelfill` ×
6663/// `panelline`), so a `figure*` fills the column and a narrow float stays narrow; the converter knows only the PDF's
6664/// column and the float's line, never a theme constant. A matrix only on strong signals: an
6665/// author-built `tabular` of panels (`tabular_panel_grid`, its cells' `colspan` and `rowspan` kept), or 2 or more rows
6666/// of the same columns — as many panels, each as wide as the other row's (within `PANEL_WIDTH_TOLERANCE`), another
6667/// row's panel as wide as the columns it spans — whose panels' own captions are none or exactly one whole row's, its
6668/// columns' labels (captioned panels elsewhere are a gallery's: independent, their order not their place;
6669/// `matrix_spans`). A float of one panel states none of it. A
6670/// sub-float group states its own (its panels' widths a fraction of its line), as it is a flex figure of its own in
6671/// HTML; as a panel of its float it states its width there too. Perl emits none of this
6672/// (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:3229-3349; subcaption.sty.ltxml:60-66 stores `width`, never emits it).
6673/// OXIDIZED_DESIGN_DIVERGENCES #887.
6674pub(crate) fn annotate_panel_grid(
6675  document: &mut Document,
6676  node: &mut Node,
6677  layout: &PanelLayout,
6678) -> Result<()> {
6679  // A lone inner float's grid, the float's since `collapse_float` made the inner's panels its own.
6680  if node.get_attribute("panelrows").is_some() {
6681    return Ok(());
6682  }
6683  // The rows, as the HTML sets them: runs of panels between breaks and captions.
6684  let mut rows: Vec<Vec<Node>> = vec![Vec::new()];
6685  for child in node.get_child_elements() {
6686    if is_panel_break_name(document::get_node_qname(&child)) {
6687      rows.push(Vec::new());
6688    } else if child
6689      .get_attribute("class")
6690      .is_some_and(|class| class.split_whitespace().any(|c| c == "ltx_figure_panel"))
6691      && let Some(row) = rows.last_mut()
6692    {
6693      row.push(child);
6694    }
6695  }
6696  rows.retain(|row| !row.is_empty());
6697  if rows.iter().map(Vec::len).sum::<usize>() < 2 {
6698    if let Some((rows, cols)) = tabular_panel_grid(document, node) {
6699      document.add_class(node, "ltx_panels_matrix")?;
6700      document.set_attribute(node, "panelrows", &rows.to_string())?;
6701      document.set_attribute(node, "panelcols", &cols.to_string())?;
6702    }
6703    return Ok(());
6704  }
6705  let line = layout.line;
6706  let width_of = |panel: &Node| {
6707    layout
6708      .widths
6709      .iter()
6710      .find(|(n, ..)| n == panel)
6711      .filter(|(_, w, stated)| *stated && layout.evaluated && line > 0.0 && *w > 0.0)
6712      .map(|(_, w, _)| *w * graphic_rounding(document, panel) / line)
6713  };
6714  let widths: Vec<Vec<Option<f64>>> = rows
6715    .iter()
6716    .map(|row| row.iter().map(width_of).collect())
6717    .collect();
6718  let spans = matrix_spans(&rows, &widths);
6719  let cols = match &spans {
6720    Some(spans) => spans
6721      .iter()
6722      .map(|row| row.iter().sum::<usize>())
6723      .max()
6724      .unwrap_or(0),
6725    None => rows.iter().map(Vec::len).max().unwrap_or(0),
6726  };
6727  for (r, row) in rows.iter_mut().enumerate() {
6728    for (c, panel) in row.iter_mut().enumerate() {
6729      if let Some(width) = widths[r][c] {
6730        document.set_attribute(panel, "panelwidth", &panel_fraction(width))?;
6731      }
6732      if let Some(span) = spans.as_ref().map(|s| s[r][c]).filter(|span| *span >= 2) {
6733        document.set_attribute(panel, "panelspan", &span.to_string())?;
6734      }
6735    }
6736  }
6737  let class = if spans.is_some() {
6738    "ltx_panels_matrix"
6739  } else {
6740    "ltx_panels_gallery"
6741  };
6742  document.add_class(node, class)?;
6743  document.set_attribute(node, "panelrows", &rows.len().to_string())?;
6744  document.set_attribute(node, "panelcols", &cols.to_string())?;
6745  // Where every panel states its width: the line as a fraction of the running-text column (`panelline`), and the
6746  // widest row's sum of the widths its panels state (`panelfill`, fractions of the float's own line).
6747  if let Some(column) = layout.column.filter(|c| *c > 0.0)
6748    && widths.iter().flatten().all(Option::is_some)
6749  {
6750    let stated = |width: f64| (width * 1000.0).round() / 1000.0;
6751    let fill = widths
6752      .iter()
6753      .map(|row| row.iter().flatten().map(|w| stated(*w)).sum::<f64>())
6754      .fold(0.0, f64::max);
6755    document.set_attribute(node, "panelline", &panel_fraction(line / column))?;
6756    document.set_attribute(node, "panelfill", &panel_fraction(fill))?;
6757  }
6758  Ok(())
6759}
6760
6761/// What a graphic panel's box lost to its image's pixel rounding, as a factor of its width (`annotate_panel_grid`; the
6762/// row rule scales the box to the real geometry, `note_stated_widths_in`, so the factor holds there too): the width its
6763/// `\includegraphics` states (`width=`, its only size) over its box's, where the two are within 1% and a point
6764/// (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1142: a raster image's box is 72/72.27 of the stated width rounded up to a whole pixel, so
6765/// 2208.08007 S0.F1.g1's `width=\linewidth` stated 0.997; review rev79c finding 4); 1 for any other panel, or a graphic
6766/// its options size otherwise (a height, a scale, an angle).
6767fn graphic_rounding(document: &Document, panel: &Node) -> f64 {
6768  if document::get_node_qname(panel) != pin!("ltx:graphics") {
6769    return 1.0;
6770  }
6771  let Some(options) = panel.get_attribute("options") else {
6772    return 1.0;
6773  };
6774  let mut stated = None;
6775  for option in options.split(',') {
6776    let (key, value) = option.split_once('=').unwrap_or((option, ""));
6777    match key.trim() {
6778      "width" => stated = Dimension::spec_to_f64(value.trim()).ok(),
6779      "height" | "totalheight" | "scale" | "angle" | "viewport" | "bb" | "natwidth"
6780      | "natheight" => return 1.0,
6781      _ => {},
6782    }
6783  }
6784  let boxed = document
6785    .get_node_box(panel)
6786    .and_then(|b| b.get_width(None).ok().flatten())
6787    .map_or(0.0, |w| w.value_of() as f64);
6788  match stated {
6789    Some(stated)
6790      if stated > 0.0 && boxed > 0.0 && (stated - boxed).abs() <= 0.01 * stated + 65536.0 =>
6791    {
6792      stated / boxed
6793    },
6794    _ => 1.0,
6795  }
6796}
6797
6798/// A fraction of a line, as `panelwidth` states it: 3 decimals, no trailing zeros.
6799fn panel_fraction(width: f64) -> String {
6800  let fixed = format!("{width:.3}");
6801  fixed
6802    .trim_end_matches('0')
6803    .trim_end_matches('.')
6804    .to_string()
6805}
6806
6807/// The columns each panel spans when the rows are a matrix (`annotate_panel_grid`), else `None`. The columns are those
6808/// of 2 or more rows that agree panel for panel (the most panels a row takes, 2 or more; each width within
6809/// `PANEL_WIDTH_TOLERANCE` of the other row's), and every other row takes them all, each panel as wide as the columns
6810/// it spans; every width is known; and the panels' own captions (`holds_a_caption`) are none, or exactly one whole
6811/// row's — they label its columns (main-session decision 3, 2026-10-23, review rev79c finding 2, checked on the PDFs:
6812/// 2209.01559 Figs 3, 5; 1404.0431 Fig 1; 2212.03198 Figs 7, 10, 13, 14; 1811.02385 S4.F3-F6). Captions on every
6813/// panel, on more than one row, or on some panels of a row make the panels a gallery's — independent, their order
6814/// not their place (2503.15158 S4.F7, 2404.12123 S3.F6, 2106.04682 A2.F4 (a)-(e) and a legend, 1808.10020
6815/// chapter5.figure11 and a blank panel, 2602.17978 Ch4.F2/F3).
6816fn matrix_spans(rows: &[Vec<Node>], widths: &[Vec<Option<f64>>]) -> Option<Vec<Vec<usize>>> {
6817  if rows.len() < 2 {
6818    return None;
6819  }
6820  // (each row's captioned panels, and its panels)
6821  let captioned: Vec<(usize, usize)> = rows
6822    .iter()
6823    .map(|row| {
6824      (
6825        row.iter().filter(|panel| holds_a_caption(panel)).count(),
6826        row.len(),
6827      )
6828    })
6829    .collect();
6830  let some_of_a_row = captioned.iter().any(|(c, n)| *c > 0 && c < n);
6831  let whole_rows = captioned.iter().filter(|(c, n)| c == n).count();
6832  let any = captioned.iter().any(|(c, _)| *c > 0);
6833  if any && (some_of_a_row || whole_rows != 1) {
6834    return None;
6835  }
6836  let known: Vec<Vec<f64>> = widths
6837    .iter()
6838    .map(|row| row.iter().copied().collect())
6839    .collect::<Option<_>>()?;
6840  let agree = |a: &[f64], b: &[f64]| {
6841    a.len() == b.len()
6842      && a
6843        .iter()
6844        .zip(b)
6845        .all(|(x, y)| (x - y).abs() <= PANEL_WIDTH_TOLERANCE)
6846  };
6847  let most = known.iter().map(Vec::len).max().unwrap_or(0);
6848  if most < 2 {
6849    return None;
6850  }
6851  let columns = known
6852    .iter()
6853    .filter(|row| row.len() == most)
6854    .find(|row| known.iter().filter(|other| agree(row, other)).count() >= 2)?;
6855  // Each row's panels over the columns, in order: a panel spans the fewest columns whose widths add up to its own.
6856  known
6857    .iter()
6858    .map(|row| {
6859      let mut at = 0;
6860      let mut spans = Vec::with_capacity(row.len());
6861      for width in row {
6862        let mut sum = 0.0;
6863        let span = (at..columns.len()).position(|column| {
6864          sum += columns[column];
6865          (sum - width).abs() <= PANEL_WIDTH_TOLERANCE
6866        })?
6867          + 1;
6868        spans.push(span);
6869        at += span;
6870      }
6871      (at == columns.len()).then_some(spans)
6872    })
6873    .collect()
6874}
6875
6876/// Is the width `arrange_panels` set a panel at (`width`, against the float's `hsize`) one the source states
6877/// (`annotate_panel_grid`): a box of a declared width (`box_panel_width`), or a panel that states its width
6878/// (`states_its_width`) — except a sub-float set at the float's whole `\hsize` with no body width of its own
6879/// (`panel_body_width`): it states none, its box takes the line (subfig's `\subfloat`, Perl's measure; the PDF's box is
6880/// its content's).
6881fn panel_width_is_stated(document: &Document, panel: &Node, width: f64, hsize: f64) -> bool {
6882  if box_panel_width(panel).is_some() {
6883    return true;
6884  }
6885  let sub_float = with(document::get_node_qname(panel), |q| {
6886    PANEL_FLOATS.contains(&q)
6887  });
6888  let body_width = panel_body_width_of(document, panel).is_some();
6889  if sub_float && !body_width && width >= hsize {
6890    return false;
6891  }
6892  states_its_width(panel)
6893}
6894
6895/// Is a panel's width one the source states (`annotate_panel_grid`), not a measure of our own setting of its material:
6896/// a graphic's (its stated size, or its image's), a rule's, a picture's, a box's of a declared width (a minipage, a
6897/// `\parbox`: `box_panel_width`), or a container's whose every part is one of those, side by side (a sub-float's body,
6898/// a merged block; its tags, captions and breaks aside). A paragraph of text, a tabular, a list, a listing, math: our
6899/// measure of their natural width is no width TeX sets them at (a paragraph is the line; 1807.05122 S2.F2's text
6900/// panel measured 9.7 lines wide).
6901fn states_its_width(panel: &Node) -> bool {
6902  let qname = document::get_node_qname(panel);
6903  if with(qname, |q| {
6904    matches!(q, "ltx:graphics" | "ltx:rule" | "ltx:picture")
6905  }) || box_panel_width(panel).is_some()
6906  {
6907    return true;
6908  }
6909  if !with(qname, |q| {
6910    matches!(
6911      q,
6912      "ltx:figure"
6913        | "ltx:table"
6914        | "ltx:float"
6915        | "ltx:block"
6916        | "ltx:inline-block"
6917        | "ltx:p"
6918        | "ltx:text"
6919    )
6920  }) {
6921    return false;
6922  }
6923  let mut parts = 0;
6924  for child in panel.get_child_nodes() {
6925    match child.get_type() {
6926      Some(NodeType::TextNode) if !child.get_content().trim().is_empty() => return false,
6927      Some(NodeType::ElementNode) => {
6928        let name = document::get_node_qname(&child);
6929        if is_panel_break_name(name) || with(name, |q| matches!(q, "ltx:note" | "ltx:indexmark")) {
6930          continue;
6931        }
6932        if !states_its_width(&child) {
6933          return false;
6934        }
6935        parts += 1;
6936      },
6937      _ => {},
6938    }
6939  }
6940  parts > 0
6941}
6942
6943/// A panel with a caption of its own (a sub-float's, a captioned minipage's), anywhere in it.
6944fn holds_a_caption(panel: &Node) -> bool {
6945  panel
6946    .get_child_elements()
6947    .iter()
6948    .any(|child| document::get_node_qname(child) == pin!("ltx:caption") || holds_a_caption(child))
6949}
6950
6951/// The least size (scaled points) a graphic or picture in a `tabular` cell has, both wide and tall (its width and its
6952/// height plus depth), to be a panel of a matrix (`tabular_panel_grid`): 24pt, two lines of text. A data table's icons,
6953/// bars and sparklines are small or thin in one of them (review rev79c finding 1: 2608.05898 S4.T2/T5's 102pt x
6954/// 6.69pt bars, 2506.23665 Ch3.T4/T5, Ch5.T4/T5's 18pt-high sparklines, 2411.16612 S7.T1/T2's 8pt icons, 2501.18280
6955/// S4.T3/A4.T6, 1509.07152 S10.T23, 1805.10096 Sx4.T1, 2504.02271 S2.T1); a matrix's panels are not (1403.6637 S4.F6,
6956/// S4.F8's 22-30pt x 38pt, 2008.05524 T11-16 72pt, 0908.0534 Figs 1-2, 1104.5469; 2502.08151 S7.T3's 491pt x 29pt
6957/// image strips). Of the 253 `tabular` matrices r1 found in the 1,907-paper population this keeps 240: the larger
6958/// dimension alone kept 246, the bars and sparklines among them.
6959const PANEL_GRAPHIC_LEAST: f64 = 24.0 * 65536.0;
6960
6961/// Is `node` a graphic or a picture of a panel's size (`PANEL_GRAPHIC_LEAST`), each dimension its box's or its
6962/// element's stated `width`/`height` (a picture's, in points), the larger.
6963fn is_panel_graphic(document: &Document, node: &Node) -> bool {
6964  if !with(document::get_node_qname(node), |q| {
6965    matches!(q, "ltx:graphics" | "ltx:picture")
6966  }) {
6967    return false;
6968  }
6969  let size = |value: Option<RegisterValue>| value.map_or(0.0, |v| v.value_of() as f64);
6970  let (boxed_width, boxed_height) = document.get_node_box(node).map_or((0.0, 0.0), |b| {
6971    (
6972      size(b.get_width(None).ok().flatten()),
6973      size(b.get_height()) + size(b.get_depth()),
6974    )
6975  });
6976  let stated = |name: &str| {
6977    node.get_attribute(name).map_or(0.0, |value| {
6978      let value = value.trim();
6979      match value.strip_suffix("pt").unwrap_or(value).parse::<f64>() {
6980        Ok(points) => points * 65536.0,
6981        Err(_) => Dimension::spec_to_f64(value).unwrap_or(0.0),
6982      }
6983    })
6984  };
6985  boxed_width
6986    .max(stated("width"))
6987    .min(boxed_height.max(stated("height")))
6988    >= PANEL_GRAPHIC_LEAST
6989}
6990
6991/// An author-built `tabular` of panels (`annotate_panel_grid`): the float's one content is a `tabular` (alone, or in
6992/// a box of nothing else: `\resizebox`, `adjustbox`) 2 or more of whose cells hold a graphic of a panel's size
6993/// (`is_panel_graphic`; a data table's icons, bars and sparklines make no matrix). Its rows and the most columns a row
6994/// takes (cells' `colspan` counted).
6995fn tabular_panel_grid(document: &Document, node: &Node) -> Option<(usize, usize)> {
6996  let content = |node: &Node| -> Vec<Node> {
6997    node
6998      .get_child_elements()
6999      .into_iter()
7000      .filter(|child| {
7001        let qname = document::get_node_qname(child);
7002        !is_panel_break_name(qname) && !with(qname, |q| matches!(q, "ltx:note" | "ltx:indexmark"))
7003      })
7004      .collect()
7005  };
7006  let mut children = content(node);
7007  let tabular = loop {
7008    let [only] = children.as_slice() else {
7009      return None;
7010    };
7011    let qname = document::get_node_qname(only);
7012    if qname == pin!("ltx:tabular") {
7013      break only.clone();
7014    }
7015    if qname != pin!("ltx:inline-block") {
7016      return None;
7017    }
7018    children = content(only);
7019  };
7020  // (its own rows and cells, not a nested tabular's)
7021  fn own(node: &Node, qname: &str, out: &mut Vec<Node>) {
7022    for child in node.get_child_elements() {
7023      let name = document::get_node_qname(&child);
7024      if with(name, |n| n == qname) {
7025        out.push(child);
7026      } else if !with(name, |n| n == "ltx:tabular") {
7027        own(&child, qname, out);
7028      }
7029    }
7030  }
7031  fn holds_graphic(document: &Document, node: &Node) -> bool {
7032    node
7033      .get_child_elements()
7034      .iter()
7035      .any(|child| is_panel_graphic(document, child) || holds_graphic(document, child))
7036  }
7037  let mut rows = Vec::new();
7038  own(&tabular, "ltx:tr", &mut rows);
7039  let mut graphic_cells = 0;
7040  let mut cols = 0;
7041  for row in &rows {
7042    let mut cells = Vec::new();
7043    own(row, "ltx:td", &mut cells);
7044    graphic_cells += cells
7045      .iter()
7046      .filter(|cell| holds_graphic(document, cell))
7047      .count();
7048    cols = cols.max(
7049      cells
7050        .iter()
7051        .map(|cell| {
7052          cell
7053            .get_attribute("colspan")
7054            .and_then(|c| c.parse::<usize>().ok())
7055            .unwrap_or(1)
7056        })
7057        .sum::<usize>(),
7058    );
7059  }
7060  (graphic_cells >= 2).then_some((rows.len(), cols))
7061}

7063/// Perl: collapseFloat (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:3437-3464)
7064/// If a figure/table/float contains exactly one inner float child,
7065/// and they don't BOTH have captions, collapse the inner into the outer.
7066fn collapse_float(document: &mut Document, float: &mut Node) -> Result<()> {
7067  let caption_qname = pin!("ltx:caption");
7068  // Find inner float/figure/table children
7069  let mut inners: Vec<Node> = Vec::new();
7070  for child in float.get_child_elements() {
7071    if with(document::get_node_qname(&child), |q| {
7072      PANEL_FLOATS.contains(&q)
7073    }) {
7074      inners.push(child);
7075    }
7076  }
7077  if inners.len() != 1 {
7078    return Ok(());
7079  }
7080  let mut inner = inners.into_iter().next().unwrap();
7081  // Check captions: collapse only if they don't BOTH have captions (Perl collapseFloat,
7082  // latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:3444). A float numbered by a phantom caption — its own `ltx:tags`, no
7083  // `ltx:caption` — is captioned in caption.sty's terms (`\caption@refstepcounter`, caption.sty:392-395):
7084  // the outer float's tags when the inner has tags of its own, an inner float's only when they came from a sub-float
7085  // counter (`after_float`'s `panel_number`: `\phantomcaption`, a bare `\subfloat{…}`,
7086  // `\phantomsubcaption`), and such a panel keeps its number and its `\label` (2605.28276
7087  // `\cref{fig:corridor}` dangled when the collapse copied the panel's `labels` over the figure's;
7088  // 2605.04869, 2605.17547, 2605.20770, 2605.27546 read the panel's graphic after the figure caption).
7089  // An inner float's other tags — a longtable's own step (2605.18937, ltablex), the outer caption's
7090  // counters taken by an inner float that closed first (2605.26653) — leave it collapsible, as Perl.
7091  let tags_qname = pin!("ltx:tags");
7092  let has_child = |node: &Node, want: SymStr| {
7093    node
7094      .get_child_elements()
7095      .iter()
7096      .any(|c| document::get_node_qname(c) == want)
7097  };
7098  // The outer's tags count only beside an inner numbered by its own tags: a tagless inner holds the
7099  // very caption whose counters the outer rescued (`\caption` in a minipage or `\parbox` of a
7100  // figure, which `insert_block` makes a figure; 57bu.2 A/B: 40 papers, 2605.01437 Fig. 1).
7101  let outer_has_caption = has_child(float, caption_qname)
7102    || (has_child(float, tags_qname) && has_child(&inner, tags_qname));
7103  let inner_has_caption = has_child(&inner, caption_qname)
7104    || (has_child(&inner, tags_qname)
7105      && document
7106        .get_node_box(&inner)
7107        .is_some_and(|b| b.get_property_bool("panel_number")));
7108  if outer_has_caption && inner_has_caption {
7109    return Ok(());
7110  }
7111  // The collapsed float keeps the id of the element that carries its number. An inner float numbered
7112  // by its caption or by its tags alone — a caption-less longtable's own step, a tabularray tall table
7113  // whose theme hides the caption — in a float with neither gives the float its id (`S1.T1`, not the
7114  // outer's `S1.tab1`); a float holding the tags a caption in its minipage stepped keeps its own
7115  // (`S1.F1`, not the minipage's `S1.F1.fig1`: 2605.01437's four figures, 2605.03502, 2605.15932's
7116  // sub-figures). Perl moves the id exactly when the inner has a caption (collapseFloat,
7117  // latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:3449-3452). Divergence #372; guards
7118  // `perfect_kernel_batch57::captionless_float_takes_the_inner_number`,
7119  // `perfect_kernel_batch57::tabularray_tall_table_in_a_captionless_float` (57cp review 5: kcoll, fl).
7120  let inner_is_the_number = !has_child(float, tags_qname)
7121    && !has_child(float, caption_qname)
7122    && (has_child(&inner, caption_qname) || has_child(&inner, tags_qname));
7123  // An inner float beside other content — a sibling panel, not only what `arrange_panels` counts as no
7124  // panel (tags, captions, breaks, notes) — is one panel of the outer: its box geometry and its box and
7125  // panel classes describe that panel, not the float. Perl copies every attribute (collapseFloat,
7126  // latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:3447-3449, KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #388), so a side caption's `0.3\linewidth`
7127  // minipage gave its figure that width beside the `0.65\linewidth` panel (2605.03502), and a subfigure
7128  // of a `0.05\linewidth` caption minipage and a `0.86\linewidth` panel claimed 17.3pt (2605.15932,
7129  // whose two `\linewidth` subfigures then shared one row); 57by, divergence #375. A lone inner float is
7130  // the float, geometry and all (an `algorithm` of one minipage). Classes merge in both cases, as
7131  // `insert_block` merges them (divergence #125): an `algorithm` keeps `ltx_float_algorithm`
7132  // (2605.17037).
7133  let beside_content = float.get_child_elements().iter().any(|child| {
7134    let qname = document::get_node_qname(child);
7135    child != &inner
7136      && !is_panel_break_name(qname)
7137      && !with(qname, |q| matches!(q, "ltx:note" | "ltx:indexmark"))
7138  });
7139  // Copy inner's attributes to outer (except xml:id); the labels and classes of both are kept.
7140  let attrs = inner.get_attributes();
7141  for (name, value) in &attrs {
7142    // get_attributes() may return the key as "id" (local name) or "xml:id" (prefixed)
7143    if name == "xml:id" || name == "id" {
7144      continue;
7145    }
7146    // (nor its panel grid's markup, `annotate_panel_grid`: the float's own is made of its panels, the inner's among
7147    // them; a lone inner's grid is the float's)
7148    if beside_content && matches!(name.as_str(), "width" | "height" | "depth" | "vattach") {
7149      continue;
7150    }
7151    if (beside_content && PANEL_GRID_ATTRIBUTES.contains(&name.as_str()))
7152      || matches!(name.as_str(), "panelwidth" | "panelspan")
7153    {
7154      continue;
7155    }
7156    if name == "class" {
7157      for class in value.split_whitespace() {
7158        if !(beside_content
7159          && matches!(
7160            class,
7161            "ltx_minipage"
7162              | "ltx_parbox"
7163              | "ltx_figure_panel"
7164              | "ltx_panels_gallery"
7165              | "ltx_panels_matrix"
7166          ))
7167        {
7168          document.add_class(float, class)?;
7169        }
7170      }
7171    } else if name == "labels"
7172      && let Some(outer) = float.get_attribute("labels")
7173    {
7174      let mut labels: Vec<&str> = outer.split_whitespace().collect();
7175      for label in value.split_whitespace() {
7176        if !labels.contains(&label) {
7177          labels.push(label);
7178        }
7179      }
7180      document.set_attribute(float, name, &labels.join(" "))?;
7181    } else {
7182      document.set_attribute(float, name, value)?;
7183    }
7184  }
7185  // If inner has caption (or is the float's only number), promote inner's xml:id to outer
7186  if inner_is_the_number {
7187    let inner_id = inner
7188      .get_attribute("xml:id")
7189      .or_else(|| inner.get_attribute_ns("id", "http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace"));
7190    if let Some(id) = inner_id {
7191      // Unrecord the outer's old ID and remove the attribute before setting the new one
7192      if let Some(old_id) = float.get_attribute_ns("id", "http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace") {
7193        document.unrecord_id(&old_id);
7194      }
7195      remove_xml_id(float);
7196      document.unrecord_id(&id);
7197      document.set_attribute(float, "xml:id", &id)?;
7198    }
7199  }
7200  // An inner float that was one panel of the outer (`arrange_panels` ran first) leaves its content
7201  // standing as that panel: its elements other than breaks, captions and notes take the panel class
7202  // its own box carried, or a tall table beside a tabular in a caption-less `table` stacked the two
7203  // (57cp review 5, side6; 2605.31204 A1.F2, a tabular beside its colorbar; guard
7204  // `perfect_kernel_batch57::tabularray_tall_table_in_a_captionless_float`). The inner's caption stays
7205  // where it stood: after a first captioned panel it splits the row (the XSLT groups a figure's panels
7206  // between captions), as before the class (2605.01542 A3.F8; divergence #372).
7207  let inner_was_a_panel = beside_content
7208    && inner
7209      .get_attribute("class")
7210      .is_some_and(|classes| classes.split_whitespace().any(|c| c == "ltx_figure_panel"));
7211  // Replace inner element with its children, where it stood (Perl saves and re-appends the
7212  // following siblings, latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:3454-3462).
7213  let float_has_tags = has_child(float, tags_qname);
7214  let children: Vec<Node> = inner.get_child_nodes();
7215  for mut child in children {
7216    // decided before the move: libxml2 merges a moved text node into an adjacent one and frees it
7217    let panel = inner_was_a_panel && child.is_element_node() && {
7218      let qname = document::get_node_qname(&child);
7219      !is_panel_break_name(qname) && !with(qname, |q| matches!(q, "ltx:note" | "ltx:indexmark"))
7220    };
7221    child.unlink_node();
7222    // (a panel's width there was a fraction of the inner's line, not the float's: dropped beside other content, the
7223    // inner a panel of the float or not — beside content of no width it was the float's only panel, its children then
7224    // the float's, review rev79c finding 3; a lone inner's grid, its widths with it, is the float's)
7225    if beside_content && child.is_element_node() {
7226      for attribute in ["panelwidth", "panelspan"] {
7227        child.remove_attribute(attribute).ok();
7228      }
7229    }
7230    // The number an inner float brings to a float without one (a captioned minipage beside other content,
7231    // `end_caption_box`) heads it, where a float's own template puts its tags.
7232    if !float_has_tags
7233      && document::get_node_qname(&child) == tags_qname
7234      && let Some(mut first) = float.get_first_element_child()
7235    {
7236      first.add_prev_sibling(&mut child).ok();
7237      continue;
7238    }
7239    inner.add_prev_sibling(&mut child).ok();
7240    if panel {
7241      document.add_class(&mut child, "ltx_figure_panel")?;
7242    }
7243  }
7244  document.safe_unlink(inner);
7245  Ok(())
7246}

7248/// Perl: tabbingBindings() — sets up alignment with repeated template and rebinds control chars
7249fn tabbing_bindings() -> Result<()> {
7250  // Template: repeated column with before=\lx@text@intercol, after=\hfil\lx@text@intercol
7251  let col = Cell {
7252    before: Some(Tokens::new(vec![T_CS!("\\lx@text@intercol")])),
7253    after: Some(Tokens::new(vec![
7254      T_CS!("\\hfil"),
7255      T_CS!("\\lx@text@intercol"),
7256    ])),
7257    empty: true,
7258    ..Cell::default()
7259  };
7260  let template = Template::new(TemplateConfig {
7261    repeated: vec![col],
7262    ..TemplateConfig::default()
7263  });
7264
7265  let mut xml_attrs = HashMap::default();
7266  xml_attrs.insert(String::from("class"), String::from("ltx_tabbing"));
7267
7268  // latex.ltx's tabbing is built from boxes, never `\halign` (tex_tables.rs `ALIGNMENT_WITHOUT_HALIGN`).
7269  let mut tabbing_properties = SymHashMap::default();
7270  tabbing_properties.insert(
7271    crate::tex_tables::ALIGNMENT_WITHOUT_HALIGN,
7272    Stored::Bool(true),
7273  );
7274  let alignment = Alignment::new(AlignmentConfig {
7275    template:        Some(template),
7276    open_container:  Rc::new(|document, props| {
7277      document
7278        .open_element("ltx:tabular", Some(props), None)
7279        .map(Some)
7280    }),
7281    close_container: Rc::new(|document| document.close_element("ltx:tabular")),
7282    open_row:        Rc::new(|document, props| {
7283      let str_props: HashMap<String, String> =
7284        props.into_iter().map(|(k, v)| (k, v.to_string())).collect();
7285      document
7286        .open_element("ltx:tr", Some(str_props), None)
7287        .and(Ok(()))
7288    }),
7289    close_row:       Rc::new(|document| document.close_element("ltx:tr")),
7290    open_column:     Rc::new(|document, props| {
7291      document.open_element("ltx:td", Some(props), None).map(Some)
7292    }),
7293    close_column:    Rc::new(|document| document.close_element("ltx:td")),
7294    is_math:         false,
7295    properties:      tabbing_properties,
7296    xml_attributes:  xml_attrs,
7297  });
7298  assign_alignment(alignment, None);
7299  clear_alignment_row_hooks();
7300
7301  // Rebind control characters within tabbing
7302  // Perl: Let("\\=", '\@tabbing@tabset') etc.
7303  // latex.ltx:10005 `\@tabacckludge#1` = `\@changed@cmd\csname\string#1
7304  // \endcsname\relax` recovers the ENCODING-level accent by name, so `\a=`,
7305  // `\a<`, `\a>` still accent although `\=`/`\<`/`\>` are tab operators
7306  // inside tabbing (encguide `\a=o`; greek-fontenc test-lgrenc/textalpha-doc
7307  // `\a<`; Perl pool:3572 saves only `'` and `` ` ``). Save every rebound
7308  // accent BEFORE rebinding it. Guard:
7309  // `perfect_kernel_batch54::tabbing_accent_kludge_recovers_rebound_accents`.
7310  let_i(&T_CS!("\\@tabbing@="), &T_CS!("\\="), None);
7311  let_i(&T_CS!("\\@tabbing@<"), &T_CS!("\\<"), None);
7312  let_i(&T_CS!("\\@tabbing@>"), &T_CS!("\\>"), None);
7313  let_i(&T_CS!("\\="), &T_CS!("\\@tabbing@tabset"), None);
7314  let_i(&T_CS!("\\>"), &T_CS!("\\@tabbing@nexttab"), None);
7315  let_i(&T_CS!("\\\\"), &T_CS!("\\@tabbing@newline"), None);
7316  let_i(&T_CS!("\\kill"), &T_CS!("\\@tabbing@kill"), None);
7317  let_i(&T_CS!("\\+"), &T_CS!("\\@tabbing@increment"), None);
7318  let_i(&T_CS!("\\-"), &T_CS!("\\@tabbing@decrement"), None);
7319  let_i(&T_CS!("\\<"), &T_CS!("\\@tabbing@untab"), None);
7320  // Save accent definitions before rebinding \' and \`
7321  let_i(&T_CS!("\\@tabbing@'"), &T_CS!("\\'"), None);
7322  let_i(&T_CS!("\\@tabbing@`"), &T_CS!("\\`"), None);
7323  let_i(&T_CS!("\\a"), &T_CS!("\\@tabbing@accent"), None);
7324  // Rebind \' and \` to tabbing-specific (flush right / hfil)
7325  let_i(&T_CS!("\\'"), &T_CS!("\\@tabbing@flushright"), None);
7326  let_i(&T_CS!("\\`"), &T_CS!("\\@tabbing@hfil"), None);
7327  let_i(&T_CS!("\\pushtabs"), &T_CS!("\\@tabbing@pushtabs"), None);
7328  let_i(&T_CS!("\\poptabs"), &T_CS!("\\@tabbing@poptabs"), None);
7329
7330  Ok(())
7331}

7333pub fn note_backmatter_element(whatsit: &mut Whatsit, backelement: &str) {
7334  if let Some(val) = lookup_mapping("BACKMATTER_ELEMENT", backelement) {
7335    whatsit.set_property("backmatterelement", val);
7336    whatsit.set_property("backmatterself", pin(backelement));
7337  }
7338}
7339
7340/// Where a backmatter element (`ltx:bibliography`, `ltx:index`, a section
7341/// declared backmatter) goes: at the point its `BACKMATTER_ELEMENT` stand-in
7342/// (`ltx:section` by default) would be inserted — UNLESS no open node can
7343/// reach that stand-in without closing a `_noautoclose` container, in which
7344/// case the element is placed where IT is legal. A `\bibliography` inside a
7345/// beamer frame (an `ltx:subsection` that never auto-closes) is the case:
7346/// asking for `ltx:section` there erred `<ltx:section> isn't allowed in
7347/// <ltx:p>` and left the bibliography inside the `<p>` (metropolis demo,
7348/// simpleplus/simpledarkblue/pure-minimalistic samples, gotham), while the
7349/// subsection itself may hold an `ltx:bibliography` — which is also what
7350/// beamer typesets: the references on that slide. Perl's
7351/// adjustBackmatterElement (pool:3843) has no fallback. Guard:
7352/// `perfect_kernel_batch54::bibliography_inside_a_beamer_frame_stays_in_the_frame`.
7353fn backmatter_insertion_target(document: &Document, asif: &str, element: &str) -> String {
7354  if !document.is_openable(asif) && document.is_openable(element) {
7355    element.to_string()
7356  } else {
7357    asif.to_string()
7358  }
7359}
7360
7361/// A backmatter element (`thebibliography`'s `ltx:bibliography`) begun inside a `{quote}`, `{quotation}` or `{verse}`
7362/// (the AAAI template's `\begin{quote}\begin{small}\bibliography{…}`): neither the unit it stands as nor the element
7363/// itself may go in an `ltx:quote` (LaTeXML-block.rnc `quote_model`), and the quote does not auto-close, so both erred
7364/// and the bibliography lost its place in the back matter. LaTeX's `thebibliography` is `\section*{\refname}` and a
7365/// `\list` (article.cls:565-584; book.cls, report.cls alike), typeset inside the quote's `\list` margins — the heading
7366/// and the list are the document's bibliography, the quote only indents it: the quotes in the way are closed when that
7367/// alone makes the bibliography's place reachable (`Document::close_quotes_blocking`, shared with a sectioning unit in a
7368/// quote). The quote's font changes (`\small`) are digested into the entries and stay. User ruling 2026-10-16
7369/// (OXIDIZED_DESIGN_DIVERGENCES #677); witnesses 2203.09193 1904.12066 1610.09996 2109.09861 2403.09260 1609.06434
7370/// (AAAI), astro-ph0410583 (quote), 1504.06728 (verse). Guard `perfect_kernel_batch69a::bibliography_in_a_quote_closes_the_quote`.
7371fn close_list_containers_before_backmatter(
7372  document: &mut Document,
7373  asif: &str,
7374  element: &str,
7375) -> Result<()> {
7376  if !document.is_openable(asif) && !document.is_openable(element) {
7377    document.close_quotes_blocking(&[pin(asif), pin(element)])?;
7378  }
7379  Ok(())
7380}
7381
7382pub fn adjust_backmatter_element(document: &mut Document, whatsit: &Whatsit) -> Result<()> {
7383  let asif_opt = match whatsit.get_property("backmatterelement").as_deref() {
7384    Some(Stored::String(asif_sym)) => Some(to_string(*asif_sym)),
7385    _ => None,
7386  };
7387  // Note: We allocate a string here, since
7388  // it looks like arena::with can deadlock with find_insertion_point
7389  // we may need a find_insertion_point_sym to avoid that...
7390  let element = match whatsit.get_property("backmatterself").as_deref() {
7391    Some(Stored::String(sym)) => to_string(*sym),
7392    _ => "ltx:bibliography".to_string(),
7393  };
7394  if let Some(asif) = asif_opt {
7395    close_list_containers_before_backmatter(document, &asif, &element)?;
7396    let mut target = backmatter_insertion_target(document, &asif, &element);
7397    // Where the unit it stands as would go cannot hold it — an inline sectional block, whose model is body content only
7398    // (a list item's or a float's sections, OXIDIZED_DESIGN_DIVERGENCES #189, then a `thebibliography` in it) — it goes
7399    // where it can go from here, inside the last unit. Decided before any node is closed.
7400    let mut ancestor = Some(document.get_node().clone());
7401    while let Some(node) = ancestor {
7402      if document::can_contain(&node, &target) {
7403        if document::get_node_qname(&node) == pin!("ltx:inline-sectional-block")
7404          && !document::can_contain(&node, &element)
7405        {
7406          target = element.clone();
7407        }
7408        break;
7409      }
7410      ancestor = node.get_parent();
7411    }
7412    let point = document.find_insertion_point(&target, None)?;
7413    document.set_node(&point);
7414  }
7415  Ok(())
7416}

7418// Do this before digesting the body of a bibliography
7419// Perl: beforeDigestBibliography in latex_constructs.pool.ltxml L3900
7420pub fn before_digest_bibliography() -> Result<()> {
7421  // The document body has begun: a sectionless letter's bibliography seals its frontmatter as a heading would
7422  // (`seal_digested_frontmatter`; a PRL body before its supplement, 2609.07332).
7423  seal_digested_frontmatter();
7424  AssignValue!("inPreamble" => false);
7425  Digest!("\\@lx@inbibliographytrue")?;
7426  // an explicit bibliography: not the lonely one a natbib `\bibitem` opened (sect11.rs `\lx@bibliography@lonely`)
7427  assign_value("lx_bibliography_lonely", false, Some(Scope::Global));
7428  // The list a heading inside the author's `{thebibliography}` interrupted (sect11.rs `\lx@bibliography@sectioned`)
7429  // goes on: its entries keep counting, as pdflatex numbers them through the one list.
7430  let continued = lookup_bool("lx_bibliography_sectioned");
7431  // whether this is the author's `{thebibliography}` (not one a `\bibitem` opened in another environment), for the
7432  // environment's group
7433  assign_value(
7434    "lx_bibliography_author_env",
7435    lookup_string("current_environment") == "thebibliography",
7436    None,
7437  );
7438  assign_value("lx_bibliography_sectioned", false, Some(Scope::Global));
7439  assign_value(
7440    "lx_bibliography_is_continued",
7441    continued,
7442    Some(Scope::Global),
7443  );
7444  // …whose number is that of the one it continues when that held no entry and is pruned (`begin_bibliography_clean`)
7445  let reuse_number = continued && lookup_bool("lx_bibliography_sectioned_empty");
7446  assign_value(
7447    "lx_bibliography_sectioned_empty",
7448    false,
7449    Some(Scope::Global),
7450  );
7451  assign_value(
7452    "lx_bibliography_reuse_number",
7453    reuse_number,
7454    Some(Scope::Global),
7455  );
7456  // …nor does natbib's pending entry stop of an earlier one (`\@bibstop`, natbib.sty:880-905) carry into its first entry
7457  Let!("\\@bibstop", "\\@undefined");
7458  // …and it has a list end of its own (sect11.rs `\lx@bibliography@nolistend`)
7459  assign_value("lx_bibliography_no_list_end", false, Some(Scope::Global));
7460  def_macro_noop("\\bibliographystyle{}")?;
7461  def_macro_noop("\\bibliography {}")?;
7462  // avoid \let-based redefinitions of the ending.
7463  Let!("\\endthebibliography", "\\saved@endthebibliography");
7464  if !continued {
7465    ResetCounter!("@bibitem");
7466  }
7467  Ok(())
7468}
