7470// Since SOME people seem to write bibliographies w/o \bibitem,
7471// just blank lines between apparent entries,
7472// Making \par do a \bibitem{} works, but screws up valid
7473// bibliographies with blank lines!
7474// So, let's do some redirection!
7475fn setup_pseudo_bibitem() -> Result<()> {
7476  // Capture the REAL meanings, but only once per arming. Perl
7477  // (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:setupPseudoBibitem L4028-4032) captures
7478  // unconditionally; if this runs while the redirection below is still
7479  // installed, all three saves capture the *redirectors* instead of the
7480  // originals — `\save@bibitem` becomes `\restoring@bibitem`, whose body ends
7481  // in `\bibitem`, which `\let\bibitem\save@bibitem` has just pointed back at
7482  // `\restoring@bibitem`. That is an unconditional infinite expansion loop
7483  // (`\let \bibitem \save@bibitem \let \par \save@par \let \\
7484  // \save@backbackslash \bibitem` forever), not a slow document.
7485  //
7486  // Perl has the identical hole — `\thebibliography \endthebibliography
7487  // \thebibliography \bibitem{b}` hangs Perl 0.8.8 too (>400 s on an 8-line
7488  // file that converts in <2 s otherwise); see KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #57. It stays
7489  // latent upstream only because Perl's biblatex binding never defines
7490  // `\printbibliography`, so Perl never reads a real `.bbl` this way.
7491  //
7492  // Rust's `.bbl` rebuilder used to reach it: a biber `.bbl` carries one
7493  // `\datalist` per sorting scheme (apa emits `nyt/apasortcite//…` *and*
7494  // `nyt/global//…`), and every `\enddatalist` expanded to a whole bare
7495  // `\thebibliography…\endthebibliography`, so the first arming was still in
7496  // force when the second opened. Witness: arXiv 2605.17646
7497  // (`Fatal:Timeout:TokenLimit`, 1e9 tokens). Since batch 56jc the `.bbl` is
7498  // read into bibentries instead; the hand-written bare pair stays guarded by
7499  // `bare_thebibliography_twice_arms_once`.
7500  if !x_equals(&T_CS!("\\bibitem"), &T_CS!("\\restoring@bibitem")) {
7501    Let!("\\save@bibitem", "\\bibitem");
7502    Let!("\\save@par", "\\par");
7503    Let!("\\save@backbackslash", "\\\\");
7504  }
7505  Let!("\\bibitem", "\\restoring@bibitem");
7506  Let!("\\par", "\\par@in@bibliography");
7507  Let!("\\\\", "\\par@in@bibliography");
7508  Let!("\\vskip", "\\vskip@in@bibliography");
7509  // Moreover some people use \item instead of \bibitem
7510  Let!("\\item", "\\item@in@bibliography");
7511  // And protect from redefinitions.
7512  Let!("\\newblock", "\\lx@bibnewblock");
7513  // Risky, but when bibliography immediatesly starts with text (no implied \par)
7514  if let Some(token) = read_non_space()? {
7515    unread_one(token);
7516    if !token.is_executable() {
7517      unread_one(T_CS!("\\par"));
7518    }
7519  }
7520  Ok(())
7521}
7522/// What a package typesets between a bibliography's heading and its list (`\lx@bibliography@preamble`, sect11.rs),
7523/// digested after the heading into the bibliography's `#preamble` — before the list's `\bibitem` redirection is armed.
7524pub fn digest_bibliography_preamble(whatsit: &mut Whatsit) -> Result<()> {
7525  let preamble = Digest!(T_CS!("\\lx@bibliography@preamble"))?;
7526  if !preamble.is_empty()? {
7527    whatsit.set_property("preamble", preamble);
7528  }
7529  Ok(())
7530}
7531
7532// This sub does things that would commonly be needed when starting a bibliography
7533// setting the ID, etc...
7534pub fn begin_bibliography(whatsit: &mut Whatsit) -> Result<()> {
7535  begin_bibliography_clean(whatsit)?;
7536  // Fix for missing \bibitems!
7537  setup_pseudo_bibitem()
7538}
7539
7540pub fn begin_bibliography_clean(whatsit: &mut Whatsit) -> Result<()> {
7541  // Check if \bibsection is defined and try to decipher it.
7542  // Expecting something like \section*{sometext}
7543  // Perl: beginBibliography_clean in latex_constructs.pool.ltxml
7544  let mut bibtitle: Option<Tokens> = None;
7545  if let Some(bs) = lookup_definition(&T_CS!("\\bibsection"))?
7546    && bs.is_expandable()
7547    && let Some(ExpansionBody::Tokens(expansion_toks)) = bs.get_expansion()
7548  {
7549    let mut tokens = expansion_toks.clone().unlist();
7550    if !tokens.is_empty() {
7551      let bibunitmap: &[(&str, &str)] = &[
7552        ("\\part", "ltx:part"),
7553        ("\\chapter", "ltx:chapter"),
7554        ("\\section", "ltx:section"),
7555        ("\\subsection", "ltx:subsection"),
7556        ("\\subsubsection", "ltx:subsubsection"),
7557        ("\\paragraph", "ltx:paragraph"),
7558        ("\\subparagraph", "ltx:subparagraph"),
7559      ];
7560      let first_cs = tokens.remove(0).to_string();
7561      if let Some((_, unit)) = bibunitmap.iter().find(|(cs, _)| *cs == first_cs) {
7562        assign_mapping("BACKMATTER_ELEMENT", "ltx:bibliography", Some(pin(unit)));
7563        // Strip * if present
7564        if !tokens.is_empty() && tokens[0].text == pin!("*") {
7565          tokens.remove(0);
7566        }
7567        if !tokens.is_empty() {
7568          // Perl L4052 flags a TODO right here: "Check for balanced? or
7569          // just take balanced begining?" — i.e. the bib-section title is
7570          // the sectional unit's *argument* (the leading brace group), not
7571          // every trailing token. Perl nonetheless takes all of @t, which
7572          // is fine until \bibsection is a parameterized renewal such as
7573          //   \renewcommand\bibsection[1]{\section*{\refname}\small #1}
7574          // (witness 1702.01165). After the unit+star strip that leaves
7575          // `{\refname}\small #1`; digesting all of it pushes the page/font
7576          // directive `\small` AND the bare parameter token `#1` — an
7577          // ARG-catcode token that errors "should never reach Stomach!".
7578          // Take only the leading balanced {...} group as the title (the
7579          // unit argument); fall back to all tokens when there is no
7580          // leading group (Perl's behavior for un-braced titles). This
7581          // realizes the Perl author's own "take balanced beginning" note
7582          // and drops trailing page/font junk LaTeXML never renders. See
7583          // docs/parity/OXIDIZED_DESIGN.md (bib-section title = leading group).
7584          let title_toks = if tokens[0].get_catcode() == Catcode::BEGIN {
7585            let mut depth = 0i32;
7586            let mut end = tokens.len();
7587            for (i, t) in tokens.iter().enumerate() {
7588              match t.get_catcode() {
7589                Catcode::BEGIN => depth += 1,
7590                Catcode::END => {
7591                  depth -= 1;
7592                  if depth == 0 {
7593                    end = i + 1;
7594                    break;
7595                  }
7596                },
7597                _ => {},
7598              }
7599            }
7600            tokens[..end].to_vec()
7601          } else {
7602            tokens
7603          };
7604          bibtitle = Some(Tokens::new(title_toks));
7605        }
7606      }
7607    }
7608  }
7609
7610  note_backmatter_element(whatsit, "ltx:bibliography");
7611  // Try to compute a reasonable, but unique ID;
7612  // relative to the document's ID, if any.
7613  // But also, if there are multiple bibliographies,
7614  // (the continuation of a bibliography a heading interrupted before its first entry takes that one's number, and the
7615  // id `prune_interrupted_bibliography` frees with it, sect11.rs `\lx@bibliography@sectioned`; Rust-only, as the
7616  // continuation is, OXIDIZED_DESIGN_DIVERGENCES #653)
7617  let reuse_number = lookup_bool("lx_bibliography_reuse_number");
7618  if reuse_number {
7619    assign_value("lx_bibliography_reuse_number", false, Some(Scope::Global));
7620  }
7621  let bibnumber = match lookup_int("n_bibliographies") {
7622    n if reuse_number && n > 0 => n,
7623    n => 1 + n,
7624  };
7625  assign_value("n_bibliographies", bibnumber, Some(Scope::Global));
7626  let mut docid: String = Expand!(T_CS!("\\thedocument@ID")).to_string();
7627  if !docid.is_empty() {
7628    docid += ".";
7629  }
7630  let bibid = s!("{}bib{}", docid, radix::radix_alpha(bibnumber - 1));
7631  DefMacro!(T_CS!("\\thebibliography@ID"), None, T_OTHER!(&bibid), scope => Some(Scope::Global));
7632  // Perl L3939 — child ID prefixes (e.g., `\the@bibitem@ID`) chain off the
7633  // parent counter's `@ID` macro. With parent counter `@lx@bibliography`,
7634  // child IDs derive from `\the@lx@bibliography@ID`. Mirror Perl exactly.
7635  DefMacro!(T_CS!("\\the@lx@bibliography@ID"), None, T_OTHER!(&bibid), scope => Some(Scope::Global));
7636  whatsit.set_property("id", bibid);
7637  // A package's title for this bibliography (`\lx@bibliography@title`, sect11.rs: biblatex's `title=`) outranks
7638  // the sectioning default; it names the title, so it may itself be `\refname`.
7639  let hook_title = match DigestIf!("\\lx@bibliography@title")? {
7640    Some(title) if !title.is_empty()? => Some(title),
7641    _ => None,
7642  };
7643  let title_opt = if hook_title.is_some() {
7644    hook_title
7645  } else if let Some(bt) = bibtitle {
7646    Some(Digest!(bt)?)
7647  } else {
7648    match digest_in_group_if(T_CS!("\\refname"))? {
7649      Some(v) => Some(v),
7650      None => digest_in_group_if(T_CS!("\\bibname"))?,
7651    }
7652  };
7653  if let Some(title) = title_opt {
7654    if let Some(titlefont) = title.get_font()? {
7655      whatsit.set_property("titlefont", titlefont);
7656    }
7657    whatsit.set_property("title", title);
7658  }
7659  if let Some(bs) = lookup_value("BIBSTYLE") {
7660    whatsit.set_property("bibstyle", bs);
7661  }
7662  if let Some(cs) = lookup_value("CITE_STYLE") {
7663    whatsit.set_property("citestyle", cs);
7664  }
7665  // The style's order (`setBibstyle`'s CITE_SORT), the one fact post numbers by: Perl leaves `#sort` unset here
7666  // (pool:3890 `# sort=> ???`) and writes it only late (:3979). OXIDIZED_DESIGN_DIVERGENCES #116.
7667  if let Some(sort) = lookup_value("CITE_SORT") {
7668    whatsit.set_property("sort", sort);
7669  }
7670  // And prepare for the likely nonsense that appears within bibliographies: the classes' `thebibliography`
7671  // (article.cls:573) runs `\usecounter{enumiv}` (latex.ltx:16048), which also names the list's counter; asl.cls's
7672  // entries read `\value{\@listctr}` (1005.4193, 0705.0395). Perl's never names it (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1230).
7673  // Not `\@nmbrlisttrue`: our `\bibitem` steps no enumiv, so a raw `\@trivlist` numbered from it would invent "0A".
7674  ResetCounter!("enumiv");
7675  Digest!(TokenizeInternal!(r"\def\@listctr{enumiv}"))?;
7676  Ok(())
7677}
7678
7679// Perl: $BIBSTYLES hash — maps bib style names to (citestyle, sort) pairs
7680// (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml L3953-3961). `sort => 'false'` is bibtex's own
7681// "leave in citation order" flag; MakeBibliography honors it (html_feedback
7682// #6294) to number the References the way the `.bst` — and the PDF — do.
7683fn lookup_bibstyle_params(style: &str) -> Option<(&'static str, &'static str)> {
7684  match style {
7685    "plain" => Some(("numbers", "true")),
7686    "unsrt" => Some(("numbers", "false")),
7687    "alpha" => Some(("AY", "true")),
7688    "abbrv" => Some(("numbers", "true")),
7689    "plainnat" => Some(("numbers", "true")),
7690    // jurabib's styles (each `.bst`'s SORT): author-year, sorted but for jurunsrt.
7691    "jurabib" | "jox" | "jureco" => Some(("authoryear", "true")),
7692    "jurunsrt" => Some(("authoryear", "false")),
7693    "unsrtnat" => Some(("numbers", "false")),
7694    "alphanat" => Some(("AY", "true")),
7695    "abbrvnat" => Some(("numbers", "true")),
7696    // Surpass-Perl: the real `ieeetr.bst`/`IEEEtran.bst` are UNSORTED (number by
7697    // first citation). Perl's base table omits them and `IEEEtran.cls.ltxml`
7698    // L331 even maps `IEEEtran → sort='true'` — both alphabetize, contradicting
7699    // the `.bst` and the published PDF. Map them to citation order to match the
7700    // ground-truth PDF (witness arXiv 2510.05438). See OXIDIZED_DESIGN.
7701    "ieeetr" => Some(("numbers", "false")),
7702    "IEEEtran" => Some(("numbers", "false")),
7703    // abnTeX2's two styles (the abntex2cite binding records its default at load):
7704    // abntex2-num.bst's `presort` drops the sort key "such that SORT has no effect"
7705    // (:2021-2022), so it numbers by first citation; abntex2-alf.bst sorts by author and
7706    // cites author-year ("(FARIA, 1994)").
7707    "abntex2-num" => Some(("numbers", "false")),
7708    "abntex2-alf" => Some(("authoryear", "true")),
7709    // figbib.bst (READ, ITERATE {call.type$}) has no SORT: its figure list is in citation order.
7710    "figbib" => Some(("numbers", "false")),
7711    _ => None,
7712  }
7713}
7714
7715/// `\bibliographystyle`'s record where a package may have taken `\bibstyle` (natbib's `\@gobble`): the style's name
7716/// and its list order (`CITE_SORT`) together, never `CITE_STYLE`, which that package owns.
7717pub fn record_bibstyle(style: &str, scope: Option<Scope>) {
7718  if let Some((_, sort)) = lookup_bibstyle_params(style) {
7719    assign_value("CITE_SORT", pin(sort), scope);
7720  }
7721  assign_value("BIBSTYLE", pin(style), scope);
7722}
7723
7724// Perl: setBibstyle($style) — set BIBSTYLE, CITE_STYLE, CITE_SORT
7725pub fn set_bibstyle(style: &str) {
7726  assign_value("BIBSTYLE", pin(style), None);
7727  if let Some((cs, so)) = lookup_bibstyle_params(style) {
7728    assign_value("CITE_STYLE", pin(cs), None);
7729    assign_value("CITE_SORT", pin(so), None);
7730  }
7731}

7733/// Perl: addIndexPhraseKey — sets the `key` attribute on index/glossary phrase
7734/// nodes from their text content, applying CleanIndexKey normalization.
7735fn add_index_phrase_key(node: &mut Node) -> Result<()> {
7736  if node.get_attribute("key").is_none() {
7737    let text = node.get_content();
7738    let key = clean_index_key(&text);
7739    if !key.is_empty() {
7740      node.set_attribute("key", &key)?;
7741    }
7742  }
7743  Ok(())
7744}
7745/// Perl: doIndexItem — open/close index list levels.
7746fn do_index_item(document: &mut Document, level: i64) -> Result<()> {
7747  if document.is_closeable("ltx:indexrefs").is_some() {
7748    document.close_element("ltx:indexrefs")?;
7749  }
7750  if document.is_closeable("ltx:indexphrase").is_some() {
7751    document.close_element("ltx:indexphrase")?;
7752  }
7753  let current_level = lookup_int("INDEXLEVEL");
7754  let mut l = current_level;
7755  while l < level {
7756    document.open_element("ltx:indexlist", None, None)?;
7757    l += 1;
7758  }
7759  while l > level {
7760    document.close_element("ltx:indexlist")?;
7761    l -= 1;
7762  }
7763  assign_value("INDEXLEVEL", Stored::Int(l), Some(Scope::Local));
7764  if level > 0 {
7765    document.open_element("ltx:indexentry", None, None)?;
7766    document.open_element("ltx:indexphrase", None, None)?;
7767  }
7768  Ok(())
7769}
7770
7771/// Perl: CleanIndexKey — trim whitespace, remove trailing punctuation.
7772/// Additionally strips ONE outer brace pair spanning the whole key — the
7773/// wrapper process_index_phrases adds to protect `]`-bearing sort keys
7774/// (never strips a pair that closes mid-string, so `{a}{b}` survives).
7775fn clean_index_key(key: &str) -> String {
7776  let mut key = key.trim();
7777  if key.len() >= 2 && key.starts_with('{') && key.ends_with('}') {
7778    let inner = &key[1..key.len() - 1];
7779    let mut depth = 0i32;
7780    if inner.chars().all(|c| {
7781      match c {
7782        '{' => depth += 1,
7783        '}' => depth -= 1,
7784        _ => {},
7785      }
7786      depth >= 0
7787    }) && depth == 0
7788    {
7789      key = inner.trim();
7790    }
7791  }
7792  key.trim_end_matches(['.', ',', ';']).to_string()
7793}
7794/// The kernel's `env/<name>/<point>` hook call, in its own token shapes:
7795/// bare `\UseHook{env/#1/<point>}` for before/begin/after
7796/// (latex.ltx:15347/15362/15391) and, for `end`,
7797/// `\romannumeral\IfHookEmptyTF{env/#1/end}{\expandafter\z@}{\z@\UseHook
7798/// {env/#1/end}}` (:15386-15388): an empty hook vanishes at EXPANSION time,
7799/// so nothing sits between an alignment's last cell and `\endtabular`'s
7800/// implicit `\crcr` (a trailing `\multicolumn` row leaked its group when an
7801/// unexpandable token stood there). Emitted only when the L3 hook system
7802/// exists and reports code for the hook (its own `\IfHookEmptyTF`,
7803/// dialect.rs): with no hook there is nothing to fire, and a line-reading
7804/// environment (comment.sty) must not see extra tokens at its `\end`.
7805pub(crate) fn env_hook_tokens(name: &str, point: &str) -> Vec<Token> {
7806  if !env_hook_has_code(name, point) {
7807    return Vec::new();
7808  }
7809  let hook = |v: &mut Vec<Token>| {
7810    v.push(T_CS!("\\UseHook"));
7811    v.push(T_BEGIN!());
7812    v.extend(ExplodeText!(s!("env/{name}/{point}")));
7813    v.push(T_END!());
7814  };
7815  let mut v = Vec::new();
7816  if point == "end" {
7817    v.push(T_CS!("\\romannumeral"));
7818    v.push(T_CS!("\\IfHookEmptyTF"));
7819    v.push(T_BEGIN!());
7820    v.extend(ExplodeText!(s!("env/{name}/end")));
7821    v.push(T_END!());
7822    v.extend([T_BEGIN!(), T_CS!("\\expandafter"), T_CS!("\\z@"), T_END!()]);
7823    v.push(T_BEGIN!());
7824    v.push(T_CS!("\\z@"));
7825    hook(&mut v);
7826    v.push(T_END!());
7827  } else {
7828    hook(&mut v);
7829  }
7830  v
7831}
7832
7833/// LaTeX's `\begin{name}` for an environment defined by macros
7834/// (latex.ltx:15346-15364): the `before` hook outside the group, then inside
7835/// it `\@currenvir`, the `begin` hook and `\name` — `\begin`'s path whenever
7836/// no `\begin{name}` constructor is defined. `env` is the name as written.
7837pub(crate) fn begin_environment_by_macro(name: &str, env: Tokens) -> Result<Vec<Token>> {
7838  let mut out = lookup_tokens(&format!("@environment@{name}@beforebegin"))
7839    .map(Tokens::unlist)
7840    .unwrap_or_default();
7841  out.extend(env_hook_tokens(name, "before"));
7842  out.push(T_CS!("\\begingroup"));
7843  if let Some(after) = lookup_tokens(&format!("@environment@{name}@atbegin")) {
7844    out.extend(after.unlist());
7845  }
7846  out.extend(Invocation!(T_CS!("\\lx@setcurrenvir"), vec![env]).unlist());
7847  out.extend(env_hook_tokens(name, "begin"));
7848  out.push(T_CS!(format!("\\{name}")));
7849  Ok(out)
7850}
7851
7852/// LaTeX's `\end{name}` for an environment defined by macros
7853/// (latex.ltx:15386-15391): the `end` hook inside the group before
7854/// `\endname`, the `after` hook after the `\endgroup`. The epilogue `\end`
7855/// shares with every path (`\if@ignore…\fi`) is the caller's.
7856pub(crate) fn end_environment_by_macro(name: &str) -> Vec<Token> {
7857  let mut out = lookup_tokens(&format!("@environment@{name}@atend"))
7858    .map(Tokens::unlist)
7859    .unwrap_or_default();
7860  out.extend(env_hook_tokens(name, "end"));
7861  let end = T_CS!(format!("\\end{name}"));
7862  if is_defined_token(&end) {
7863    out.push(end);
7864  }
7865  // latex.ltx:15389 `\@checkend{#1}` before the `\endgroup`. Not for a
7866  // nameless `\end` (AMS-TeX's document end read as LaTeX's `\end`, 0902.2535,
7867  // alg-geom9410004): there `\end` + "" is `\end` itself, which would take
7868  // `\lx@checkend` as its argument, as TeX's `\end` would take `\@checkend`,
7869  // and leave `{}` behind. A nameless `\end` names no environment to check;
7870  // skipping it is this binding's choice (no latex.ltx or tex.web rule), kept
7871  // because the doubled diagnostic carries nothing (cond-mat9211014 shows the
7872  // same capture through a `\let\endX\end`, which is left as TeX does it).
7873  if !name.is_empty() {
7874    out.push(T_CS!("\\lx@checkend"));
7875    out.push(T_BEGIN!());
7876    out.extend(Explode!(name));
7877    out.push(T_END!());
7878  }
7879  out.push(T_CS!("\\endgroup"));
7880  out.extend(env_hook_tokens(name, "after"));
7881  if let Some(afterend) = lookup_tokens(&format!("@environment@{name}@afterend")) {
7882    out.extend(afterend.unlist());
7883  }
7884  out
7885}
7886
7887/// The makeindex characters an entry is written with: makeindex(1)'s style
7888/// keys `level`, `actual`, `encap` and `quote` (defaults `!`, `@`, `|`, `"`).
7889/// A document that writes its entries for a style of its own declares them:
7890/// doc.sty:521-524 defines `\levelchar` `>`, `\actualchar` `=`, `\encapchar`
7891/// `|` and `\quotechar` `!` to match gind.ist/gglo.ist and assembles every
7892/// `\index`/`\glossary` entry from those macros (doc.sty:626-650, 1054-1093);
7893/// amsldoc.cls:74-77 and tvz-user.sty:99-102 spell out makeindex's defaults
7894/// the same way. Split with the defaults, each doc.sty entry stayed ONE
7895/// phrase (`foo=\verb!*+\foo+`, `v1.0>!!=General:>…`); split with the
7896/// characters in force it parses as the pdflatex + makeindex run does.
7897#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
7898pub(crate) struct IndexChars {
7899  level:  String,
7900  actual: String,
7901  encap:  String,
7902  quote:  String,
7903}
7904
7905/// The macros a writer spells its makeindex characters with (doc.sty:521-524).
7906const INDEX_CHAR_MACROS: [&str; 4] = ["\\levelchar", "\\actualchar", "\\encapchar", "\\quotechar"];
7907
7908impl IndexChars {
7909  /// makeindex's own characters: `!`, `@`, `|`, `"`.
7910  pub(crate) fn makeindex_default() -> Self {
7911    IndexChars {
7912      level:  "!".to_string(),
7913      actual: "@".to_string(),
7914      encap:  "|".to_string(),
7915      quote:  "\"".to_string(),
7916    }
7917  }
7918
7919  /// The characters an `\index` entry was written with. The style is chosen
7920  /// per index FILE, outside the document (`makeindex -s gind.ist`), and one
7921  /// document can hold entries of both kinds: keytheorems-doc and
7922  /// csvsimple-l3 load doc.sty (through ltxdoc) but index with tcolorbox's
7923  /// documentation library, which writes makeindex's defaults
7924  /// (tcbdocumentation.code.tex:214 `index default settings`: `@`) for a
7925  /// default `makeindex` run; read in doc's characters their sort keys were
7926  /// never split off and raised `Script _`. So an entry is read in the
7927  /// declared characters only when it shows them — spelled with
7928  /// `\levelchar` & co., as every doc.sty writer's entry is (doc.sty:541,
7929  /// 1054-1093; hypdoc.sty:351; amsldoc.cls:88), or holding the declared
7930  /// actual character itself at its top level, as nlctdoc.cls:496-570 writes
7931  /// `\index{#1=\appfmt{#1}…}` for its own style (nlctdoc.cls:140-150) — and
7932  /// in makeindex's defaults otherwise.
7933  pub(crate) fn for_index_entry(entry: &Tokens) -> Self {
7934    let declared = Self::in_force();
7935    let default = Self::makeindex_default();
7936    if declared == default {
7937      return default;
7938    }
7939    let mut depth = 0i32;
7940    let mut in_math = false;
7941    for t in entry.unlist_ref() {
7942      match t.get_catcode() {
7943        Catcode::BEGIN => depth += 1,
7944        Catcode::END => depth -= 1,
7945        Catcode::MATH if depth == 0 => in_math = !in_math,
7946        Catcode::CS if t.with_str(|s| INDEX_CHAR_MACROS.contains(&s)) => return declared,
7947        _ => {},
7948      }
7949      if depth == 0
7950        && !in_math
7951        && declared.actual != default.actual
7952        && t.get_catcode() != Catcode::CS
7953        && t.with_str(|s| s == declared.actual)
7954      {
7955        return declared;
7956      }
7957    }
7958    default
7959  }
7960
7961  /// The characters in force. Each of `\levelchar`, `\actualchar`,
7962  /// `\encapchar` and `\quotechar` that is a parameterless macro whose body
7963  /// is one character overrides makeindex's default for its key. (hypdoc
7964  /// re-`\def`s `\encapchar` WITH parameters inside its own writers,
7965  /// hypdoc.sty:344-353 — no declaration; the default stands.) A `\glossary`
7966  /// entry is always read in them: the `.glo` file needs a style that names
7967  /// its `\glossaryentry` keyword (gglo.ist `keyword`), and doc.sty's
7968  /// `\changes` expands the characters into the entry before writing it
7969  /// (doc.sty:627 `\protected@edef`), so they leave no spelling to see.
7970  pub(crate) fn in_force() -> Self {
7971    let default = Self::makeindex_default();
7972    let pick = |cs: &str, default: String| declared_index_char(cs).unwrap_or(default);
7973    IndexChars {
7974      level:  pick("\\levelchar", default.level),
7975      actual: pick("\\actualchar", default.actual),
7976      encap:  pick("\\encapchar", default.encap),
7977      quote:  pick("\\quotechar", default.quote),
7978    }
7979  }
7980}
7981
7982/// The one character a `\def\levelchar{>}`-style declaration stands for.
7983fn declared_index_char(cs: &str) -> Option<String> {
7984  let defn = lookup_definition(&T_CS!(cs)).ok()??;
7985  if !defn.is_expandable()
7986    || defn
7987      .get_parameters()
7988      .is_some_and(|p| !p.get_parameters().is_empty())
7989  {
7990    return None;
7991  }
7992  match defn.get_expansion() {
7993    Some(ExpansionBody::Tokens(body)) => match body.unlist_ref().as_slice() {
7994      [t] if !t.get_catcode().is_active_or_cs() => Some(t.with_str(|s| s.to_string())),
7995      _ => None,
7996    },
7997    _ => None,
7998  }
7999}
8000
8001/// The next token of a `\verb` run as the `.ind` re-read receives it. A
8002/// control sequence is EXPANDED, as `\protected@write` expands a
8003/// macro-assembled entry (doc.sty's `\verb\quotechar*\verbatimchar…`;
8004/// l3doc.cls:2151 `\verbatimchar` = `&`, an unexpanded `&` is a stray
8005/// alignment tab — ltx-talk, postnotes, pythonimmediate). Returns the token,
8006/// the unconsumed rest, and whether a macro supplied it; None when nothing is
8007/// left. A failed expansion is the caller's error.
8008fn written_index_token(toks: Vec<Token>) -> Result<Option<(Token, Vec<Token>, bool)>> {
8009  let Some(first) = toks.first().copied() else {
8010    return Ok(None);
8011  };
8012  if first.get_catcode() != Catcode::CS {
8013    return Ok(Some((first, toks[1..].to_vec(), false)));
8014  }
8015  let tail = Tokens::new(toks);
8016  let expanded: Result<(Option<Token>, Vec<Token>)> =
8017    reading_from_mouth(Mouth::new("", None).expect("empty mouth"), move || {
8018      unread(tail);
8019      let first = read_x_token(None, false, None)?;
8020      let mut remaining = Vec::new();
8021      while let Some(t) = read_token()? {
8022        remaining.push(t);
8023      }
8024      Ok((first, remaining))
8025    });
8026  let (first, remaining) = expanded?;
8027  Ok(first.map(|t| (t, remaining, true)))
8028}
8029
8030/// [`written_index_token`] after makeindex has read it: the QUOTE character
8031/// takes the next character literally and is dropped (makeindex(1) `quote`),
8032/// so doc.sty's `\verb!*+\foo+` is `\verb*+\foo+` and lshort's
8033/// `\index{^@\verb"|^"|}` is `\verb|^|` (lshort-*/math.tex; real makeindex
8034/// output checked).
8035fn unquoted_index_token(
8036  toks: Vec<Token>,
8037  chars: &IndexChars,
8038) -> Result<Option<(Token, Vec<Token>, bool)>> {
8039  let Some((t, rest, from_macro)) = written_index_token(toks)? else {
8040    return Ok(None);
8041  };
8042  if t.get_catcode() != Catcode::CS && t.with_str(|s| s == chars.quote) && !rest.is_empty() {
8043    return Ok(
8044      written_index_token(rest)?
8045        .map(|(quoted, rest, quoted_from_macro)| (quoted, rest, from_macro || quoted_from_macro)),
8046    );
8047  }
8048  Ok(Some((t, rest, from_macro)))
8049}
8050
8051/// A `\verb` body as makeindex hands it on: the quote character is dropped
8052/// and makes the next character literal — a quoted delimiter still closes
8053/// the run, since makeindex writes it out bare — and a control SYMBOL named
8054/// by the quote character is makeindex's ESCAPE rule (`\"` stays `\"`, the
8055/// umlaut) unless the backslash is itself quoted: amsldoc.tex's
8056/// `\index{"|@\verb"*+"\"|+}` is `\verb*+\|+` (makeindex output checked).
8057/// The re-tokenization of the entry welded that `\` and `"` into one token.
8058struct IndexVerbBody<'q> {
8059  delim:  String,
8060  quote:  &'q str,
8061  quoted: bool,
8062  body:   Vec<Token>,
8063}
8064
8065impl IndexVerbBody<'_> {
8066  /// Take one written token; true when it closes the run.
8067  fn feed(&mut self, t: Token) -> bool {
8068    let is_cs = t.get_catcode() == Catcode::CS;
8069    let s = t.with_str(|s| s.to_string());
8070    if !self.quoted {
8071      if !is_cs && s == self.quote {
8072        self.quoted = true;
8073        return false;
8074      }
8075    } else if is_cs && s.strip_prefix('\\') == Some(self.quote) {
8076      self.body.push(T_OTHER!("\\"));
8077      return false;
8078    }
8079    self.quoted = false;
8080    if s == self.delim {
8081      return true;
8082    }
8083    self.body.push(t);
8084    false
8085  }
8086}
8087
8088/// The script characters of an entry's display as the `.ind`/`.gls` re-read
8089/// gives them. The entry was re-tokenized with the internal catcodes (`_`
8090/// subscript, `^` superscript); makeindex's output is read back in the
8091/// document, where underscore.sty makes `_` active (underscore.sty:29-31,
8092/// `\catcode`_\active` at begin document; l3doc.cls:432 loads it): active in
8093/// the document, the character is active here too. Outside math, where the
8094/// entry was read under a `\@sanitize` (doc.sty's `\changes`, :626-650) or the
8095/// document made the character text, it is the text character — an other `_`
8096/// would print through OT1's slot as `˙`. lt3graph's `\changes{…}{…}{\texttt{
8097/// \textbackslash graph_(g)put_vertex}}` prints `\graph_(g)put_vertex` (golden
8098/// lt3graph.pdf) where the subscript raised `Script _ can only appear in math
8099/// mode`. A subscript `_` of the document stays one, in math and out (pdflatex
8100/// reports the latter too).
8101fn reread_script_chars(phrase: Vec<Token>) -> Vec<Token> {
8102  let mut in_math = false;
8103  phrase
8104    .into_iter()
8105    .map(|t| {
8106      let cc = t.get_catcode();
8107      if cc == Catcode::MATH {
8108        in_math = !in_math;
8109      }
8110      if cc != Catcode::SUB && cc != Catcode::SUPER {
8111        return t;
8112      }
8113      let Some(c) = t.with_str(|s| {
8114        let mut chars = s.chars();
8115        chars.next().filter(|_| chars.next().is_none())
8116      }) else {
8117        return t;
8118      };
8119      match lookup_catcode(c) {
8120        Some(Catcode::ACTIVE) => T_ACTIVE!(c),
8121        Some(Catcode::SUB | Catcode::SUPER) | None => t,
8122        Some(_) if in_math => t,
8123        Some(_) if cc == Catcode::SUB => T_CS!("\\textunderscore"),
8124        Some(_) => T_CS!("\\textasciicircum"),
8125      }
8126    })
8127    .collect()
8128}
8129
8130/// Perl: process_index_phrases — expand \index{a!b@c|see{d}} into
8131/// \@index{\@indexphrase{a}\@indexphrase[c]{b}} etc.
8132///
8133/// Port of latex_constructs.pool.ltxml L4528-4591
8134/// #354 surpass (OXIDIZED_DESIGN #119): a `\verb`/`\verb*` inside `\index`.
8135/// `\index` reads its argument `SanitizedVerbatim` and re-reads it (`reread_sanitized_entry`) —
8136/// collapsing `\verb`'s raw body back into control sequences (`\delta`, not
8137/// `\`,`d`,…) and leaving `\verb` with no mouth to scan a delimiter from. In
8138/// both engines this yielded an empty `<verbatim/>` with the body leaking out
8139/// mis-tokenized, and a `|` delimiter additionally collided with the makeindex
8140/// encap separator. Consume each whole `\verb<D>body<D>` run HERE — before
8141/// expansion and before the `!`/`@`/`|` split can see the delimiter — and emit
8142/// `\@internal@text@verb{star}{D}{body}` (a non-expandable constructor, so the
8143/// run also survives the `\protected@write` expansion below) so the body
8144/// renders as typewriter.
8145///
8146/// The run is read as makeindex reads the written entry
8147/// ([`unquoted_index_token`], [`IndexVerbBody`]). When a MACRO supplied the
8148/// head (doc.sty:1054-1093 `\verb\quotechar*\verbatimchar\bslash\@gtempa
8149/// \verbatimchar`), the body was assembled by macros too and is expanded
8150/// before it is scanned — `\protected@write` expands it before makeindex ever
8151/// sees it — so it is `\foo`, closed by the expanded `\verbatimchar`, not the
8152/// literal `\bslash\@gtempa\verbatimchar…` running to the end of the entry
8153/// (every doc.sty usage entry: source2e, sunpath). A literal head keeps its
8154/// body literal (`\index{\verb+\delta+}` is `\delta`, not δ). The caller
8155/// runs this inside its `\protected@write` frame (`\protect`, inert symbols).
8156fn absorb_index_verb_runs(toks: &[Token], chars: &IndexChars) -> Result<Vec<Token>> {
8157  let mut out: Vec<Token> = Vec::with_capacity(toks.len());
8158  let mut i = 0;
8159  while i < toks.len() {
8160    let tok = toks[i];
8161    i += 1;
8162    // `\string\verb` WRITES the characters `\verb`, and the `.ind` re-read
8163    // makes them the command again: amsldoc.cls:87-92 `\@indexcs`
8164    // (`\string\verb\quotechar*\verbatimchar…`), doc.sty's `\changes`
8165    // (:641). Left in place, the `\string` stringified the run's opening
8166    // brace (`–` through OT1, amsldoc-it, amsldoc-vi).
8167    if tok == T_CS!("\\string") && toks.get(i) == Some(&T_CS!("\\verb")) {
8168      continue;
8169    }
8170    if tok != T_CS!("\\verb") {
8171      out.push(tok);
8172      continue;
8173    }
8174    if i >= toks.len() {
8175      out.push(tok);
8176      continue;
8177    }
8178    // The head: an optional `*`, then the delimiter.
8179    let head = match unquoted_index_token(toks[i..].to_vec(), chars)? {
8180      Some((first, rest, m1)) if first == T_OTHER!("*") => {
8181        unquoted_index_token(rest, chars)?.map(|(delim, rest, m2)| (true, delim, rest, m1 || m2))
8182      },
8183      Some((first, rest, m1)) => Some((false, first, rest, m1)),
8184      None => None,
8185    };
8186    let Some((starred, delim, rest, from_macro)) = head else {
8187      // Not a verbatim invocation at all: keep `\verb` as index text.
8188      out.extend(Explode!("\\verb"));
8189      continue;
8190    };
8191    let mut body = IndexVerbBody {
8192      delim:  delim.with_str(|d| d.to_string()),
8193      quote:  &chars.quote,
8194      quoted: false,
8195      body:   Vec::new(),
8196    };
8197    // A macro-assembled run is `\protected@write`-expanded before it is read
8198    // (robust and `\protected` commands stay, as in the `\write`): source2e's
8199    // `\DescribeMacro{\g__hook_\meta{hook}_code_prop}` (lthooks.dtx) carries
8200    // doc.sty's `\meta` into the body; read with `read_x_token`, which
8201    // expands robust commands, it ran through `\meta`'s internals (65
8202    // errors on lthooks.dtx). The remainder is handed on expanded; the
8203    // entry's own expansion then finds nothing more to expand in it (a
8204    // `\protect`ed command re-protects itself).
8205    //
8206    // The run may close inside a group of the expanded entry: doc.sty:544-548
8207    // `\LeftBraceIndex` writes `…\verbatimchar\quotechar\bslash{\verbatimchar
8208    // \string\iffalse}\string\fi`, whose re-read makes `\iffalse…\fi` hide the
8209    // `}` again; a remainder that does not balance is read literally instead.
8210    let literal_rest = rest.clone();
8211    let mut rest = if from_macro {
8212      do_expand_partially(Tokens::new(rest))?.unlist()
8213    } else {
8214      rest
8215    };
8216    let scan = |rest: &[Token], body: &mut IndexVerbBody| {
8217      let mut j = 0;
8218      while j < rest.len() && !body.feed(rest[j]) {
8219        j += 1;
8220      }
8221      // consume the closing delimiter
8222      rest[(j + 1).min(rest.len())..].to_vec()
8223    };
8224    let mut after: Vec<Token> = scan(&rest, &mut body);
8225    if from_macro && !Tokens::new(after.clone()).is_balanced() {
8226      body.body.clear();
8227      body.quoted = false;
8228      rest = literal_rest;
8229      after = scan(&rest, &mut body);
8230    }
8231    // The re-tokenized body collapsed `\verb`'s raw chars back into control
8232    // sequences; `untex` + `Explode!` restores them to catcode-OTHER literals
8233    // so the digested `#3` renders as typewriter text instead of re-expanding
8234    // (which is exactly the `\delta`→math-δ leak this fixes).
8235    let mut body_toks = body.body;
8236    if from_macro {
8237      // A robust command is written by its name: the `.idx` line of
8238      // `\DescribeMacro{\foo\meta{name}}` reads `\verb!*+\foo\meta  {name}+`
8239      // (pdflatex), without the `\protect` the expansion stops at.
8240      let protect = T_CS!("\\protect");
8241      let mut kept = Vec::with_capacity(body_toks.len());
8242      for (k, t) in body_toks.iter().enumerate() {
8243        let next_is_cs = body_toks
8244          .get(k + 1)
8245          .is_some_and(|n| n.get_catcode() == Catcode::CS);
8246        if !(*t == protect && next_is_cs) {
8247          kept.push(*t);
8248        }
8249      }
8250      body_toks = kept;
8251    }
8252    let body_str = Tokens::new(body_toks).untex();
8253    // In a group, as `\verb` itself is: the constructor's typewriter font
8254    // must not run on into the rest of the phrase (doc.sty's change entry
8255    // `\verb*+\foo+:` → the `:` and the next level were typewriter).
8256    out.push(T_BEGIN!());
8257    out.push(T_CS!("\\@internal@text@verb"));
8258    out.push(T_BEGIN!());
8259    if starred {
8260      out.push(T_OTHER!("*"));
8261    }
8262    out.push(T_END!());
8263    out.push(T_BEGIN!());
8264    out.push(delim);
8265    out.push(T_END!());
8266    out.push(T_BEGIN!());
8267    out.extend(Explode!(body_str));
8268    out.push(T_END!());
8269    out.push(T_END!());
8270    // The remainder may hold further runs; it is a fresh slice now.
8271    out.extend(absorb_index_verb_runs(&after, chars)?);
8272    return Ok(out);
8273  }
8274  Ok(out)
8275}
8276
8277/// The tokens that typeset `tokens`, an entry TeX writes for the list `list` (`idx`, a named index, `glo`,
8278/// `nomenclature`) and prints only from `\printindex` or its like: the entry itself once the list is printed, else the
8279/// anchor `\lx@deferred@print{id}` of an entry kept raw until it is (latexml_core `defer_print`;
8280/// OXIDIZED_DESIGN_DIVERGENCES #738).
8281pub fn deferred_print_tokens(list: &str, tokens: Tokens) -> Tokens {
8282  if tokens.is_empty() || deferred_list_is_printed(list) {
8283    return tokens;
8284  }
8285  let id = defer_print(list, tokens);
8286  let mut out = vec![T_CS!("\\lx@deferred@print"), T_BEGIN!()];
8287  out.extend(Explode!(id.to_string()));
8288  out.push(T_END!());
8289  Tokens::new(out)
8290}
8291
8292/// `chars` are the makeindex characters the entry is split with
8293/// ([`IndexChars::in_force`]); `inlist` names the list the mark belongs to
8294/// (Perl's third argument: `\@index[style][inlist]`) — `\glossary` marks
8295/// list `glo`, collected by a `.gls` stand-in's `<ltx:index lists="glo">`;
8296/// `formed` are the control words the `.idx` re-read formed from typed
8297/// characters ([`reread_sanitized_entry`]), written verbatim, never expanded.
8298pub(crate) fn process_index_phrases(
8299  tokens: Tokens,
8300  chars: &IndexChars,
8301  inlist: Option<&str>,
8302  formed: &[Token],
8303) -> Result<Tokens> {
8304  if tokens.is_empty() {
8305    return Ok(Tokens::new(vec![]));
8306  }
8307  // Perl pool:4332-4336: an entry whose groups do not balance is discarded, as
8308  // makeindex rejects it. doc.sty's `\changes{v1.2i}{…}{Use \cs{protected} for
8309  // \cs{\bslash} variant}` (ltmath.dtx, source2e) writes `\cs{\}`, whose
8310  // re-read `\}` leaves the `{` open (the golden change history has no such
8311  // entry); read as a phrase it ran the entry's reader off its end.
8312  if !tokens.is_balanced() {
8313    Warn!(
8314      "malformed",
8315      "indexentry",
8316      s!(
8317        "index entry has unbalanced groups, discarding: \"{}\"",
8318        tokens
8319      )
8320    );
8321    return Ok(Tokens::new(vec![]));
8322  }
8323  let token_list = tokens.unlist();
8324  // Real `\index` (latex.ltx:17720-17725 `\@wrindex`) writes the entry with
8325  // `\protected@write`, i.e. the argument is EXPANDED (robust/`\protected`
8326  // commands deferred) before makeindex ever sees the `@`/`!`/`|` separators.
8327  // Packages build entries out of macros — tcolorbox's documentation library
8328  // writes `\kvtcb@doc@sortindex\idx@actual\tcbIndexPrintComC{…}` where
8329  // `\idx@actual` IS the `@` (tcbdocumentation.code.tex:147/495) — so a split
8330  // over unexpanded tokens sees no separator, digests the sort key as text,
8331  // and every `_` in it becomes `Script _ can only appear in math mode`
8332  // (tagpdf manual: 92 lines; perfect-kernel repro `\begin{docCommand}
8333  // {tag_if_active:TF}{}`). Perl's process_index_phrases (pool:4376-4397)
8334  // shares the omission; expanding is the faithful `\@wrindex` behaviour.
8335  // The `\verb` runs are absorbed first so their bodies stay verbatim.
8336  // `\protected@write` (latex.ltx:9551) does `\let\protect\@unexpandable@protect`
8337  // before its `\edef`, so a `\protect`ed macro is FROZEN into the entry and
8338  // runs only when the entry is typeset. Expanding with `\protect`=`\relax`
8339  // ran manyind.sty:100/119's `\protect\def\nwletre{…}`/`\protect\nxtletre`
8340  // at write time — the `\def` never bound its name (`undefined \nwletre`)
8341  // and `\proc@letter`'s caller-closing `\fi` (manyind.sty:148) surfaced as a
8342  // stray `\fi` (mindsample; Perl, which never expands here, is clean).
8343  // Guard: `perfect_kernel_batch54::index_entry_defers_protected_macros`.
8344  // A control SYMBOL in the entry is never expanded here. After `\@sanitize`
8345  // (latex.ltx:1778) real `\@wrindex` writes a `\string`ed control symbol as
8346  // two characters, makeindex drops the sort key entirely and `\printindex`
8347  // re-reads only the display — so amsldoc.cls:84-89's sort key `\*` for
8348  // `\cn{\\*}` is never executed. The `.idx` re-read (`reread_sanitized_entry`)
8349  // welds those two characters back into the live `\*` (amsldoc.cls:213
8350  // `\def\*#1`), which ate the rest of the entry (itamsldoc, amsldoc-vi;
8351  // Perl shares it, PLANS P73). Freezing every control symbol with
8352  // `\noexpand` keeps `\*` inert (the key is a string anyway) while accents
8353  // in the display (`M\"uller`) are constructors and unaffected; separators
8354  // still come from control WORDS (`\idx@actual`). Guard:
8355  // `perfect_kernel_batch54::index_sanitized_backslash_symbol_stays_literal`.
8356  // An UNDEFINED control word is frozen too: the entry is a `.idx` STRING
8357  // that `\printindex` re-reads and digests in order, so manyind.sty:100/119's
8358  // `\protect\def \nwletre {\"O}…\nwletre` defines the name before its use;
8359  // force-expanding the bare `\nwletre` here stubbed it as `<ltx:ERROR/>`
8360  // (mindsample; Perl, which never expands, is clean). Guard:
8361  // `perfect_kernel_batch56::index_entry_passes_undefined_words_inert`.
8362  // The freeze is a STATE-level `\let` to `\relax` inside the expansion
8363  // frame, never an injected `\noexpand` TOKEN: `\string` reads the next
8364  // token literally, so `\string\noexpand\cmd` stringified "\noexpand" and
8365  // re-exposed `\cmd` to expansion — beamerug-macros.tex:44's
8366  // `\gdef\stripcommand#1{\expandafter\@gobble\string#1}` (which hides the
8367  // `\string` from any token-level neighbour check) made every documented
8368  // command undefined and every `\if…` name a runaway conditional
8369  // (beameruserguide 167 errors; Perl 0). Let to `\relax`, the name is
8370  // unexpandable for the pass, stringifies by NAME, and is restored to its
8371  // real (or undefined) meaning when the frame pops. Guard:
8372  // `cluster_package_guards::index_string_of_undefined_command_stringifies_its_name`.
8373  let inert: Vec<Token> = token_list
8374    .iter()
8375    .filter(|t| {
8376      t.get_catcode() == Catcode::CS
8377        && (t.with_str(|s| {
8378          let mut chars = s.chars();
8379          chars.next() == Some('\\')
8380            && chars.next().is_some_and(|c| !c.is_alphabetic())
8381            && chars.next().is_none()
8382        }) || lookup_meaning(t).is_none()
8383          || formed.contains(t))
8384    })
8385    .cloned()
8386    .collect();
8387  push_frame();
8388  let_i(
8389    &T_CS!("\\protect"),
8390    &T_CS!("\\@unexpandable@protect"),
8391    Some(Scope::Local),
8392  );
8393  for t in &inert {
8394    let_i(t, &T_CS!("\\relax"), Some(Scope::Local));
8395  }
8396  // The `\verb` runs are absorbed inside the same frame: a macro-assembled
8397  // run's body is expanded as it is scanned, and amsldoc's `\cn{\\*}`
8398  // entry (`\@indexcs`, amsldoc.cls:87-92) carries the control symbol `\*`
8399  // into it, whose amsldoc.cls:213 `\def\*#1` ate the rest of the entry and
8400  // spilled keyval errors (amsldoc-it, amsldoc-vi).
8401  // A Fatal inside either stays Fatal; the frame pops first.
8402  let expanded = absorb_index_verb_runs(&token_list, chars)
8403    .and_then(|toks| do_expand_partially(Tokens::new(toks)));
8404  pop_frame()?;
8405  // The `.ind` re-read: `\printindex` `\input`s the written entry in the
8406  // document body, where `@` is OTHER, so a control word that still carries
8407  // an `@` after the `\protected@write` expansion splits there —
8408  // mindsample.tex:208 `\index{\AB@\relax…}` is the key `\AB` and the
8409  // separator (Perl's `TokenizeInternal` re-read keeps one undefined `\AB@`;
8410  // OXIDIZED_DESIGN_DIVERGENCES #222). Names the expansion consumed
8411  // (`\kvtcb@doc@sortindex`, `\idx@actual`) never reach this point; a
8412  // DEFINED survivor is a robust command or one of our own markers
8413  // (`\@internal@text@verb` from the `\verb` absorption) and stays whole —
8414  // only an undefined `@`-name, which could otherwise just error, is re-read.
8415  // No `\protect` reaches the file: the `\write` is expanded again at
8416  // shipout under `\let\protect\noexpand` (latex.ltx:20913 `\@outputpage`),
8417  // which writes each frozen `\protect X` as `X` — tikz-ext's
8418  // `\index{…\protect\string\protect\pgftext…}` is written `\string\pgftext`
8419  // and prints "\pgftext"; kept, its `\pgftext` ran as the entry was read
8420  // (501 `\egroup` errors). Guard:
8421  // `perfect_kernel_batch61::index_entry_protect_is_consumed_at_shipout`.
8422  let token_list: Vec<Token> = expanded?
8423    .unlist()
8424    .into_iter()
8425    .flat_map(|t| {
8426      if t.get_catcode() == Catcode::CS && t.with_str(|s| s == "\\protect") {
8427        vec![]
8428      } else if t.get_catcode() == Catcode::CS
8429        && t.with_str(|s| s[1..].contains('@'))
8430        && lookup_meaning(&t).is_none()
8431      {
8432        t.with_str(|s| mouth::tokenize(TeXString::assembled(s.to_string())).unlist())
8433      } else {
8434        vec![t]
8435      }
8436    })
8437    .collect();
8438  // Add a terminal level character if not present
8439  let mut toks = token_list;
8440  if toks
8441    .last()
8442    .map(|t| t.with_str(|s| s != chars.level))
8443    .unwrap_or(true)
8444  {
8445    toks.push(T_OTHER!(chars.level.as_str()));
8446  }
8447  let mut expansion: Vec<Token> = Vec::new();
8448  let mut phrase: Vec<Token> = Vec::new();
8449  let mut sortas: Vec<Token> = Vec::new();
8450  let mut style: Option<String> = None;
8451  let mut i = 0;
8452  // Separator chars (makeindex's quote/actual/level/encap, by default
8453  // `"`/`@`/`!`/`|`) act ONLY at brace depth 0. A flat
8454  // scan (Perl latex_constructs.pool.ltxml L4326-4350 — Perl shares this
8455  // byte-identically) cuts through nested groups: packdoc.sty L328/L331
8456  // writes `\index{#2@\PDElement{#1}{#2}\csuse{packdoc@#1@IndexRemark}}`,
8457  // whose in-group `@`s shredded the phrase and emitted UNBALANCED braces
8458  // into the live stream — one mode error + one orphaned indexphrase per
8459  // `\OptionInd` (algxpar-doc 162+149 errs, numerica; pdflatex clean —
8460  // real makeindex splits the out-of-band .idx STRING where imbalance
8461  // cannot corrupt the document). KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #83.
8462  // Nor inside math: `\index{arroba@$@$}` (latex-via-exemplos.tex:1042
8463  // `\arrobasymbforindex` = `$@$`, used at :4238/:4691/:5363) is the key
8464  // `arroba` and the display `$@$`; splitting at the `@` inside the math
8465  // emitted `\@indexphrase[$]{$}` with a lone `$` that opened inline math
8466  // the bounded `\@index` box could never close (three errors per entry and
8467  // a leaked `<ltx:XMath>` swallowing the paragraph; Perl digests the lone
8468  // `$` silently, pdflatex is clean). A `$` at brace depth 0 toggles the
8469  // math state (`$$` twice: display math toggles net zero as it should).
8470  let mut depth: i32 = 0;
8471  let mut in_math = false;
8472  while i < toks.len() {
8473    let tok = toks[i];
8474    match tok.get_catcode() {
8475      Catcode::BEGIN => depth += 1,
8476      Catcode::END => depth -= 1,
8477      Catcode::MATH if depth == 0 => in_math = !in_math,
8478      _ => {},
8479    }
8480    if depth > 0
8481      || tok.get_catcode() == Catcode::END && depth == 0
8482      || in_math
8483      || tok.get_catcode() == Catcode::MATH
8484    {
8485      // Inside a group (or the closing brace returning to depth 0) or
8486      // inside math (or its closing `$`): plain phrase material, never a
8487      // separator.
8488      phrase.push(tok);
8489      i += 1;
8490      continue;
8491    }
8492    let s = tok.with_str(|s| s.to_string());
8493    i += 1;
8494    if s == chars.quote && i < toks.len() {
8495      // Escaped character: take next token literally
8496      phrase.push(toks[i]);
8497      i += 1;
8498    } else if s == chars.actual {
8499      // Sort key: everything before @ is the sort key
8500      while phrase
8501        .last()
8502        .map(|t| t.with_str(|s| s.trim().is_empty()))
8503        .unwrap_or(false)
8504      {
8505        phrase.pop();
8506      }
8507      // The sort key is a makeindex STRING: real `\index` reads it under
8508      // `\@sanitize` (latex.ltx:17705-17711) and it is never typeset, so
8509      // `_`/`^`/`&`/`#`/`$`/`~` in it are literal characters (tcolorbox
8510      // `docCommand{tag_if_active:TF}` → sortindex `tag_if_active:TF`;
8511      // `\index{a_b@\texttt{a\_b}}`). Digesting the key with their live
8512      // catcodes raised `Script _ can only appear in math mode`; Perl
8513      // (`\@indexphrase[]` digests too) shares that. Neutralize them here.
8514      // An undefined control word in the key is literal text as well:
8515      // makeindex sorts on the characters `\A`/`\AB` (mindsample.tex:200-208
8516      // `\index{\A>@…}`, `\index{\AB@…}` — manyind's sort-key idiom), and
8517      // digesting it can only raise `undefined` (Perl shares that error).
8518      // Guard: `perfect_kernel_batch56::index_sort_key_undefined_word_is_text`.
8519      // So is any control word typed in the source (`formed`): written
8520      // verbatim, the key is its characters — `\index{\key @\show}` sorts on
8521      // `\key`, whatever `\key` means.
8522      // So is an implicit brace (`\bgroup`/`\egroup`, a `\let` to `{`/`}`):
8523      // doc.sty:544-555 `\LeftBraceIndex`/`\RightBraceIndex` sort their entries
8524      // under `\bgroup`/`\egroup`, and digested they opened or closed a group
8525      // of the document.
8526      let implicit_brace = |t: &Token| {
8527        with_meaning(t, |m| {
8528          matches!(m, Some(Stored::Token(l))
8529            if matches!(l.get_catcode(), Catcode::BEGIN | Catcode::END))
8530        })
8531      };
8532      sortas = phrase
8533        .drain(..)
8534        .flat_map(|t| match t.get_catcode() {
8535          Catcode::MATH
8536          | Catcode::ALIGN
8537          | Catcode::PARAM
8538          | Catcode::SUPER
8539          | Catcode::SUB
8540          | Catcode::ACTIVE => vec![T_OTHER!(t.with_str(|s| s.to_string()))],
8541          Catcode::CS
8542            if lookup_meaning(&t).is_none() || implicit_brace(&t) || formed.contains(&t) =>
8543          {
8544            // `\textbackslash` + the name: an OTHER `\` would typeset
8545            // through the OT1 slot (“).
8546            let mut lit = vec![T_CS!("\\textbackslash")];
8547            t.with_str(|s| {
8548              lit.extend(s.chars().skip(1).map(|c| T_OTHER!(c.to_string())));
8549            });
8550            lit
8551          },
8552          _ => vec![t],
8553        })
8554        .collect();
8555    } else if s == chars.level || s == chars.encap {
8556      // End of phrase
8557      while phrase
8558        .last()
8559        .map(|t| t.with_str(|s| s.trim().is_empty()))
8560        .unwrap_or(false)
8561      {
8562        phrase.pop();
8563      }
8564      if !phrase.is_empty() {
8565        expansion.push(T_CS!("\\@indexphrase"));
8566        if !sortas.is_empty() {
8567          // Brace-protect the sort key: a raw `]` inside it (examdoc
8568          // `\indc{gradetable[v]}`, pgfornament `pgfornament[<options>]`)
8569          // truncates the constructor's `[]` re-parse at the first `]`,
8570          // spilling the display phrase as illegal <ltx:indexmark> children
8571          // (Perl shares the flat re-parse — KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #83 sibling).
8572          // clean_index_key strips the one wrapping pair symmetrically.
8573          expansion.push(T_OTHER!("["));
8574          expansion.push(T_BEGIN!());
8575          expansion.append(&mut sortas);
8576          expansion.push(T_END!());
8577          expansion.push(T_OTHER!("]"));
8578        }
8579        expansion.push(T_BEGIN!());
8580        expansion.extend(reread_script_chars(std::mem::take(&mut phrase)));
8581        expansion.push(T_END!());
8582      }
8583      sortas.clear();
8584      if s == chars.encap {
8585        // Collect remaining tokens as style/see/seealso
8586        if i < toks.len()
8587          && toks
8588            .last()
8589            .map(|t| t.with_str(|s| s == chars.level))
8590            .unwrap_or(false)
8591        {
8592          // Remove the terminal level-character stopbit
8593          toks.pop();
8594        }
8595        let extra: String = toks[i..]
8596          .iter()
8597          .map(|t| t.with_str(|s| s.to_string()))
8598          .collect();
8599        if extra.starts_with("see{") || extra.starts_with("see {") {
8600          // \@indexsee{content} — pass the ORIGINAL tokens (Perl:
8601          // @tokens[3..]) rather than a re-Exploded string, so macros
8602          // and math inside the see-phrase keep their catcodes and
8603          // expand normally (e.g. \index{X|see{\foo $n$-cube}}).
8604          // The brace tokens ride along as the constructor's argument
8605          // delimiters.
8606          expansion.push(T_CS!("\\@indexsee"));
8607          expansion.extend(toks[i + 3..].iter().cloned());
8608        } else if extra.starts_with("seealso{") || extra.starts_with("seealso {") {
8609          expansion.push(T_CS!("\\@indexseealso"));
8610          expansion.extend(toks[i + 7..].iter().cloned());
8611        } else if extra.starts_with("seeonly{") || extra.starts_with("seeonly {") {
8612          // DEVIATION from Perl LaTeXML, which lets `|seeonly{...}`
8613          // fall through to the style branch below: the raw string
8614          // (catcode-mangled) ends up as a font attribute and renders
8615          // as a garbage ltx_font_* class (98 occurrences in the AoBF
8616          // book, 181 validation errors). The makeindex idiom means
8617          // "print ONLY the see-reference, no locators" — treating it
8618          // as \@indexsee both renders it correctly and suppresses
8619          // this mark's locator refs (Scan skips referrer recording
8620          // when ltx:indexsee children are present).
8621          expansion.push(T_CS!("\\@indexsee"));
8622          expansion.extend(toks[i + 7..].iter().cloned());
8623        } else if extra == "(" {
8624          style = Some("rangestart".to_string());
8625        } else if extra == ")" {
8626          style = Some("rangeend".to_string());
8627        } else if !extra.is_empty() {
8628          // Style name (e.g., textbf → bold)
8629          style = Some(match extra.as_str() {
8630            "textbf" | "bf" => "bold".to_string(),
8631            "textit" | "it" | "emph" => "italic".to_string(),
8632            "textrm" | "rm" => String::new(),
8633            // An encap with arguments is `\cmd{args}{page}`; the style is
8634            // the command — hypdoc's `hdpindex{main}` / `hdclindex{2}{usage}`
8635            // (hypdoc.sty:344-364, every doc.sty index entry under
8636            // hyperref) are `hdpindex` / `hdclindex`. Perl keeps the whole
8637            // encap, a `font` no stylesheet names (`ltx_font_hdpindex{main}`).
8638            other => match other.split_once('{') {
8639              Some((cmd, _)) if !cmd.trim().is_empty() => cmd.trim().to_string(),
8640              _ => other.to_string(),
8641            },
8642          });
8643        }
8644        break; // Consumed everything after |
8645      }
8646    } else if phrase.is_empty() && s.trim().is_empty() {
8647      // Skip leading whitespace
8648    } else {
8649      phrase.push(tok);
8650    }
8651  }
8652  // Wrap in \@index[style][inlist]{...} (Perl: the `[style]` slot is
8653  // written, possibly empty, whenever a list follows it). No group around it:
8654  // `\@index` neutralizes the font itself, as Perl's (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:4410);
8655  // a `{\normalfont …}` wrapper left `{}` in the tex= of a formula holding an `\index`.
8656  let mut result = vec![T_CS!("\\@index")];
8657  let style = style.filter(|sty| !sty.is_empty());
8658  if style.is_some() || inlist.is_some() {
8659    result.push(T_OTHER!("["));
8660    if let Some(sty) = style {
8661      // ONE token, as Perl's `T_OTHER($style)`: exploded, the braces of an
8662      // encap with arguments (hypdoc's `hdpindex{main}`, hypdoc.sty:344-353) were
8663      // digested through the OT1 slots into `hdpindex–main˝`.
8664      result.push(T_OTHER!(sty.as_str()));
8665    }
8666    result.push(T_OTHER!("]"));
8667  }
8668  if let Some(list) = inlist {
8669    result.push(T_OTHER!("["));
8670    result.extend(Explode!(list));
8671    result.push(T_OTHER!("]"));
8672  }
8673  result.push(T_BEGIN!());
8674  result.extend(expansion);
8675  result.push(T_END!());
8676  Ok(Tokens::new(result))
8677}
8678
8679/// Convert TeX points to CSS pixels using DPI setting (default 100).
8680/// Perl: $$self[0] / 65536 * DPI / 72.27
8681fn px_value(pt: f64) -> f64 {
8682  // DPI default is 100 in LaTeXML (state::lookupValue('DPI') || 100)
8683  let dpi = lookup_value("DPI")
8684    .and_then(|v| {
8685      if let Stored::Number(n) = v {
8686        Some(n.0 as f64)
8687      } else {
8688        None
8689      }
8690    })
8691    .unwrap_or(100.0);
8692  // Round to 2 decimal places (Perl default precision)
8693  (pt * dpi / 72.27 * 100.0).round() / 100.0
8694}
8695/// Format a px value, dropping trailing ".0" for integers
8696fn fmt_px(v: f64) -> String {
8697  if v == v.round() && v.abs() < 1e10 {
8698    format!("{}", v as i64)
8699  } else {
8700    format!("{v}")
8701  }
8702}

8704/// Perl: %unicode_enclosed_alphanumerics table
8705/// Maps single chars (0-9, a-z, A-Z) and numbers 10-20 to their circled Unicode equivalents; beyond Perl's table,
8706/// the circled numbers 21-35 (U+3251-325F) and 36-50 (U+32B1-32BF) of Enclosed CJK Letters and Months, which Perl
8707/// prints as "21⃝" (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #361).
8708fn unicode_enclosed_alphanumeric(text: &str) -> Option<String> {
8709  if let Ok(n) = text.parse::<u32>()
8710    && text.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_digit())
8711    && !text.starts_with('0')
8712  {
8713    let ch = match n {
8714      21..=35 => char::from_u32(0x3251 + (n - 21)),
8715      36..=50 => char::from_u32(0x32B1 + (n - 36)),
8716      _ => None,
8717    };
8718    if let Some(ch) = ch {
8719      return Some(ch.to_string());
8720    }
8721  }
8722  let ch = match text {
8723    "0" => '\u{24EA}',
8724    "1" => '\u{2460}',
8725    "2" => '\u{2461}',
8726    "3" => '\u{2462}',
8727    "4" => '\u{2463}',
8728    "5" => '\u{2464}',
8729    "6" => '\u{2465}',
8730    "7" => '\u{2466}',
8731    "8" => '\u{2467}',
8732    "9" => '\u{2468}',
8733    "10" => '\u{2469}',
8734    "11" => '\u{246A}',
8735    "12" => '\u{246B}',
8736    "13" => '\u{246C}',
8737    "14" => '\u{246D}',
8738    "15" => '\u{246E}',
8739    "16" => '\u{246F}',
8740    "17" => '\u{2470}',
8741    "18" => '\u{2471}',
8742    "19" => '\u{2472}',
8743    "20" => '\u{2473}',
8744    "a" => '\u{24D0}',
8745    "b" => '\u{24D1}',
8746    "c" => '\u{24D2}',
8747    "d" => '\u{24D3}',
8748    "e" => '\u{24D4}',
8749    "f" => '\u{24D5}',
8750    "g" => '\u{24D6}',
8751    "h" => '\u{24D7}',
8752    "i" => '\u{24D8}',
8753    "j" => '\u{24D9}',
8754    "k" => '\u{24DA}',
8755    "l" => '\u{24DB}',
8756    "m" => '\u{24DC}',
8757    "n" => '\u{24DD}',
8758    "o" => '\u{24DE}',
8759    "p" => '\u{24DF}',
8760    "q" => '\u{24E0}',
8761    "r" => '\u{24E1}',
8762    "s" => '\u{24E2}',
8763    "t" => '\u{24E3}',
8764    "u" => '\u{24E4}',
8765    "v" => '\u{24E5}',
8766    "w" => '\u{24E6}',
8767    "x" => '\u{24E7}',
8768    "y" => '\u{24E8}',
8769    "z" => '\u{24E9}',
8770    "A" => '\u{24B6}',
8771    "B" => '\u{24B7}',
8772    "C" => '\u{24B8}',
8773    "D" => '\u{24B9}',
8774    "E" => '\u{24BA}',
8775    "F" => '\u{24BB}',
8776    "G" => '\u{24BC}',
8777    "H" => '\u{24BD}',
8778    "I" => '\u{24BE}',
8779    "J" => '\u{24BF}',
8780    "K" => '\u{24C0}',
8781    "L" => '\u{24C1}',
8782    "M" => '\u{24C2}',
8783    "N" => '\u{24C3}',
8784    "O" => '\u{24C4}',
8785    "P" => '\u{24C5}',
8786    "Q" => '\u{24C6}',
8787    "R" => '\u{24C7}',
8788    "S" => '\u{24C8}',
8789    "T" => '\u{24C9}',
8790    "U" => '\u{24CA}',
8791    "V" => '\u{24CB}',
8792    "W" => '\u{24CC}',
8793    "X" => '\u{24CD}',
8794    "Y" => '\u{24CE}',
8795    "Z" => '\u{24CF}',
8796    _ => return None,
8797  };
8798  Some(ch.to_string())
8799}

8802/// `\makebox[w][align]` horizontal alignment (Perl `%makebox_alignment` #2829:
8803/// l/r/c/s → left/right/center). The `s` (stretch-to-fill) case is emitted as
8804/// `justified` — the schema `align` enum is `left|center|right|justified`
8805/// (`LaTeXML-common.rnc:216`), with no `stretched`; `[s]` justifies the box's
8806/// inter-word glue to fill the width, which `text-align:justify` renders
8807/// faithfully. Perl emits the schema-invalid `stretched` here; this is an
8808/// intentional, schema-validity divergence (OXIDIZED_DESIGN #239).
8809fn makebox_alignment(key: &str) -> &'static str {
8810  match key {
8811    "l" => "left",
8812    "r" => "right",
8813    "c" => "center",
8814    "s" => "justified",
8815    _ => "",
8816  }
8817}

8873LoadDefinitions!({
8874  // Perl `latex_constructs.pool.ltxml` L19-38 — force-reload of
8875  // `plain_constructs` and `math_common`. By the time
8876  // `latex_constructs` runs, both pools were already loaded during the
8877  // plain-format chain (`tex.rs::LoadFormat('plain')`), and several of
8878  // their definitions have since been clobbered by `latex_base` and
8879  // earlier `latex_constructs` activity. Perl explicitly clears the
8880  // `_loaded` flags and re-runs `LoadPool('plain_constructs')` (L21)
8881  // followed by `LoadPool('math_common')` (L38) to re-establish those
8882  // pools' definitions on top of LaTeX-side changes.
8883  //
8884  // Rust note: since commit `8dfcb12f7`, `InnerPool!(...)` honors
8885  // `<name>.pool_loaded` (mirror of Perl `LoadPool`'s
8886  // `<name>.pool.ltxml_loaded` guard, with the Rust suffix
8887  // convention). The two `assign_value(... Stored::None)` resets
8888  // below are therefore load-bearing — without them, `InnerPool!`
8889  // would skip the re-run.
8890  //
8891  // Perl interleaves a handful of defs (font reset, `\hline`,
8892  // `\f@encoding`, `\par→\lx@normal@par`, etc.) between L21 and L38;
8893  // Rust collapses both reloads here at the top because the
8894  // intervening defs are positioned later in this file (or in
8895  // `plain_constructs.rs`) and are agnostic to whether `math_common`
8896  // is reloaded before or after them.
8897  assign_value(
8898    "plain_constructs.pool_loaded",
8899    Stored::None,
8900    Some(Scope::Global),
8901  );
8902  assign_value("math_common.pool_loaded", Stored::None, Some(Scope::Global));
8903  // The reloads MUST run with state unlocked. By the time we get here,
8904  // the first plain-format pass has already locked common math CSes
8905  // (e.g. `\prime`, `\active@math@prime`) via their `locked => true`
8906  // DefMath/DefMacro entries. Without an unlocked frame, the second
8907  // pass sees `\prime:locked` and silently drops the redefinition,
8908  // leaving the dump-loaded `\mathchardef\prime="0230` mathchar in
8909  // place — which renders as digit `0` (char 0x30 in fam 2) instead
8910  // of U+2032 ′. Mirror Perl's LoadPool flow which reloads via the
8911  // top-level binding scope where re-locks are allowed.
8912  local_state_unlocked(true);
8913  InnerPool!(plain_constructs);
8914  InnerPool!(math_common);
8915  expire_state_unlocked();
8916
8917  // Perl latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:36 — `Let('\par', '\lx@normal@par')`.
8918  // After the dump load (which installs `\par` as the heavy expl3 chain
8919  // `\para_end:` body via Lt-aliases), Perl re-Lets `\par` to the engine's
8920  // plain `\lx@normal@par` Constructor here. So at document-body time,
8921  // `\par` is a Constructor (no body residue), not the chain. Without
8922  // this re-Let in Rust, dump-path `\par` stays the expl3 chain;
8923  // `leave_horizontal()`'s implicit `\par` invocation then leaves chain
8924  // residue (`\tex_unskip:D \mode_if_horizontal:TF{...}\tex_par:D ...`)
8925  // in the gullet pushback, corrupting subsequent numeric/token reads —
8926  // breaks box_test, ifthen_test, aftergroup_test, halign_test,
8927  // vmode_test, IEEE_test, plainfonts_test (each NODUMP-passes,
8928  // DUMP-only-fails, all share the same `\par` chain residue root cause).
8929  Let!("\\par", "\\lx@normal@par");
8930
8931  // Perl latex_constructs.pool.ltxml L42-43 — early DefAccent duplicates
8932  // for `\k` (Ogonek) and `\r` (Ring above). Per Perl: "These really
8933  // shouldn't be here, but somehow aren't getting defined in the right
8934  // place???". The dump installs `\k`/`\r` as raw t1enc Expandables
8935  // (`\T1-cmd \k \T1\k`); without this re-install they stay broken
8936  // until `\k` is reinstalled at L8820 in math section. Mirror Perl by
8937  // restoring the DefAccent right after dump at C.1 region.
8938  DefAccent!("\\k", '\u{0328}', "\u{02DB}", below => true); // COMBINING OGONEK & OGONEK
8939  DefAccent!("\\r", '\u{030A}', "\u{02DA}"); // COMBINING RING ABOVE & non-combining
8940
8941  // Perl latex_constructs.pool.ltxml L25-26 — restore default fonts after
8942  // dump load. Without this, dump-time font residue (CJK shimming etc.)
8943  // leaks into document body. Mirror Perl `assignValue('font' => textDefault, 'global')`.
8944  assign_value(
8945    "font",
8946    Stored::Font(Rc::new(Font::text_default())),
8947    Some(Scope::Global),
8948  );
8949  assign_value(
8950    "mathfont",
8951    Stored::Font(Rc::new(Font::math_default())),
8952    Some(Scope::Global),
8953  );
8954
8955  // \&, \#, \%, \$, \_ math-mode dispatch — the dump captures these as raw
8956  // CharDef registers losing plain_base.rs's `\ifmmode` dispatch. Tried
8957  // re-DefMacro to `\ifmmode\lx@math@amp\else\lx@text@amp\fi` but the
8958  // `\lx@(text|math)@*` targets live in plain_base.rs (DefPrimitive
8959  // closures) which is SKIPPED on dump path — re-DefMacro produces
8960  // <ERROR class="undefined"/>. Proper fix needs relocating the
8961  // `\lx@text@amp`/`\lx@math@amp` family from plain_base.rs to
8962  // plain_constructs.rs (which runs in both paths) before adding the
8963  // re-DefMacro here. Deferred — dump's CharDef-38 works in text mode,
8964  // ifthen_test remaining failure is the only known math-mode issue.
8965
8966  sect01::load()?;
8967  sect02::load()?;
8968  sect03::load()?;
8969  sect04::load()?;

8971  sect06::load()?;

8981/// `\verb`'s expansion: the verbatim argument read ([`read_verb_invocation`]) in the hidden group `\verb@egroup`
8982/// closes. Shared by the kernel `\verb` and tabularx's `\TX@verb` (`token_delimited`).
8983pub fn verb_group(token_delimited: bool) -> Result<Tokens> {
8984  Ok(match read_verb_invocation(token_delimited)? {
8985    Some(inner) => {
8986      let mut result = vec![T_CS!("\\lx@hidden@bgroup")];
8987      result.extend(inner);
8988      result.push(T_CS!("\\verb@egroup"));
8989      Tokens::new(result)
8990    },
8991    None => Tokens!(),
8992  })
8993}
8994
8995/// Read a `\verb`-style verbatim argument from the current input — the
8996/// optional `*`, the delimiter, and the body up to the next delimiter — and
8997/// return the tokens that typeset it: `[\lx@use@visiblespace]
8998/// \@internal@verb{star}{delim}{body}`, WITHOUT the enclosing hidden group,
8999/// so a wrapper (newverbs' `\newverbcommand{\cmd}{before}{after}`) can put
9000/// its own tokens inside the same group. `None` when no delimiter was found
9001/// (an `expected:delimiter` error has been reported).
9002pub fn read_verb_invocation(token_delimited: bool) -> Result<Option<Vec<Token>>> {
9003  begin_semiverbatim(Some(&SEMIVERBATIM_CHARS));
9004  apply_dospecials();
9005  // Do NOT (necessarily) skip spaces after \verb!!!
9006  assign_catcode(' ', Catcode::ACTIVE, None);
9007  let mut init = None;
9008  let mut skipped_space = false;
9009  // As of texlive 2021, DO skip spaces before delimiter (even tho we've changed catcodes)
9010  // but if we do skip spaces, * can be the delimiter
9011  let space_sym = pin!(" ");
9012  while let Some(maybe_init) = read_token()? {
9013    if maybe_init.get_sym() == space_sym {
9014      skipped_space = true;
9015    } else {
9016      init = Some(maybe_init);
9017      break;
9018    }
9019  }
9020  let mut starred = false;
9021  if let Some(ref init_token) = init
9022    && *init_token == T_OTHER!("*")
9023    && !skipped_space
9024  {
9025    starred = true;
9026    while let Some(maybe_init) = read_token()? {
9027      if maybe_init.get_sym() != space_sym {
9028        init = Some(maybe_init);
9029        break;
9030      }
9031    }
9032  }
9033  if let Some(init_token) = init {
9034    let init_ch = init_token.with_str(|is| is.chars().next().unwrap());
9035    assign_catcode(init_ch, Catcode::ACTIVE, None);
9036    let delim = T_ACTIVE!(init_ch);
9037    // latex.ltx:15504-15510 `\verb@eol@error`: `\obeylines` makes the end of
9038    // the line active, and that `^^M` closes the verb group with ONE
9039    // recoverable "\verb ended by end of line" error. Perl's `readUntil`
9040    // (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:1797) has no such bound, so an unterminated
9041    // `\verb v1.1 )` scanned across lines and swallowed a later `{verbatim}`
9042    // (bigints manual, 10-error cascade; SHARED, pdflatex recovers with one
9043    // error). Guard: `perfect_kernel_batch56::verb_ended_by_end_of_line_recovers`.
9044    assign_catcode('\r', Catcode::ACTIVE, None);
9045    let eol = T_ACTIVE!('\r');
9046    let par = T_CS!("\\par");
9047    // `token_delimited`: tabularx's `\TX@verb` (tabularx.sty:205-209) ends at the delimiter as it stands, so a
9048    // `\verb|…|` in an argument read before it (the `|` frozen "other") ends there; the kernel's needs it active.
9049    let mut body = Vec::new();
9050    let mut terminated = false;
9051    while let Some(token) = read_token()? {
9052      if token == delim
9053        || (token_delimited
9054          && token.get_catcode() == Catcode::OTHER
9055          && token.with_str(|s| s.starts_with(init_ch) && s.chars().count() == 1))
9056      {
9057        terminated = true;
9058        break;
9059      }
9060      if token == eol || token == par {
9061        Error!("unexpected", "\\verb", "\\verb ended by end of line", "");
9062        terminated = true;
9063        break;
9064      }
9065      body.push(token);
9066    }
9067    if !terminated {
9068      // Perl `Gullet::readUntil` (Core/Gullet.pm:683-685): ran out of tokens
9069      // before the delimiter — unread everything scanned and return an EMPTY
9070      // body. That is where a `\verb` inside a pre-tokenized argument
9071      // (`\footnote{… \verb+x+ …}`) lands: the closing `+` was frozen as OTHER
9072      // when the argument was read, so the ACTIVE delimiter never matches and
9073      // the scan hits the end of the argument. Keeping the scanned tokens as
9074      // the body swallowed the rest of the note (an `<item>` inside
9075      // `<verbatim>`; platex-tools/plarray.tex:20, RUST-ONLY). Guard:
9076      // `verb_inside_pretokenized_argument_unreads_instead_of_running_away`.
9077      unread(Tokens::new(std::mem::take(&mut body)));
9078    }
9079    let body = Tokens::new(body);
9080    end_semiverbatim()?;
9081    let mut result = Vec::new();
9082    if starred {
9083      result.push(T_CS!("\\lx@use@visiblespace"));
9084    }
9085    result.extend(
9086      Invocation!(T_CS!("\\@internal@verb"), vec![
9087        if starred {
9088          Tokens!(T_OTHER!("*"))
9089        } else {
9090          Tokens!()
9091        },
9092        Tokens!(init_token),
9093        body
9094      ])
9095      .unlist(),
9096    );
9097    Ok(Some(result))
9098  } else {
9099    // typically something read too far got \verb and the content is somewhere else..?
9100    Error!(
9101      "expected",
9102      "delimiter",
9103      "Verbatim argument lost\n Bindings for preceding code is probably broken"
9104    );
9105    end_semiverbatim()?;
9106    Ok(None)
9107  }
9108}

9110/// True when some open ancestor can hold `qname` (`ltx:caption` /
9111/// `ltx:toccaption`) — i.e. the caption really is inside a float. The
9112/// transient capture wrappers (`ltx:_CaptureBlock_`, `insert_block`'s
9113/// holder for a `{center}` body inside a figure; `ltx:_Capture_`) admit every
9114/// block element and are unwrapped into their parent afterwards, so they
9115/// neither count nor stop the walk: a `marginfigure` (`lrbox` + minipage,
9116/// used from a `\marginpar`) reaches `ltx:note` → `ltx:p` → document and
9117/// answers no; `{center}` inside `{figure}` reaches the figure. See
9118/// OXIDIZED_DESIGN #182.
9119fn caption_can_float(document: &Document, qname: &str) -> bool {
9120  let Some(mut node) = document.get_element() else {
9121    return false;
9122  };
9123  loop {
9124    if !node.get_name().starts_with('_') && document::can_contain(&node, qname) {
9125      return true;
9126    }
9127    match node.get_parent() {
9128      Some(parent) if parent.get_type() == Some(NodeType::ElementNode) => node = parent,
9129      _ => return false,
9130    }
9131  }
9132}
9133
9134/// Absorb a formatted caption title without its `\lx@tag` pieces — the
9135/// float's counter label, which only a float's `ltx:caption` may carry
9136/// (OXIDIZED_DESIGN #182). Lists are walked so a tag nested beside the title
9137/// text is dropped without losing the text.
9138pub(crate) fn absorb_without_tags(document: &mut Document, piece: &Digested) -> Result<()> {
9139  match piece.data() {
9140    DigestedData::Whatsit(w) => {
9141      // Exactly the two tag constructors (`\lx@tag`, `\lx@tags`), by
9142      // identity — not any internal name containing `lx@tag`.
9143      let is_tag = {
9144        let whatsit = w.borrow();
9145        let name = whatsit.get_definition().get_cs_name().into_owned();
9146        name == "\\lx@tag" || name == "\\lx@tags"
9147      };
9148      if is_tag {
9149        return Ok(());
9150      }
9151      document.absorb(piece, None)?;
9152    },
9153    DigestedData::List(l) => {
9154      let boxes = l.borrow().boxes.clone();
9155      for inner in boxes {
9156        absorb_without_tags(document, &inner)?;
9157      }
9158    },
9159    _ => {
9160      document.absorb(piece, None)?;
9161    },
9162  }
9163  Ok(())
9164}
